controls.name: 4.1 Principle 1 – Accountability
controls.title: 4.1 Principle 1 – Accountability
controls.body: An organization is responsible for personal information under its control and shall designate an individual or individuals who are accountable for the organization’s compliance with the following principles.

controls.name: PT-1 - Policy and Procedures
controls.title: Policy and Procedures
controls.body:
a. Develop, document, and disseminate to [Assignment: organization-defined personnel or roles]:
  1. [Selection (one or more): Organization-level; Mission/business process-level; System-level] personally identifiable information processing and transparency policy that:
     (a) Addresses purpose, scope, roles, responsibilities, management commitment, coordination among organizational entities, and compliance; and
     (b) Is consistent with applicable laws, executive orders, directives, regulations, policies, standards, and guidelines; and
  2. Procedures to facilitate the implementation of the personally identifiable information processing and transparency policy and the associated personally identifiable information processing and transparency controls;

b. Designate an [Assignment: organization-defined official] to manage the development, documentation, and dissemination of the personally identifiable information processing and transparency policy and procedures; and

c. Review and update the current personally identifiable information processing and transparency:
  1. Policy [Assignment: organization-defined frequency] and following [Assignment: organization-defined events]; and
  2. Procedures [Assignment: organization-defined frequency] and following [Assignment: organization-defined events].

controls.name: 4.1.1 Principle 1.1 – Accountability (designated individual(s))
controls.title: 4.1.1 Principle 1.1 – Accountability (designated individual(s))
controls.body: Accountability for the organization’s compliance with the principles rests with the designated individual(s), even though other individuals within the organization may be responsible for the day-to-day collection and processing of personal information. In addition, other individuals within the organization may be delegated to act on behalf of the designated individual(s).

controls.name: 4.1.2 Principle 1.2 – Accountability (identity of designated individual(s))
controls.title: 4.1.2 Principle 1.2 – Accountability (identity of designated individual(s))
controls.body: The identity of the individual(s) designated by the organization to oversee the organization’s compliance with the principles shall be made known upon request.

controls.name: 4.1.3 Principle 1.3 – Accountability (third parties)
controls.title: 4.1.3 Principle 1.3 – Accountability (third parties)
controls.body: An organization is responsible for personal information in its possession or custody, including information that has been transferred to a third party for processing. The organization shall use contractual or other means to provide a comparable level of protection while the information is being processed by a third party.

controls.name: 4.1.4 Principle 1.4 – Accountability (policies and practices)
controls.title: 4.1.4 Principle 1.4 – Accountability (policies and practices)

controls.name: 4.10 Principle 10 – Challenging Compliance
controls.title: 4.10 Principle 10 – Challenging Compliance
controls.body: An individual shall be able to address a challenge concerning compliance with the above principles to the designated individual or individuals accountable for the organization’s compliance.

controls.name: 4.10.1 Principle 10.1 – Challenging Compliance (designated individual(s))
controls.title: 4.10.1 Principle 10.1 – Challenging Compliance (designated individual(s))
controls.body: The individual accountable for an organization’s compliance is discussed in Clause 4.1.1. (Accountability for the organization’s compliance with the principles rests with the designated individual(s), even though other individuals within the organization may be responsible for the day-to-day collection and processing of personal information. In addition, other individuals within the organization may be delegated to act on behalf of the designated individual(s).)

controls.name: 4.10.2 Principle 10.2 – Challenging Compliance (policies and practices)
controls.title: 4.10.2 Principle 10.2 – Challenging Compliance (policies and practices)
controls.body: Organizations shall put procedures in place to receive and respond to complaints or inquiries about their policies and practices relating to the handling of personal information. The complaint procedures should be easily accessible and simple to use.

controls.name: 4.10.3 Principle 10.3 – Challenging Compliance (compaint procedures)
controls.title: 4.10.3 Principle 10.3 – Challenging Compliance (compaint procedures)
controls.body: Organizations shall inform individuals who make inquiries or lodge complaints of the existence of relevant complaint procedures. A range of these procedures may exist. For example, some regulatory bodies accept complaints about the personal-information handling practices of the companies they regulate.

controls.name: 4.10.4 Principle 10.4 – Challenging Compliance (investigation)
controls.title: 4.10.4 Principle 10.4 – Challenging Compliance (investigation)
controls.body: An organization shall investigate all complaints. If a complaint is found to be justified, the organization shall take appropriate measures, including, if necessary, amending its policies and practices.

controls.name: 4.2 Principle 2 – Identifying Purposes
controls.title: 4.2 Principle 2 – Identifying Purposes
controls.body: The purposes for which personal information is collected shall be identified by the organization at or before the time the information is collected.

controls.name: 4.2.1 Principle 2.1 – Identifying Purposes (documented purposes)
controls.title: 4.2.1 Principle 2.1 – Identifying Purposes (documented purposes)
controls.body: The organization shall document the purposes for which personal information is collected in order to comply with the Openness principle (Clause 4.8) and the Individual Access principle (Clause 4.9).

controls.name: PCI 10.4 - Time Synchronization
controls.title: Time Synchronization
controls.body:
Using time-synchronization technology, synchronize all critical system clocks and times and ensure that the following is implemented for acquiring, distributing, and storing time.

Note: One example of time synchronization technology is Network Time Protocol (NTP).

controls.name: 4.2.2 Principle 2.2 – Identifying Purposes (determining collection)
controls.title: 4.2.2 Principle 2.2 – Identifying Purposes (determining collection)
controls.body: Identifying the purposes for which personal information is collected at or before the time of collection allows organizations to determine the information they need to collect to fulfil these purposes. The Limiting Collection principle (Clause 4.4) requires an organization to collect only that information necessary for the purposes that have been identified.

controls.name: 1.2.2 - Consistency of Privacy Policies and Procedures with laws and regulations
controls.title: Consistency of Privacy Policies and Procedures with laws and regulations
controls.body: Policies and procedures are reviewed and compared to the requirements of applicable laws and regulations at least annually and whenever changes to such laws and regulations are made . Privacy policies and procedures are revised to conform with the requirements of applicable laws and regulations .

controls.name: 4.2.3 Principle 2.3 – Identifying Purposes (timing)
controls.title: 4.2.3 Principle 2.3 – Identifying Purposes (timing)
controls.body: The identified purposes should be specified at or before the time of collection to the individual from whom the personal information is collected. Depending upon the way in which the information is collected, this can be done orally or in writing. An application form, for example, may give notice of the purposes.

controls.name: IM5 - Incident Response Responsibilities
controls.title: Incident Response Responsibilities
controls.body: Management has established defined roles and responsibilities to oversee the implementation of security policies including incident response.

controls.name: 4.2.4 Principle 2.4 – Identifying Purposes (additional purposes)
controls.title: 4.2.4 Principle 2.4 – Identifying Purposes (additional purposes)
controls.body: When personal information that has been collected is to be used for a purpose not previously identified, the new purpose shall be identified prior to use. Unless the new purpose is required by law, the consent of the individual is required before information can be used for that purpose. For an elaboration on consent, please refer to the Consent principle (Clause 4.3).

controls.name: 4.2.5 Principle 2.5 – Identifying Purposes (explanation)
controls.title: 4.2.5 Principle 2.5 – Identifying Purposes (explanation)
controls.body: Persons collecting personal information should be able to explain to individuals the purposes for which the information is being collected.

controls.name: 4.3 Principle 3 – Consent
controls.title: 4.3 Principle 3 – Consent
controls.body:
The knowledge and consent of the individual are required for the collection, use, or disclosure of personal information, except where inappropriate.

Note: In certain circumstances personal information can be collected, used, or disclosed without the knowledge and consent of the individual. For example, legal, medical, or security reasons may make it impossible or impractical to seek consent. When information is being collected for the detection and prevention of fraud or for law enforcement, seeking the consent of the individual might defeat the purpose of collecting the information. Seeking consent may be impossible or inappropriate when the individual is a minor, seriously ill, or mentally incapacitated. In addition, organizations that do not have a direct relationship with the individual may not always be able to seek consent. For example, seeking consent may be impractical for a charity or a direct-marketing firm that wishes to acquire a mailing list from another organization. In such cases, the organization providing the list would be expected to obtain consent before disclosing personal information.

controls.name: CAN 4.3.3.1 - Investment in Cyber Security Awareness
controls.title: Investment in Cyber Security Awareness
controls.body: The organization shall invest in regular and ongoing cyber security awareness and training for their employees.

controls.name: PCI 6.3 - Internal and External Software Security
controls.title: Internal and External Software Security
controls.body:
Develop internal and external software applications (including web-based administrative access to applications) securely, as follows:·
- In accordance with PCI DSS (for example, secure authentication and logging)·
- Based on industry standards and/or best practices.·
- Incorporating information security throughout the software-development life cycle


Note: this applies to all software developed internally as well as bespoke or custom software developed by a third party.

controls.name: PL-10 - Baseline Selection
controls.title: Baseline Selection
controls.body: Select a control baseline for the system.

controls.name: 4.3.1 Principle 3.1 – Consent (timing)
controls.title: 4.3.1 Principle 3.1 – Consent (timing)
controls.body: Consent is required for the collection of personal information and the subsequent use or disclosure of this information. Typically, an organization will seek consent for the use or disclosure of the information at the time of collection. In certain circumstances, consent with respect to use or disclosure may be sought after the information has been collected but before use (for example, when an organization wants to use information for a purpose not previously identified).

controls.name: 4.3.2 Principle 3.2 – Consent (purpose)
controls.title: 4.3.2 Principle 3.2 – Consent (purpose)
controls.body: The principle requires “knowledge and consent”. Organizations shall make a reasonable effort to ensure that the individual is advised of the purposes for which the information will be used. To make the consent meaningful, the purposes must be stated in such a manner that the individual can reasonably understand how the information will be used or disclosed.

controls.name: 4.3.3 Principle 3.3 – Consent (limitation)
controls.title: 4.3.3 Principle 3.3 – Consent (limitation)
controls.body: An organization shall not, as a condition of the supply of a product or service, require an individual to consent to the collection, use, or disclosure of information beyond that required to fulfil the explicitly specified, and legitimate purposes.

controls.name: 4.3.4 Principle 3.4 – Consent (sensitivity of information)
controls.title: 4.3.4 Principle 3.4 – Consent (sensitivity of information)
controls.body: The form of the consent sought by the organization may vary, depending upon the circumstances and the type of information. In determining the form of consent to use, organizations shall take into account the sensitivity of the information. Although some information (for example, medical records and income records) is almost always considered to be sensitive, any information can be sensitive, depending on the context. For example, the names and addresses of subscribers to a newsmagazine would generally not be considered sensitive information. However, the names and addresses of subscribers to some special-interest magazines might be considered sensitive.

controls.name: 4.3.5 Principle 3.5 – Consent (reasonable expectations)
controls.title: 4.3.5 Principle 3.5 – Consent (reasonable expectations)
controls.body: In obtaining consent, the reasonable expectations of the individual are also relevant. For example, an individual buying a subscription to a magazine should reasonably expect that the organization, in addition to using the individual’s name and address for mailing and billing purposes, would also contact the person to solicit the renewal of the subscription. In this case, the organization can assume that the individual’s request constitutes consent for specific purposes. On the other hand, an individual would not reasonably expect that personal information given to a health-care professional would be given to a company selling health-care products, unless consent were obtained. Consent shall not be obtained through deception.

controls.name: 4.3.6 Principle 3.6 – Consent (express vs implied)
controls.title: 4.3.6 Principle 3.6 – Consent (express vs implied)
controls.body: The way in which an organization seeks consent may vary, depending on the circumstances and the type of information collected. An organization should generally seek express consent when the information is likely to be considered sensitive. Implied consent would generally be appropriate when the information is less sensitive. Consent can also be given by an authorized representative (such as a legal guardian or a person having power of attorney).

controls.name: 10.1.1 - Detecting, managing and recording incidents and breaches - 1
controls.title: Detecting, managing and recording incidents and breaches - 1
controls.body: You have appropriate training in place so that staff are able to recognise a security incident and a personal data breach.

controls.name: 4.3.7 Principle 3.7 – Consent (consent method)
controls.title: 4.3.7 Principle 3.7 – Consent (consent method)

controls.name: 4.3.8 Principle 3.8 – Consent (consent withdrawal)
controls.title: 4.3.8 Principle 3.8 – Consent (consent withdrawal)
controls.body: An individual may withdraw consent at any time, subject to legal or contractual restrictions and reasonable notice. The organization shall inform the individual of the implications of such withdrawal.

controls.name: 4.4 Principle 4 – Limiting Collection
controls.title: 4.4 Principle 4 – Limiting Collection
controls.body: The collection of personal information shall be limited to that which is necessary for the purposes identified by the organization. Information shall be collected by fair and lawful means.

controls.name: IA-3(3) - Device Identification and Authentication | Dynamic Address Allocation
controls.title: Device Identification and Authentication | Dynamic Address Allocation
controls.body:
a. Where addresses are allocated dynamically, standardize dynamic address allocation lease information and the lease duration assigned to devices in accordance with [Assignment: organization-defined lease information and lease duration]; and
b. Audit lease information when assigned to a device.

controls.name: 4.4.1 Principle 4.1 – Limiting Collection (necessity)
controls.title: 4.4.1 Principle 4.1 – Limiting Collection (necessity)
controls.body: Organizations shall not collect personal information indiscriminately. Both the amount and the type of information collected shall be limited to that which is necessary to fulfil the purposes identified. Organizations shall specify the type of information collected as part of their information-handling policies and practices, in accordance with the Openness principle (Clause 4.8).

controls.name: 4.4.2 Principle 4.2 – Limiting Collection (fair and lawful)
controls.title: 4.4.2 Principle 4.2 – Limiting Collection (fair and lawful)
controls.body: The requirement that personal information be collected by fair and lawful means is intended to prevent organizations from collecting information by misleading or deceiving individuals about the purpose for which information is being collected. This requirement implies that consent with respect to collection must not be obtained through deception.

controls.name: 4.5 Principle 5 – Limiting Use, Disclosure and Retention
controls.title: 4.5 Principle 5 – Limiting Use, Disclosure and Retention
controls.body: Personal information shall not be used or disclosed for purposes other than those for which it was collected, except with the consent of the individual or as required by law. Personal information shall be retained only as long as necessary for the fulfilment of those purposes.

controls.name: 1.2.3 - Personal Information Identification and classification
controls.title: Personal Information Identification and classification
controls.body: The types of personal information and sensitive personal information and the related processes, systems, and third parties involved in the handling of such information are identified . Such information is covered by the entity’s privacy and related security policies and procedures .

controls.name: 4.5.1 Principle 5.1 – Limiting Use, Disclosure and Retention (documented purpose)
controls.title: 4.5.1 Principle 5.1 – Limiting Use, Disclosure and Retention (documented purpose)
controls.body: Organizations using personal information for a new purpose shall document this purpose (see Clause 4.2.1).

controls.name: CAN 4.4.3.1 - Cyber Security Risk Assessments
controls.title: Cyber Security Risk Assessments
controls.body: The member of the senior-level leadership team appointed to oversee the organization’s IT security shall conduct cyber security risk assessments and coordinate the implementation of cyber security controls to address potential cyber security risks.

controls.name: CAN 4.4.3.3 - Authorization on Accepted Cyber Risks
controls.title: Authorization on Accepted Cyber Risks
controls.body: Cyber security risks accepted by the organization shall be documented and authorized by a senior official of the organization.

controls.name: CAN 4.4.3.4 - Budgeting on IT Security
controls.title: Budgeting on IT Security
controls.body: The organization shall identify their financial spending levels for IT and IT security investment (as raw numbers and as a percent of total expenditures).

controls.name: CAN 4.4.3.5 - Identification of Staffing Levels
controls.title: Identification of Staffing Levels
controls.body: The organization shall identify their internal staffing levels for IT and IT security (as raw numbers and as a percent of total staff).

controls.name: 4.5.2 Principle 5.2 – Limiting Use, Disclosure and Retention (guidelines and procedures)
controls.title: 4.5.2 Principle 5.2 – Limiting Use, Disclosure and Retention (guidelines and procedures)
controls.body: Organizations should develop guidelines and implement procedures with respect to the retention of personal information. These guidelines should include minimum and maximum retention periods. Personal information that has been used to make a decision about an individual shall be retained long enough to allow the individual access to the information after the decision has been made. An organization may be subject to legislative requirements with respect to retention periods.

controls.name: IM1 - Customer Support System
controls.title: Customer Support System
controls.body:
The organization provides an external-facing support system that allows users to report incidents, complaints, issues, and any other challenge through an appropriate channel.
Reported incidents are addressed by the organization's support staff in a timely manner.

controls.name: CAN 4.4.3.8 - Implementation of Cyber Security Controls
controls.title: Implementation of Cyber Security Controls
controls.body: Regardless of the outcomes from the cyber security risk assessment, the organization shall implement the foundational or baseline cyber security controls specified in Section 5 (Baseline controls), and as appropriate, Section 6 (Baseline controls by operating environment) based on its business environment.

controls.name: 4.5.3 Principle 5.3 – Limiting Use, Disclosure and Retention (disposal)
controls.title: 4.5.3 Principle 5.3 – Limiting Use, Disclosure and Retention (disposal)
controls.body: Personal information that is no longer required to fulfil the identified purposes should be destroyed, erased, or made anonymous. Organizations shall develop guidelines and implement procedures to govern the destruction of personal information.

controls.name: OM2.13 - Third-party/Vendor Management Process
controls.title: OM2.13 - Third-party/Vendor Management Process
controls.body: A vendor management process has been implemented whereby management performs risk assessments of potential new vendors and evaluates the performance of existing vendors on an annual basis. Corrective actions are taken as required based on the results of the assessments.

controls.name: 4.6 Principle 6 – Accuracy
controls.title: 4.6 Principle 6 – Accuracy
controls.body: Personal information shall be as accurate, complete, and up-to-date as is necessary for the purposes for which it is to be used.

controls.name: 4.6.1 Principle 6.1 – Accuracy (extent)
controls.title: 4.6.1 Principle 6.1 – Accuracy (extent)
controls.body: The extent to which personal information shall be accurate, complete, and up-to-date will depend upon the use of the information, taking into account the interests of the individual. Information shall be sufficiently accurate, complete, and up-to-date to minimize the possibility that inappropriate information may be used to make a decision about the individual.

controls.name: IA-4 (4) Identifier management | identify user status
controls.title: IA-4 (4) Identifier management | identify user status
controls.body:
The organization manages individual identifiers by uniquely identifying each individual as
[Assignment: organization-defined characteristic identifying individual status].

controls.name: CAN 5.1.2.2 - Responsibilities for Incident Handling
controls.title: Responsibilities for Incident Handling
controls.body: The incident response plan shall detail who is responsible for handling incidents including any relevant contact information for communicating to external parties, stakeholders and regulators. The organization shall have an up-to-date hard copy version of this plan available for situations where soft copies are not available.

controls.name: 1.2.4 - Risk Assessment
controls.title: Risk Assessment
controls.body: A risk assessment process is used to establish a risk baseline and, at least annually, to identify new or changed risks to personal information and to develop and update responses to such risks .

controls.name: 4.6.2 Principle 6.2 – Accuracy (routine updates)
controls.title: 4.6.2 Principle 6.2 – Accuracy (routine updates)
controls.body: An organization shall not routinely update personal information, unless such a process is necessary to fulfil the purposes for which the information was collected.

controls.name: OM2.14 - SOC Acknowledgement
controls.title: OM2.14 - SOC Acknowledgement
controls.body: On a semi-annual basis, control owners sign an acknowledgement form, certifying that they have read applicable SOC control descriptions and, as needed, narratives, and understand their related process and control responsibilities. Desired updates, if any, are communicated to applicable internal and external (auditors) personnel to update appropriate documentation.

controls.name: CAN 5.2.2.2 - Automatic Patching
controls.title: Automatic Patching
controls.body: The organization shall enable automatic patching for all software and hardware or document all instances where they make the business decision not to do so.

controls.name: 4.6.3 Principle 6.3 – Accuracy (ongoing use)
controls.title: 4.6.3 Principle 6.3 – Accuracy (ongoing use)
controls.body: Personal information that is used on an ongoing basis, including information that is disclosed to third parties, should generally be accurate and up-to-date, unless limits to the requirement for accuracy are clearly set out.

controls.name: CAN 5.2.2.3 - Systems Incapable of Automatic Patching
controls.title: Systems Incapable of Automatic Patching
controls.body: The organization shall perform a risk assessment whether to replace systems incapable of automatic patching.

controls.name: 4.7 Principle 7 – Safeguards
controls.title: 4.7 Principle 7 – Safeguards
controls.body: Personal information shall be protected by security safeguards appropriate to the sensitivity of the information.

controls.name: 4.7.1 Principle 7.1 – Safeguards (threats)
controls.title: 4.7.1 Principle 7.1 – Safeguards (threats)
controls.body: The security safeguards shall protect personal information against loss or theft, as well as unauthorized access, disclosure, copying, use, or modification. Organizations shall protect personal information regardless of the format in which it is held.

controls.name: 4.7.2 Principle 7.2 – Safeguards (factors)
controls.title: 4.7.2 Principle 7.2 – Safeguards (factors)
controls.body: The nature of the safeguards will vary depending on the sensitivity of the information that has been collected, the amount, distribution, and format of the information, and the method of storage. More sensitive information should be safeguarded by a higher level of protection. The concept of sensitivity is discussed in Clause 4.3.4.

controls.name: 4.7.3 Principle 7.3 – Safeguards (methods)
controls.title: 4.7.3 Principle 7.3 – Safeguards (methods)
controls.body:
The methods of protection should include
(a) physical measures, for example, locked filing cabinets and restricted access to offices;
(b) organizational measures, for example, security clearances and limiting access on a “need-to-know” basis; and
(c) technological measures, for example, the use of passwords and encryption.

controls.name: 4.7.4 Principle 7.4 – Safeguards (awareness)
controls.title: 4.7.4 Principle 7.4 – Safeguards (awareness)
controls.body: Organizations shall make their employees aware of the importance of maintaining the confidentiality of personal information.

controls.name: CAN 5.3.2.1 - Anti-Malware Solutions
controls.title: Anti-Malware Solutions
controls.body: The organization shall enable anti-malware solutions that update automatically and prevent malware from executing without user intervention.

controls.name: CAN 5.4.2.1 - Changing Default Passwords
controls.title: Changing Default Passwords
controls.body: The organization shall implement secure configurations for all their devices by changing all default passwords.

controls.name: 4.7.5 Principle 7.5 – Safeguards (disposal)
controls.title: 4.7.5 Principle 7.5 – Safeguards (disposal)
controls.body: Care shall be used in the disposal or destruction of personal information, to prevent unauthorized parties from gaining access to the information (see Clause 4.5.3).

controls.name: 4.8 Principle 8 – Openness
controls.title: 4.8 Principle 8 – Openness
controls.body: An organization shall make readily available to individuals specific information about its policies and practices relating to the management of personal information.

controls.name: IR-4(11) - Incident Handling | Integrated Incident Response Team
controls.title: Incident Handling | Integrated Incident Response Team
controls.body: Establish and maintain an integrated incident response team that can be deployed to any location identified by the organization in [Assignment: organization-defined time period].

controls.name: CAN 5.5.2.2 - Password Change on Suspicion
controls.title: Password Change on Suspicion
controls.body: The organization shall enforce password changes on suspicion or evidence of compromise.

controls.name: 4.8.1 Principle 8.1 – Openness (policies and practices)
controls.title: 4.8.1 Principle 8.1 – Openness (policies and practices)
controls.body: Organizations shall be open about their policies and practices with respect to the management of personal information. Individuals shall be able to acquire information about an organization’s policies and practices without unreasonable effort. This information shall be made available in a form that is generally understandable.

controls.name: D1.RM.Au.Inn.2 - Data Mining Tools in Audit Function
controls.title: Data Mining Tools in Audit Function
controls.body: The independent audit function uses sophisticated data mining tools to perform continuous monitoring of cybersecurity processes or controls.

controls.name: CAN 5.6.2.1 - Identification of Business Information and Software
controls.title: Identification of Business Information and Software
controls.body: The organization shall determine on a case-by-case basis what business information and software (including but not limited to sensitive information) is essential to the functioning of the organization, and how frequently this information changes.

controls.name: AC-10 Concurrent session control
controls.title: AC-10 Concurrent session control
controls.body: The information system limits the number of concurrent sessions for each [Assignment: organization-defined account and/or account type] to [Assignment: organization-defined number].

controls.name: 4.8.2 Principle 8.2 – Openness (notice)
controls.title: 4.8.2 Principle 8.2 – Openness (notice)

controls.name: 4.8.3 Principle 8.3 – Openness (methods)
controls.title: 4.8.3 Principle 8.3 – Openness (methods)
controls.body: An organization may make information on its policies and practices available in a variety of ways. The method chosen depends on the nature of its business and other considerations. For example, an organization may choose to make brochures available in its place of business, mail information to its customers, provide online access, or establish a toll-free telephone number.

controls.name: CC2.3.4 - Contact Information for Reporting Security Incidents
controls.title: CC2.3.4 - Contact Information for Reporting Security Incidents
controls.body: Customers are provided contact information for reporting security incidents on the customer-facing website and in customer contracts.

controls.name: PCI 5.4 - Policies and Procedures for Malware
controls.title: Policies and Procedures for Malware
controls.body: Ensure that security policies and operational procedures for protecting systems against malware are documented, in use, and known to all affected parties.

controls.name: CE.005 - Information Systems Responsibility
controls.title: Information Systems Responsibility
controls.body: Designate staff to be responsible for the management of the information systems that are in scope for the assessment.

controls.name: CAN 5.6.2.5 - Encrypted Backups
controls.title: Encrypted Backups
controls.body: The organization should consider the use of encrypted backups with securely stored and recoverable key material. Decryption keys and/or unencrypted backups should be stored securely and should be accessible only to authorized employees or officers.

controls.name: CAN 5.6.3.1 - Testing of Recovery Procedures
controls.title: Testing of Recovery Procedures
controls.body: The organization shall use a sampling of backup data to test and verify recovery procedures at regular intervals to ensure the integrity of the end-to-end backup and restoration process.

controls.name: PCI 12.2 - Risk Assessment Exercise
controls.title: Risk Assessment Exercise
controls.body: Implement a risk-assessment process that:·Is performed at least annually and upon significant changes to the environment (for example, acquisition, merger, relocation, etc.),·Identifies critical assets, threats, and vulnerabilities, and·Results in a formal, documented analysis of risk.Examples of risk-assessment methodologies include but are not limited to OCTAVE, ISO 27005 and NIST SP 800-30.

controls.name: D2.MA.Ma.A.4 - Threat Intelligence Analysis
controls.title: Threat Intelligence Analysis
controls.body: Threat intelligence is viewed within the context of the institution's risk profile and risk appetite to prioritize mitigating actions in anticipation of threats.

controls.name: CAN 5.7.3.3 - Software Firewall
controls.title: Software Firewall
controls.body: The organization shall activate any software firewalls included on devices within their networks or document the alternative measures in place instead of these firewalls.

controls.name: PE-6 (1) Monitoring physical access | intrusion alarms / surveillance equipment
controls.title: PE-6 (1) Monitoring physical access | intrusion alarms / surveillance equipment
controls.body: The organization monitors physical intrusion alarms and surveillance equipment.

controls.name: HR6 - Background and Reference Checks
controls.title: Background and Reference Checks
controls.body: New employees are subjected to background and reference checks prior to joining the organization.

controls.name: A.10.1.2 - Key Management
controls.title: Key Management
controls.body: A policy on the use, protection and lifetime of cryptographic keys shall be developed and implemented through their whole lifecycle.

controls.name: 4.9 Principle 9 – Individual Access
controls.title: 4.9 Principle 9 – Individual Access
controls.body:
Upon request, an individual shall be informed of the existence, use, and disclosure of his or her personal information and shall be given access to that information. An individual shall be able to challenge the accuracy and completeness of the information and have it amended as appropriate.

Note: In certain situations, an organization may not be able to provide access to all the personal information it holds about an individual. Exceptions to the access requirement should be limited and specific. The reasons for denying access should be provided to the individual upon request. Exceptions may include information that is prohibitively costly to provide, information that contains references to other individuals, information that cannot be disclosed for legal, security, or commercial proprietary reasons, and information that is subject to solicitor-client or litigation privilege.

controls.name: 1.2.5 - Consistency of commitments with Privacy Policies and Procedures
controls.title: Consistency of commitments with Privacy Policies and Procedures
controls.body: Internal personnel or advisers review contracts for consistency with privacy policies and procedures and address any inconsistencies

controls.name: 4.9.1 Principle 9.1 – Individual Access (access requests)
controls.title: 4.9.1 Principle 9.1 – Individual Access (access requests)
controls.body: Upon request, an organization shall inform an individual whether or not the organization holds personal information about the individual. Organizations are encouraged to indicate the source of this information. The organization shall allow the individual access to this information. However, the organization may choose to make sensitive medical information available through a medical practitioner. In addition, the organization shall provide an account of the use that has been made or is being made of this information and an account of the third parties to which it has been disclosed.

controls.name: 4.9.2 Principle 9.2 – Individual Access (verification)
controls.title: 4.9.2 Principle 9.2 – Individual Access (verification)
controls.body: An individual may be required to provide sufficient information to permit an organization to provide an account of the existence, use, and disclosure of personal information. The information provided shall only be used for this purpose.

controls.name: 4.9.3 Principle 9.3 – Individual Access (third parties)
controls.title: 4.9.3 Principle 9.3 – Individual Access (third parties)
controls.body: In providing an account of third parties to which it has disclosed personal information about an individual, an organization should attempt to be as specific as possible. When it is not possible to provide a list of the organizations to which it has actually disclosed information about an individual, the organization shall provide a list of organizations to which it may have disclosed information about the individual.

controls.name: 4.9.4 Principle 9.4 – Individual Access (response)
controls.title: 4.9.4 Principle 9.4 – Individual Access (response)
controls.body: An organization shall respond to an individual’s request within a reasonable time and at minimal or no cost to the individual. The requested information shall be provided or made available in a form that is generally understandable. For example, if the organization uses abbreviations or codes to record information, an explanation shall be provided.

controls.name: 4.9.5 Principle 9.5 – Individual Access (rectification)
controls.title: 4.9.5 Principle 9.5 – Individual Access (rectification)
controls.body: When an individual successfully demonstrates the inaccuracy or incompleteness of personal information, the organization shall amend the information as required. Depending upon the nature of the information challenged, amendment involves the correction, deletion, or addition of information. Where appropriate, the amended information shall be transmitted to third parties having access to the information in question.

controls.name: PCI 8.3 - Multi-Factor Authentication
controls.title: Multi-Factor Authentication
controls.body:
Secure all individual non-console administrative access and all remote access to the CDE using multi-factor authentication.

Note:Multi-factor authentication requires that a minimum of two of the three authentication methods (see Requirement 8.2 for descriptions of authentication methods) be used for authentication. Using one factor twice (for example, using two separate passwords) is not considered multi-factor authentication.

controls.name: 4.9.6 Principle 9.6 – Individual Access (disputes)
controls.title: 4.9.6 Principle 9.6 – Individual Access (disputes)
controls.body: When a challenge is not resolved to the satisfaction of the individual, the substance of the unresolved challenge shall be recorded by the organization. When appropriate, the existence of the unresolved challenge shall be transmitted to third parties having access to the information in question.

controls.name: D1.G.SP.Int.4 - Strategic Cybersecurity Objectives to Tactical Goals
controls.title: Strategic Cybersecurity Objectives to Tactical Goals
controls.body: Management links strategic cybersecurity objectives to tactical goals.

controls.name: AAU2.0 - Customer Contracts
controls.title: AAU2.0 - Customer Contracts
controls.body: New customer contracts or modification to existing customer contracts and end user license agreements (EULA) are reviewed by Management to ensure commitments are met by the system.

controls.name: D1.G.Ov.B.2 - Discussion of Information Security Risks
controls.title: Discussion of Information Security Risks

controls.name: CIP-013.R2 - Supply Chain Cyber Security Risk Management Plan Implementation
controls.title: Supply Chain Cyber Security Risk Management Plan Implementation
controls.body: Each responsible entity shall implement its supply chain cyber security risk management plan(s) specified in CIP-013.R1.

controls.title: Management
controls.body: The entity defines, documents, communicates, and assigns accountability for its privacy policies and procedures.

controls.name: 10.1.2 - Detecting, managing and recording incidents and breaches - 2
controls.title: Detecting, managing and recording incidents and breaches - 2
controls.body: A dedicated person or team manages security incidents and personal data breaches.

controls.name: CAN 5.7.3.6 - Segmentation of Networks
controls.title: Segmentation of Networks
controls.body: The organization should segment their networks to ensure networks provided to the public/customers are separated (and/or isolated) from the corporate networks.

controls.name: CAN 5.7.3.7 - DMARC for Email Services
controls.title: DMARC for Email Services
controls.body: The organization shall ensure the implementation of DMARC on all organization email services.

controls.name: PCI 3.5.4 - Storage Location for Cryptographic Keys
controls.title: Storage Location for Cryptographic Keys
controls.body: Store cryptographic keys in the fewest possible locations.

controls.name: PCI 11.2 - Vulnerability Scans
controls.title: Vulnerability Scans
controls.body:
Run internal and external network vulnerability scans at least quarterly and after any significant change in the network (such as new system component installations, changes in network topology, firewall rule modifications, product upgrades).

Note:Multiple scan reports can be combined for the quarterly scan process to show that all systems were scanned and all applicable vulnerabilities have been addressed. Additional documentation may be required to verify non-remediated vulnerabilities are in the process of being addressed. For initial PCI DSS compliance, it is not required that four quarters of passing scans be completed if the assessor verifies 
1) the most recent scan result was a passing scan, 
2) the entity has documented policies and procedures requiring quarterly scanning, and 
3) vulnerabilities noted in the scan results have been corrected as shown in a re-scan(s). 
For subsequent years after the initial PCI DSS review, four quarters of passing scans must have occurred.

controls.name: D1.TC.Cu.E.2 - Periodic Discussion of Cyber Risks
controls.title: Periodic Discussion of Cyber Risks
controls.body: Cyber risks are actively discussed at business unit meetings.

controls.name: CAN 5.8.3.2 - Removing Accounts
controls.title: Removing Accounts
controls.body: The organization shall remove accounts and/or functionality when users no longer require these for their tasks.

controls.title: Tenant-specific, contained definition of roles

controls.title: Qualifications of Internal Personnel
controls.body: The entity establishes qualifications for personnel responsible for protecting the privacy and security of personal information and assigns such responsibilities only to those personnel who meet these qualifications and have received the necessary training .

controls.title: Adminstrative Activities
controls.body: The organization shall only permit administrator accounts to perform administrative activities (and not user-level activities such as accessing email or browsing the web).

controls.title: Centralized Authorization Control System

controls.title: Account Lockout Mechanism
controls.body: Limit repeated access attempts by locking out the user ID after not more than six attempts.

controls.title: Procedures Include Information Security Responsibilities
controls.body: Ensure that the security policy and procedures clearly define information security responsibilities for all personnel.

controls.title: Instances of noncompliance
controls.body: Instances of noncompliance with privacy policies and procedures are documented and reported and, if needed, corrective and disciplinary measures are taken on a timely basis .

controls.title: Ongoing Monitoring
controls.body: Ongoing procedures are performed for monitoring the effectiveness of controls over personal information based on a risk assessment and for taking timely corrective actions where necessary .

controls.title: Assessment of IT Service Providers

controls.name: CAN 6.3.3.2 - OWASP ASVS Level
controls.title: OWASP ASVS Level
controls.body: The organization shall ensure that they understand the OWASP ASVS level they need to meet for each of their websites.

controls.name: AAC3.6 - Role-based Access
controls.title: AAC3.6 - Role-based Access
controls.body: Role-based access system has been defined and implemented to manage authentication and access to production systems.

controls.name: CAN 6.4.2.1 - Organization-owned Portable Media
controls.title: Organization-owned Portable Media
controls.body: Organizations using portable media shall mandate the sole use of organization-owned secure portable media.

controls.body:
The entity provides notice about its privacy policies and procedures and identifies the purposes for which personal information is collected, used,
 retained, and disclosed.

controls.title: Privacy Policies
controls.body: The entity’s privacy policies address providing notice to individuals .

controls.title: Compliance to PCI DSS

controls.title: AU3.0 - Email Archiving
controls.body: Email archiving is implemented for automatic data retention, auditing and legal discovery purposes.

controls.title: Access Restriction to Audit Logs
controls.body: Limit viewing of audit trails to those with a job-related need.

controls.title: Communication to Individuals
controls.body: Notice is provided to individuals regarding the following privacy policies: purpose; choice/consent; collection; use/retention/ disposal; access; disclosure to third parties; security for privacy; quality; and monitoring/enforcement . If personal information is collected from sources other than the individual, such sources are described in the notice .

controls.name: Sec. 33. Provision (c) - Review of Covered Information
controls.title: Sec. 33. Provision (c) - Review of Covered Information
controls.body:
Except for a parent of a student enrolled in a nonpublic school, the parent of a student enrolled in a school has the right to all of the following:
(1) Inspect and review the student's covered information, regardless of whether it is maintained by the school, the State Board, or an operator.

(2) Request from a school a paper or electronic copy of the student's covered information, including covered information maintained by an operator of the State Board.  If a parent requests an electronic copy of the student's covered information under this paragraph, the school must provide an electronic copy of that information, unless the school does not maintain the information in an electronic format and reproducing the information in an electronic format would be unduly burdensome to the school. If a parent requests a paper copy of the student's covered information, the school may charge the parent the reasonable cost for copying the information in an amount not to exceed the amount fixed in a schedule adopted by the State Board, except that no parent may be denied a copy of the information due to the parent's inability to bear the cost of the copying. The State Board must adopt rules on the methodology and frequency of requests under this paragraph.

(3) Request corrections of factual inaccuracies contained in the student's covered information. After receiving a request for corrections and determining that a factual inaccuracy exists, a school must do either of the following:

(A) If the school maintains or possesses the covered information that contains the factual inaccuracy, correct the factual inaccuracy and confirm the correction with the parent within 90 calendar days after receiving the parent's request.

(B) If the operator or State Board maintains or possesses the covered information that contains the factual inaccuracy, notify the operator or the State Board of the correction. The operator or the State Board must correct the factual inaccuracy and confirm the correction with the school within 90 calendar days after receiving the notice. Within 10 business days after receiving confirmation of the correction from the operator or State Board, the school must confirm the correction with the parent.

* #### Your school has a procedure for a student or parent to inspect and review all student information.
* #### Your school is capable of providing electronic copies of all documents stored in electronic form to students or parents upon request.  
* #### Your school has a procedure to revise any incorrect student information stored by your school. 
* #### Your school has a procedure to inform a student or parent that inaccurate information stored by the school has been revised within three months of receiving the request to correct the information. 
* #### Your school has a procedure to revise any incorrect student information stored by a third party but provided by your school to that third party.

controls.title: Event Logging
controls.body: Event logs recording user activities, exceptions, faults and information security events shall be produced, kept and regularly reviewed.

controls.title: CC7.1.1 - Logging & Monitoring Software

controls.name: DORA-08-003 ICT Risks Identification And Assessment
controls.title: DORA-08-003 ICT Risks Identification And Assessment
controls.body:
(a) All sources of ICT risks are identified on a continuous basis., All cyber threats and ICT vulnerabilities relevant to the entity's ICT-supported business functions, information assets, and ICT assets are assessed and classified.

(b) The identification and assessment of ICT risks are reviewed at least annually, in conjunction with the risk scenarios impacting them.

(c) Risk assessment is performed each time a major change occurs in the network and information system infrastructure.

controls.title: CM-8 (1) Information system component inventory | updates during installations / removals
controls.body: The organization updates the inventory of information system components as an integral part of component installations, removals, and information system updates.

controls.title: PCI 2.5 - Policies and Procedures for Vendor-Suplied Defaults
controls.body: Ensure that security policies and operational procedures for managing vendor defaults and other security parameters are documented, in use, and known to all affected parties.

controls.title: Inventory of Information Systems and Assets
controls.body: The organization shall develop and maintain a list of their information systems and assets. For any information systems and assets not included in their implementation of the baseline cyber security controls, the organization shall document all instances where they make the business decision not to do so.

controls.title: TBL18 - Administrative/Privileged Access
controls.body: Access to a generic administrator or privileged accounts on the databases and servers supporting the application is restricted to authorized personnel based on a role-based access scheme.

controls.name: CAN 4.4.3.6 - Improvements to Cyber Security
controls.title: Improvements to Cyber Security
controls.body: The organization shall commit to progressive improvements to cyber security.

Your school meets one of the following criteria:

controls.body: Organization corrects, amends, or appends personal information based on information provided by data subjects and communicates such information to third parties to meet its objectives related to privacy.

controls.name: 10.0.0 - Monitoring and Enforcement
controls.title: Monitoring and Enforcement
controls.body: The entity monitors compliance with its privacy policies and procedures and has procedures to address privacy-related inquiries, complaints and disputes.

controls.name: CAN 4.4.3.7 - Update to Cyber Security Risk Assessment
controls.title: Update to Cyber Security Risk Assessment
controls.body: The organization shall determine triggers and thresholds to conduct a new or update an existing cyber security risk assessment.

controls.name: CAN 4.4.3.9 - Assessment of Cyber Security Controls
controls.title: Assessment of Cyber Security Controls
controls.body: The organization shall periodically review and/or test cyber security controls to ensure effectiveness. Testing and/or review shall take place at a minimum annually, or if a major change occurs in their system.

controls.name: CR6 - Disaster Recovery Plan (DRP)
controls.title: Disaster Recovery Plan (DRP)

controls.title: Multi-Factor Authentication
controls.body: The organization shall implement multi-factor authentication or document all instances where they cannot or make the business decision not to do so.

controls.name: 10.1.0 - Privacy Policies
controls.title: Privacy Policies
controls.body: The entity’s privacy policies address the monitoring and enforcement of privacy policies and procedures .

controls.name: 10.1.1 - Communication to Individuals
controls.title: Communication to Individuals
controls.body: Individuals are informed about how to contact the entity with inquiries, complaints and disputes .

controls.name: CAN 5.1.2.1 - Incident Response Plan
controls.title: Incident Response Plan
controls.body: The organization shall have an incident response plan for how to respond to incidents of varying severity. If an organization is unable to manage some types of incidents on its own, the organization should have a plan for what it will do.

controls.name: CAN 5.1.2.3 - Cyber Security Insurance
controls.title: Cyber Security Insurance
controls.body: The organization should consider purchasing a cyber security insurance policy that includes coverage for incident response and recovery activities or provide rationale for not purchasing one.

controls.name: HS - Logging and Monitoring (R)
controls.title: Logging and Monitoring (R)
controls.body: Logging is enabled to record administrative activities, access login attempts and security events and monitored on a regular basis. Automated alerts are configured, notifying IT management of any security issues followed up and resolved in a timely manner through the incident management process.

controls.name: 10.2.1 - Inquiry, complaint and dispute Process
controls.title: Inquiry, complaint and dispute Process
controls.body: A process is in place to address inquiries, complaints and disputes .

controls.name: TBL2 - Access Management
controls.title: TBL2 - Access Management
controls.body:
The organization has a formalized process to manage user access requests, changes, and revocations.

User access rights are reviewed on a quarterly basis.

controls.name: HS - Log Management Process (A)
controls.title: Log Management Process (A)
controls.body: The organization has established and implemented a formal log management procedure for monitoring log-in attempts and reporting discrepancies. Access to change log configurations or to modify logs is restricted.

controls.name: IR-4(13) - Incident Handling | Behavior Analysis
controls.title: Incident Handling | Behavior Analysis
controls.body: Analyze anomalous or suspected adversarial behavior in or related to [Assignment: organization-defined environments or resources].

controls.name: 10.2.2 - Dispute resolution and recourse
controls.title: Dispute resolution and recourse
controls.body: Each complaint is addressed, and the resolution is documented and communicated to the individual .

controls.name: 10.2.3 - Compliance review
controls.title: Compliance review
controls.body: Compliance with privacy policies and procedures, commitments and applicable laws, regulations, servicelevel agreements and other contracts is reviewed and documented and the results of such reviews are reported to management . If problems are identified, remediation plans are developed and implemented .

controls.title: SSPA52 - Physical Access Management

controls.title: AC8.1 - Cryptographic Controls

controls.title: SSPA35 - Network Security Assessments

controls.name: CAN 5.4.3.1 - Secure Configuration on Devices

The organization shall implement secure configurations for all their devices unless it is impossible to do so on a specific device:
a. by turning off unnecessary features i.e., block unused ports, disable unused services, remove unused or obsolete software; and
b. by enabling all relevant security features.

controls.name: 3.2.1 - Implicit or explicit consent

controls.body: Implicit or explicit consent is obtained from the individual at or before the time personal information is collected or soon after . The individual’s preferences expressed in his or her consent are confirmed and implemented .
