Additional information:
https://privacypatterns.org/patterns/Strip-invisible-metadata

controls.name: 1.3 - Added-Noise Measurement
controls.title: Added-Noise Measurement
controls.body:
Add some noise to service operation measurements, but make it cancel itself in the long-term.

Additional information:
https://privacypatterns.org/patterns/Added-noise-measurement-obfuscation

controls.name: 1.3 - Appropriate reporting
controls.title: Appropriate reporting
controls.body: Your organisation's operational roles support the practical implementation of data protection and information governance.

controls.name: 10.5.4 - External audit or compliance check - 4
controls.title: External audit or compliance check - 4
controls.body: You produce audit reports to document the findings.

controls.name: 6.18 - Increasing Awareness of Information Aggregation
controls.title: Increasing Awareness of Information Aggregation
controls.body:
Inform users about the potentially identifying effects of information aggregation to prevent them from unknowingly endangering their privacy.

Additional information:
https://privacypatterns.org/patterns/Increasing-Awareness-of-Information-Aggregation

controls.name: 2.1 - Encryption with User-Managed Keys
controls.title: Encryption with User-Managed Keys
controls.body:
Use encryption in such a way that the service provider cannot decrypt the user's information because the user manages the keys.

Enable encryption, with user-managed encryption keys, to protect the confidentiality of personal information that may be transferred or stored by an untrusted 3rd party.

Supports user control, cloud computing and mobile.

Additional information:
https://privacypatterns.org/patterns/Encryption-user-managed-keys

controls.name: 2.10 - Obtain Explicit Consent
controls.title: Obtain Explicit Consent
controls.body:
Controllers require consent to be given willingly and specifically when in any way processing the personal data of their users.

Additional information:
https://privacypatterns.org/patterns/Obtaining-Explicit-Consent

controls.name: 2.11 - Retroactive Location Sharing/Decoupling content and location information visibility
controls.title: Retroactive Location Sharing/Decoupling content and location information visibility
controls.body:
Allow users to retroactively configure privacy for location information with respect to the content's contextual privacy requirements.

Additional information:
https://privacypatterns.org/patterns/Decoupling-[content]-and-location-information-visibility

controls.name: 2.12 - Selective Access Control
controls.title: Selective Access Control
controls.body:
Allow users to specify who may access the content they generate, both during and after submission.

Additional information:
https://privacypatterns.org/patterns/Selective-Access-Control

controls.name: 2.13 - Pay Back
controls.title: Pay Back
controls.body:
Give users some benefits in exchange for providing informaton or content.

Additional information:
https://privacypatterns.org/patterns/Pay-Back

controls.name: 2.14 - Negotiation of Privacy Policy
controls.title: Negotiation of Privacy Policy
controls.body:
Over time, build user preferences from a privacy-preserving default semi-automatically, through opt-in/opt-out, semantics, and informed solicitations.

When a user's preference is not known, assume the most privacy-preserving settings.

Additional information:
https://privacypatterns.org/patterns/Negotiation-of-Privacy-Policy

controls.name: 2.15 - Reasonable Level of Control
controls.title: Reasonable Level of Control
controls.body:
Let users share selectively (push) and make available (pull) specific information to predefined groups or individuals.

Additional information:
https://privacypatterns.org/patterns/Reasonable-Level-of-Control

controls.name: 2.16 - Masquerade
controls.title: Masquerade
controls.body:
Let users filter out some or all personal information they would otherwise provide to a service.

Additional information:
https://privacypatterns.org/patterns/Masquerade

controls.name: 2.17 - Buddy List
controls.title: Buddy List
controls.body:
By default, isolate users to a selection of social connections in a user-defined circle of trust. Allow them to expand this circle or create new ones based on the existing member.

Additional information:
https://privacypatterns.org/patterns/Buddy-List

controls.name: 2.18 - Lawful Consent
controls.title: Lawful Consent
controls.body:
This pattern covers in detail the legal and social obligations surrounding a data subject's consent to processing of their data in specific circumstances. Every use of the subject's personal data should be covered by an explicit agreement in which the data subject was made aware of the implications of their consent.

Additional information:
https://privacypatterns.org/patterns/Lawful-Consent

controls.name: 2.19 - Informed Consent for Web-Based Transactions
controls.title: Informed Consent for Web-Based Transactions
controls.body:
This pattern describes how controllers can inform users whenever they intend to collect or otherwise use a user's personal data.

Additional information:
https://privacypatterns.org/patterns/Informed-Consent-for-Web-based-Transactions

controls.name: 2.2 - Discouraging Blanket Strategies
controls.title: Discouraging Blanket Strategies
controls.body:
Give users the possibility to define a privacy level from a range of options each time they share content.

Additional information:
https://privacypatterns.org/patterns/Discouraging-blanket-strategies

controls.name: 2.20 - Selective Disclosure
controls.title: Selective Disclosure
controls.body:
Many services (or products) require the collection of a fixed, often large, amount of personal data before users can use them. Many users, instead, want to freely choose what information they share. This pattern recommends that services support selective disclosure, tailoring functionality to work with the level of data the user feels comfortable sharing.

Additional information:
https://privacypatterns.org/patterns/Support-Selective-Disclosure

controls.name: 2.21 - Private Link
controls.title: Private Link
controls.body:
Enable sharing and re-sharing without wide public visibility or cumbersome authenticated access control.

Additional information:
https://privacypatterns.org/patterns/Private-link

controls.name: 2.8 - Single Point of Contact
controls.title: Single Point of Contact
controls.body:
The Single Point of Contact is a security authority who protects the privacy and security of sensitive data stored online by validating the authority of requests and ensuring secure communication channels.

Additional information:
https://privacypatterns.org/patterns/Single-Point-of-Contact

controls.name: 2.9 - Enable/Disable Functions
controls.title: Enable/Disable Functions
controls.body:
Allow users to decide granularly what functions they consent to before the function is used.

Additional information:
https://privacypatterns.org/patterns/Enable-Disable-Functions

controls.name: 6.19 - Privacy Awareness Panel
controls.title: Privacy Awareness Panel
controls.body:
Establish user awareness of the risks inherent in the disclosure of their data, whether to the controller themselves or to other users.

Additional information:
https://privacypatterns.org/patterns/Privacy-Awareness-Panel

controls.name: 3.1 - Location Granularity
controls.title: Location Granularity
controls.body:
Since most geographical data has different level of precision (e.g., street, city, county, state, country), consider collecting or distributing only the necessary level of granularity.

Support minimization of data collection and distribution. Important when a service is collecting location data from or about a user, or transmitting location data about a user to a third-party.

Additional information:
https://privacypatterns.org/patterns/Location-granularity

controls.name: 4.1 - User Data Confinement
controls.title: User Data Confinement
controls.body:
Avoid the central collection of personal data by shifting some amount of the processing of personal data to the user-trusted environments (e.g. their own devices). Allow users to control the exact data that shares with service providers.

Additional information:
https://privacypatterns.org/patterns/User-data-confinement-pattern

controls.name: 4.2 - Anonymous Reputation-Based Blacklisting
controls.title: Anonymous Reputation-Based Blacklisting
controls.body:
Get rid of troublemakers without even knowing who they are.

Additional information:
https://privacypatterns.org/patterns/Anonymous-reputation-based-blacklisting

controls.name: 5.1 - Use of Dummies
controls.title: Use of Dummies
controls.body:
Hide the user's actions by adding fake actions that are indistinguishable from real.

Additional information:
https://privacypatterns.org/patterns/Use-of-dummies

controls.name: 5.2 - Pseudonymous Messaging
controls.title: Pseudonymous Messaging
controls.body:
Enhance a messaging service by using a trusted third party to exchange the identifiers of the communication partners by pseudonyms.

Additional information:
https://privacypatterns.org/patterns/Pseudonymous-messaging

controls.name: 5.3 - Onion Routing
controls.title: Onion Routing
controls.body:
Provide unlinkability between senders and receivers by encapsulating the data in different layers of encryption, limiting the knowledge of each node along the delivery path.

Consider applying this to a system in which data is routed between different nodes.

Additional information:
https://privacypatterns.org/patterns/Onion-routing

controls.name: 5.4 - Pseudonymous Identity
controls.title: Pseudonymous Identity
controls.body:
Hide the identity by using a pseudonym and ensure that the pseudonymous identity can not be linked with a real identity during online interactions.

Additional information:
https://privacypatterns.org/patterns/Pseudonymous-identity

controls.name: 5.5 - Aggregation Gateway
controls.title: Aggregation Gateway
controls.body:
Encrypt, aggregate and decrypt at different places.

Additional information:
https://privacypatterns.org/patterns/Aggregation-gateway

controls.name: 5.6 - Trustworthy Privacy Plug-in
controls.title: Trustworthy Privacy Plug-in
controls.body:
Aggregate usage records at the user side in a trustworthy manner.

When you are in charge of billing for the service usage, consider using a privacy plugin at a consumer-trusted device between you and the metering and billing systems. The privacy plugin computes and aggregated invoice and send it to you without providing any fine-grained consumption records.

Additional information:
https://privacypatterns.org/patterns/Trustworthy-privacy-plugin

controls.name: 5.7 - Anonymity Set
controls.title: Anonymity Set
controls.body:
Aggregate multiple entities into a set, such that they cannot be distinguished anymore.

Additional information:
https://privacypatterns.org/patterns/Anonymity-set

controls.name: 6.1 - Informed Implicit Consent
controls.title: Informed Implicit Consent
controls.body:
Provide unavoidable notice of a users implicit consent to the processing of their data, where reasonable to do so.

This is for the situation where you need to collect and process personal data to fulfill you legitimate interests but cannot feasibly acquire each user's explicit consent.

Additional information:
https://privacypatterns.org/patterns/Informed-Implicit-Consent

controls.name: 6.10 - Awareness Feed
controls.title: Awareness Feed
controls.body:
Inform users about how visible data about them is, and what may be derived from that data. This allows users to reconsider what they are comfortable about sharing, and take action if desired.

Additional information:
https://privacypatterns.org/patterns/Awareness-Feed

controls.name: 6.13 - Abridged Terms and Conditions
controls.title: Abridged Terms and Conditions
controls.body:
Enables the user to better understand the Terms and Conditions presented by a system through summarization. The most important elements therein are condensed into a more concise overview.

Additional information:
https://privacypatterns.org/patterns/Abridged-Terms-and-Conditions

controls.name: 6.14 - Policy Matching Display
controls.title: Policy Matching Display
controls.body:
Allow users to specify what privacy preferences they have and non-intrusively bring policy mismatches to their attention.

Additional information:
https://privacypatterns.org/patterns/Policy-matching-display

controls.name: 6.15 - Trust Evaluation of Service Sides
controls.title: Trust Evaluation of Service Sides
controls.body:
A visual highlight provided by an authority which signals the extent to which given privacy criteria are fulfilled. It should be clearly placed and easily found, with links to additional information.

Additional information:
https://privacypatterns.org/patterns/Trust-Evaluation-of-Services-Sides

controls.name: 6.17 - Platform for Privacy Preferences
controls.title: Platform for Privacy Preferences
controls.body:
Use privacy policies which consist of standardized and extensible vocabulary and data element sets, both of which user should be aware of, in order to streamline their review by eliminating redundancies.

This is to solve the problem that users usually do not read privacy policies, as they are too complex and repetitive among the sites they visit. Consider standardizing your policies to enhance comprehension, and providing distinctions for policies shared with other controllers.

Additional information:
https://privacypatterns.org/patterns/Platform-for-Privacy-Preferences

controls.name: 6.2 - Asynchronous Notice
controls.title: Asynchronous Notice
controls.body:
Proactively provide continual, recurring notice to consented users of repeating access to their personal data, including tracking, storage, or redistribution.

Additional information:
https://privacypatterns.org/patterns/Asynchronous-notice

controls.name: 6.20 - Privacy Dashboard
controls.title: Privacy Dashboard
controls.body:
An informational privacy dashboard can provide collected summaries of the collected or processed personal data for a particular user.

Additional information:
https://privacypatterns.org/patterns/Privacy-dashboard

controls.name: 6.21 - Personal Data Table
controls.title: Personal Data Table
controls.body:
In order for users to see what information a controller has about them, they can be provided with a detailed tabular overview of that data upon request.

Additional information:
https://privacypatterns.org/patterns/Personal-Data-Table

controls.name: 6.22 - Informed Secure Passwords
controls.title: Informed Secure Passwords
controls.body:
Ensure that users maintain healthy authentication habits through awareness and understanding.

Additional information:
https://privacypatterns.org/patterns/Informed-Secure-Passwords

controls.name: 6.23 - Layered Policy Design
controls.title: Layered Policy Design
controls.body:
Make privacy policies easier for users to understand by layering detail behind successively more concise and summarized information.

Additional information:
https://privacypatterns.org/patterns/Layered-policy-design

controls.name: 6.24 - Privacy Labels
controls.title: Privacy Labels
controls.body:
Standardize warning labels similar to nutrition information to quickly inform users about privacy policies and preferences.

Additional information:
https://privacypatterns.org/patterns/Privacy-Labels

controls.name: 6.25 - Privacy-Aware Network Client
controls.title: Privacy-Aware Network Client
controls.body:
Enhance user awareness of privacy policies by automatically converting it into a standardized and easily readable format over a secure channel.

Additional information:
https://privacypatterns.org/patterns/Privacy-aware-network-client

controls.name: 6.26 - Privacy Color Coding
controls.title: Privacy Color Coding
controls.body:
Provide visual cues in standardized colors about privacy policies and preferences to help convey information to users more quickly.

Additional information:
https://privacypatterns.org/patterns/Privacy-color-coding

controls.name: 6.27 - Privacy Icons
controls.title: Privacy Icons
controls.body:
A privacy policy which is hard to understand by general audience is summarized and translated into commonly agreed visual icons.

Additional information:
https://privacypatterns.org/patterns/Privacy-icons

controls.name: 6.28 - Appropriate Privacy Icons
controls.title: Appropriate Privacy Icons
controls.body:
Use consistent icons in place of policy aspects. The icons should convey these aspects reliably, without allowing room for misinterpretation once explained to the user.

Additional information:
https://privacypatterns.org/patterns/Appropriate-Privacy-Icons

controls.name: 6.31 - Informed Credential Selection
controls.title: Informed Credential Selection
controls.body:
Ensure users are informed of the potential privacy consequences of sharing various authenticating data.

Additional information:
https://privacypatterns.org/patterns/Informed-Credential-Selection

controls.name: 6.32 - Privacy Aware Wording
controls.title: Privacy Aware Wording
controls.body:
Ensure that the content of privacy related information provided to the user is worded carefully, maintaining both attention and understanding.

Additional information:
https://privacypatterns.org/patterns/Privacy-Aware-Wording

controls.name: 6.33 - Active Broadcast of Presence
controls.title: Active Broadcast of Presence
controls.body:
Users may actively choose to automatically provide updates when they want to share presence information, to increase both the relevance of, and control over, their sharing.

Additional information:
https://privacypatterns.org/patterns/Active-broadcast-of-presence

controls.name: 6.4 - Dynamic Privacy Policy Display
controls.title: Dynamic Privacy Policy Display
controls.body:
Provide standardized contextual policy information on the nature and risks of disclosure through tooltips.

Additional information:
https://privacypatterns.org/patterns/Dynamic-Privacy-Policy-Display

controls.name: 6.5 - Data Breach Notification
controls.title: Data Breach Notification
controls.body:
Ensure that unauthorized access and processing of personal data is detected and reported to the supervisory authority and any sufficiently affected users without any undue delay.

Additional information:
https://privacypatterns.org/patterns/Data-breach-notification-pattern

controls.name: 6.6 - Appropriate Privacy Feedback
controls.title: Appropriate Privacy Feedback
controls.body:
Provide feedback about who a user will disclose their information to using certain privacy settings before that information is actually published.

Additional information:
https://privacypatterns.org/patterns/Appropriate-Privacy-Feedback

controls.name: 6.7 - Preventing Mistakes or Reducing the Impact
controls.title: Preventing Mistakes or Reducing the Impact
controls.body:
Prevent accidental automatic disclosure of personal information.

Additional information:
https://privacypatterns.org/patterns/Preventing-Mistakes-or-Reducing-Their-Impact

controls.name: 6.8 - Unusual Activity
controls.title: Unusual Activity
controls.body:
Prevent suspicious access to user data through alerts and authenticate through multiple factors upon potential compromise of an account.

Additional information:
https://privacypatterns.org/patterns/Unusual-activities

controls.name: Sec. 19 - Security Safeguards - Security measures on integrity and confidentiality of personal information
controls.title: Security Safeguards - Security measures on integrity and confidentiality of personal information
controls.body: "A responsible party must secure the integrity and confidentiality of personal information in its possession or under its conrol by taking appropriate, reaonable technical and organisational meaures to prevent - (a) loss of, damage to or unauthorised destruction of personal information; and (b) unlawful access to or processing of personal information[...]" (POPIA § 19)

controls.name: Sec. 20 - Security Safeguards - Information processed by operator or person acting under authority
controls.title: Security Safeguards - Information processed by operator or person acting under authority
controls.body: "An operator or anyone processing personal infromation on behalf of a responsible party or an ooperator must - (a) process such information only with the knowledge or authorisation of the responsible party; and (b) treat personal information which comes to their knowledge as confidential and must not disclosure it, unless required by law or in the course of the proper performance of their duties." (POPIA § 20)

controls.name: Sec. 21(1) - Security Safeguards - Security measures regarding information processed by operator
controls.title: Security Safeguards - Security measures regarding information processed by operator
controls.body: "A responsible party must, in terms of a written conract between the responsible party and the operator, ensure that the operator which processes personal information for the responsible party established and maintains the security measures referred to in section 19." (POPIA § 21(1))

controls.name: Sec. 22(2) - Security Safeguards - Notification of security compromises
controls.title: Security Safeguards - Notification of security compromises
controls.body: "Where there are reasonable grounds to believe that the personal information of a data subject has been accessed or acquired by any unauthorised person, the responsible party must notify (a) the Regulator; and (b) subject to subsection (3), the data subject[...]" (POPIA § 22(2))

controls.name: 6.9 - Minimal Information Asymmetry
controls.title: Minimal Information Asymmetry
controls.body:
Prevent users from being disenfranchised by their lack of familiarity with the policies, potential risks, and their agency within processing.

Additional information:
https://privacypatterns.org/patterns/Minimal-Information-Asymmetry

controls.name: 7.2 - Identity Federation Do Not Track
controls.title: Identity Federation Do Not Track
controls.body:
The Do Not Track Pattern makes sure that neither the Identity Provider nor the Identity Broker can learn the relationship between the user and the Service Providers the user use.

Additional information:
https://privacypatterns.org/patterns/identity-federation-do-not-track-pattern

controls.name: Sec. 5(a) - Notice
controls.title: Notice
controls.body:
"A data subject has the right [...] to be notified that—
(i) personal information about him, her or it is being collected as provided for in terms of section 18; or
(ii) his, her or its personal information has been accessed or acquired by an unauthorised person as provided for in terms of section 22" (POPIA § 4(a))

controls.name: Sec. 5(b) - Right of access
controls.title: Right of access
controls.body:
"A data subject has the right [...] to establish whether a responsible party holds personal information of that
data subject and to request access to his, her or its personal information as provided for in terms of section 23" (POPIA § 5(b))

controls.name: Sec. 5(c) - Right to rectification and deletion
controls.title: Right to rectification and deletion
controls.body: "A data subject has the right [...] to request, where necessary, the correction, destruction or deletion of his, her or its personal information as provided for in terms of section 24" (POPIA § 5(c))

controls.name: 7.3 - Obligation Management
controls.title: Obligation Management
controls.body:
The pattern allows obligations relating to data sharing, storing and processing to be transferred and managed when the data is shared between multiple parties.

Additional information:
https://privacypatterns.org/patterns/Obligation-management

controls.name: Sec. 5(d)-(f) - Right to object
controls.title: Right to object
controls.body:
"A data subject has the right [...] to object, on reasonable grounds relating to his, her or its particular situation to the processing of his, her or its personal information as provided for in terms of section 11(3)(a)" (POPIA § 5(d))

"A data subject has the right [...] to object to the processing of his, her or its personal information—
(i) at any time for purposes of direct marketing in terms of section 11(3)(b); or
(ii)in terms of section 69(3)(c)" (POPIA § 5(e))

"A data subject has the right [...] not to have his, her or its personal information processed for purposes of direct marketing by means of unsolicited electronic communications except as referred to in section 69(1)" (POPIA § 5(f))

controls.name: Sec. 5(g) - Right to not be subject to automated decisions
controls.title: Right to not be subject to automated decisions
controls.body: "A data subject has the right [...] not to be subject, under certain circumstances, to a decision which is based solely on the basis of the automated processing of his, her or its personal information intended to provide a pro?le of such person as provided for in terms of section 71" (POPIA  § 5(g))

controls.name: 7.4 - Sticky Policy
controls.title: Sticky Policy
controls.body:
Machine-readable policies are sticked to data to define allowed usage and obligations as it travels across multiple parties, enabling users to improve control over their personal information.

Additional information:
https://privacypatterns.org/patterns/Sticky-policy

controls.name: Sec. 55 - Information Officer
controls.title: Information Officer

controls.name: TLS.2.1.01.c - Verwendung von TLS-Protokoll-Versionen
controls.title: Verwendung von TLS-Protokoll-Versionen
controls.body: Bei Neubeschaffungen, die für einen produktiven Einsatz gedacht sind, MUSS auf Kompatibilität mit TLS 1.3 geachtet werden.

controls.name: Sec. 56 - Deputy Information Officers
controls.title: Deputy Information Officers
controls.body: "Each public and private body must make provision, in the manner prescribed in section 17 of the Promotion of Access to Information Act, with the necessary changes, for the designation of - (a) such a number of persons, if any, as deputy information officers as is necessary to perform the duties and responsibilities as set out in section 55(1) of this Act; and (b) any power or duty conferred or imposed on an information officer by this Act to a deputy information officer of that public or private body." (POPIA § 56)

controls.name: § 64(3)(13) - Availability control
controls.title: Availability control
controls.body: Ensure that personal data are protected against loss and destruction

controls.name: § 64(3)(14) - Separability
controls.title: Separability
controls.body: Ensure that personal data collected for different purposes can be processed separately

controls.name: § 64(3)(2) - Data media control
controls.title: Data media control
controls.body: Prevent the unauthorized reading, copying, modification or erasure of data media

controls.name: § 64(3)(4) - User control
controls.title: User control
controls.body: Prevent the use of automated processing systems by unauthorized persons using data communication equipment

controls.name: § 64(3)(5) - Data access control
controls.title: Data access control
controls.body: Ensure that persons authorized to use an automated processing system have access only to the personal data covered by their access authorization

controls.name: § 64(3)(6) - Communication control
controls.title: Communication control
controls.body: Ensure that it is possible to verify and establish the bodies to which personal data have been or may be transmitted or made available using data communication equipment

controls.name: § 64(3)(7) - Input control
controls.title: Input control
controls.body: Ensure that it is subsequently possible to verify and establish which personal data have been input into automated processing systems and when and by whom the personal data were input

controls.name: § 64(3)(8) - Transport control
controls.title: Transport control
controls.body: Ensure that the confidentiality and integrity of personal data are protected during transfers of personal data or during transport of data media

controls.name: § 64(3)(9) - Recovery
controls.title: Recovery
controls.body: Ensure that installed systems may, in the case of interruption, be restored

controls.name: D.1.5.13 - Providing information about the processing of personal data to data subjects
controls.title: Providing information about the processing of personal data to data subjects
controls.body: Providing information about the processing of personal data to data subjects

controls.name: 11 - Select and develop general controls over technology
controls.title: Select and develop general controls over technology
controls.body: The organization selects and develops general control activities over technology to support the achievement of objectives.

controls.name: 13 - Use relevant information
controls.title: Use relevant information
controls.body: The organization obtains or generates and uses relevant, quality information to support the functioning of internal control.

controls.name: 14 - Communicate internally
controls.title: Communicate internally
controls.body: The organization internally communicates information, including objectives and responsibilities for internal control, necessary to support the functioning of internal control.

controls.name: 15 - Communicate externally
controls.title: Communicate externally
controls.body: The organization communicates with external parties regarding matters affecting the functioning of internal control.

controls.name: 16 - Conduct ongoing and/or separate evaluations
controls.title: Conduct ongoing and/or separate evaluations
controls.body: The organization selects, develops, and performs ongoing and/or separate evaluations to ascertain whether the components of internal control are present and functioning.

controls.name: 17 - Evaluate and communicate deficiencies
controls.title: Evaluate and communicate deficiencies
controls.body: The organization evaluates and communicates internal control deficiencies in a timely manner to those parties responsible for taking corrective action, including senior management and the board of directors, as appropriate.

controls.name: 2 - Exercise oversight responsibility
controls.title: Exercise oversight responsibility
controls.body: The board of directors demonstrates independence from management and exercises oversight of the development and performance of internal control.

controls.name: 3 - Establish structure, authority, and responsibility
controls.title: Establish structure, authority, and responsibility
controls.body: Management establishes, with board oversight, structures, reporting lines, and appropriate authorities and responsibilities in the pursuit of objectives.

controls.name: 4 - Demonstrate commitment to competence
controls.title: Demonstrate commitment to competence
controls.body: The organization demonstrates a commitment to attract, develop, and retain competent individuals in alignment with objectives.

controls.name: 5 - Enforce accountability
controls.title: Enforce accountability
controls.body: The organization holds individuals accountable for their internal control responsibilities in the pursuit of objectives.

controls.name: 6 - Specify suitable objectives
controls.title: Specify suitable objectives
controls.body: The organization specifies objectives with sufficient clarity to enable the identification and assessment of risks relating to objectives.

controls.name: 7 - Identify and analyze risk
controls.title: Identify and analyze risk
controls.body: The organization identifies risks to the achievement of its objectives across the entity and analyzes risks as a basis for determining how the risks should be managed.

controls.name: 8 - Assess fraud risk
controls.title: Assess fraud risk
controls.body: The organization considers the potential for fraud in assessing risks to the achievement of objectives.

controls.name: 9 - Identify and analyze significant change
controls.title: Identify and analyze significant change
controls.body: The organization identifies and assesses changes that could significantly affect the system of internal control.

controls.name: Art. 11(II)(b) - Sensitive data - public policy
controls.title: Sensitive data - public policy
controls.body:
"The processing of sensitive personal data shall only occur in the following
situations: . . .
(b) shared processing of data when necessary by the public administration for the execution of public policies provided in laws or regulations" (LGPD Art. 11(II)(b), unofficial translation)

controls.name: Art. 11(II)(c) - Sensitive data - research
controls.title: Sensitive data - research
controls.body:
"The processing of sensitive personal data shall only occur in the following
situations: . . .
(c) studies carried out by a research entity, whenever possible ensuring the anonymization of sensitive personal data" (LGPD Art. 11(II)(c), unofficial translation)

controls.name: Art. 11(II)(d) - Sensitive data - legal rights
controls.title: Sensitive data - legal rights
controls.body:
"The processing of sensitive personal data shall only occur in the following
situations: . . .
(d) the regular exercise of rights, including in a contract and in a judicial, administrative and arbitration procedure, the last in accordance with the terms of Law No. 9,307, of September 23, 1996 (the “Brazilian Arbitration Law”)" (LGPD Art. 11(II)(d), unofficial translation)

controls.name: Art. 11(II)(e) - Sensitive data - life protection
controls.title: Sensitive data - life protection
controls.body:
"The processing of sensitive personal data shall only occur in the following
situations: . . .
(e) protecting life or physical safety of the data subject or a third party" (LGPD Art. 11(II)(e), unofficial translation)

controls.name: Art. 11(II)(f) - Sensitive data - health protection
controls.title: Sensitive data - health protection
controls.body:
"The processing of sensitive personal data shall only occur in the following
situations: . . .
(f) to protect the health, exclusively, in a procedure carried out by health professionals, health services or sanitary authorities; (New Wording Given by Law No. 13,853/2019)" (LGPD Art. 11(II)(f), unofficial translation)

controls.name: Art. 11(II)(g) - Sensitive data - fraud prevention
controls.title: Sensitive data - fraud prevention
controls.body:
"The processing of sensitive personal data shall only occur in the following
situations: . . .
(g) ensuring the prevention of fraud and the safety of the data subject, in processes of identification and authentication of registration in electronic systems, respecting the rights mentioned in Art. 9 of this Law and except when fundamental rights and liberties of the data subject which require protection of personal data prevail" (LGPD Art. 11(II)(g), unofficial translation)

controls.name: Art. 33(I) - Cross-border transfer - adquacy
controls.title: Cross-border transfer - adquacy
controls.body:
"International transfer of personal data is only allowed in the following cases:
(I)  - to countries or international organizations that provide a level of protection of personal data that is adequate to the provisions of this Law" (LGPD Art. 33(I), unofficial Translation)

controls.name: Art. 15 - Termination of processing
controls.title: Termination of processing
controls.body:
"The processing of personal data shall be terminated under the following
circumstances:
I – verification that the purpose has been achieved or that the data are no longer
necessary or pertinent to achieve the specific purpose intended;
II – end of the processing period;
III – communication by the data subject, including when exercising her/his right to
revoke consent, as provided in §5 of Art. 8 of this Law, subject to the public interest; or
IV – determination by the national authority when there has been a violation of the
provisions of this Law." (LGPD Art. 15, unofficial translation)

controls.name: Art. 16 - Erasure of personal data
controls.title: Erasure of personal data
controls.body:
"Personal data shall be deleted following the termination of their processing,
within the scope and technical limits of the activities, but their storage is authorized for the
following purposes:
I – compliance with a legal or regulatory obligation by the controller;
II – study by a research entity, ensuring, whenever possible, the anonymization of the
personal data;
III – transfer to third parties, provided that the requirements for data processing as
provided in this Law are obeyed; or
IV – exclusive use of the controller, with access by third parties being prohibited, and
provided the data has been anonymized." (LGPD Art. 16, unofficial translation)

controls.name: Art. 18(I) - Right to confirmation
controls.title: Right to confirmation
controls.body:
"The data subject, regarding the data subject’s data being processed by the
controller, at any time and by means of request, has the right to obtain the following from the controller:
(I)  – confirmation of the existence of the processing" (LGPD Art. 18(I), unofficial translation)

controls.name: Art. 18(III) - Right to correction
controls.title: Right to correction
controls.body:
"The data subject, regarding the data subject’s data being processed by the
controller, at any time and by means of request, has the right to obtain the following from the controller: . . .
(III)  – correction of incomplete, inaccurate or out-of-date data"  (LGPD Art. 18(III), unofficial translation)

controls.name: Art. 18(VI) - Right to deletion
controls.title: Right to deletion
controls.body:
"The data subject, regarding the data subject’s data being processed by the
controller, at any time and by means of request, has the right to obtain the following from the controller: . . .
(VI) – deletion of personal data processed with the consent of the data subject, except in the situations provided in Art. 16 of this Law" (LGPD Art. 18(VI), unofficial translation)

controls.name: Art. 18(VII) - Right to information about third-party sharing
controls.title: Right to information about third-party sharing
controls.body:
"The data subject, regarding the data subject’s data being processed by the
controller, at any time and by means of request, has the right to obtain the following from the controller: . . .
(VII)  – information about public and private entities with which the controller has shared data"  (LGPD Art. 18(VII), unofficial translation)

controls.name: Art. 20 - Right to request review of automated decisions
controls.title: Right to request review of automated decisions
controls.body:
"The data subject has the right to request for the review of decisions made
solely based on automated processing of personal data affecting her/his interests, including decisions intended to define her/his personal, professional, consumer and credit profile, or aspects of her/his personality" (LGPD Art. 20, unofficial translation)

controls.name: Art. 18(IV) - Right to anonymization/blocking/deletion
controls.title: Right to anonymization/blocking/deletion
controls.body:
"The data subject, regarding the data subject’s data being processed by the
controller, at any time and by means of request, has the right to obtain the following from the controller: . . .
(IV)  – anonymization, blocking or deletion of unnecessary or excessive data or data
processed in noncompliance with the provisions of this Law" (LGPD Art. 18(IV), unofficial translation)

controls.name: Art. 18(IX) - Right to withdraw consent
controls.title: Right to withdraw consent
controls.body:
"The data subject, regarding the data subject’s data being processed by the
controller, at any time and by means of request, has the right to obtain the following from the controller: . . .
(IX) – revocation of consent as provided in §5 of Art. 8 of this Law" (LGPD Art. 18(IX), unofficial translation)

controls.name: Art. 18(VIII) - Right to information about denying consent
controls.title: Right to information about denying consent
controls.body:
"The data subject, regarding the data subject’s data being processed by the
controller, at any time and by means of request, has the right to obtain the following from the controller: . . .
(VIII) – information about the possibility of denying consent and the consequences of such denial" (LGPD Art. 18(VIII), unofficial translation)

controls.name: Art. 25 - Public entities - interoperable and structured format
controls.title: Public entities - interoperable and structured format
controls.body:
"Data shall be kept in an interoperable format and structured for shared use
intended for the execution of public policies, provision of public services, decentralization of public activity, dissemination and access to information by the general public." (LGPD Art. 25, unofficial translation)

controls.name: Art. 32 - Public entities - impact reports
controls.title: Public entities - impact reports
controls.body: "The national authority may request agents of the public authorities to publish impact reports on protection of personal data and may suggest the adoption of standards and good practices for processing personal data by the public authorities" (LGPD Art. 32, unofficial translation)

controls.name: 15 - Principle 15: Assesses Substantial Change
controls.title: Principle 15: Assesses Substantial Change
controls.body: The organization identifies and assesses changes that may substantially affect strategy and business objectives.

controls.name: Art. 33(II)(a) - Cross-border transfer - specific contractual clauses
controls.title: Cross-border transfer - specific contractual clauses
controls.body:
"International transfer of personal data is only allowed in the following cases: . . .
(II) --When the controller offers and proves guarantees of compliance with the principles and the rights of the data subject and the regime of data protection provided in this Law, in the form of:
(a) specific contractual clauses for a given transfer" (LGPD Art. 33(II)(a), unofficial Translation)

controls.name: Art. 33(II)(b) - Cross-border transfer - standard contractual clauses
controls.title: Cross-border transfer - standard contractual clauses
controls.body:
"International transfer of personal data is only allowed in the following cases: . . .
(II) --When the controller offers and proves guarantees of compliance with the principles and the rights of the data subject and the regime of data protection provided in this Law, in the form of: . . .
(b) standard contractual clauses" (LGPD Art. 33(II)(b), unofficial Translation)

controls.name: Art. 33(II)(c) - Cross-border transfer - binding corporate rules
controls.title: Cross-border transfer - binding corporate rules
controls.body:
"International transfer of personal data is only allowed in the following cases: . . .
(II) --When the controller offers and proves guarantees of compliance with the principles and the rights of the data subject and the regime of data protection provided in this Law, in the form of: . . .
(c) binding corporate rules" (LGPD Art. 33(II)(c), unofficial Translation)

controls.name: Art. 33(II)(d) - Cross-border transfer - stamps, certificates and codes of confuct
controls.title: Cross-border transfer - stamps, certificates and codes of confuct
controls.body:
"International transfer of personal data is only allowed in the following cases: . . .
(II) --When the controller offers and proves guarantees of compliance with the principles and the rights of the data subject and the regime of data protection provided in this Law, in the form of: . . .
(d) regularly issued stamps, certificates and codes of conduct" (LGPD Art. 33(II)(d), unofficial Translation)

controls.name: Art. 33(III) - Cross-border transfer - international law
controls.title: Cross-border transfer - international law
controls.body:
"International transfer of personal data is only allowed in the following cases: . . .
(III)  – when the transfer is necessary for international legal cooperation between public intelligence, investigative and prosecutorial agencies, in accordance with the instruments of international law" (LGPD Art. 33(III), unofficial Translation)

controls.name: Art. 33(IV) - Cross-border transfer - life protection
controls.title: Cross-border transfer - life protection
controls.body:
"International transfer of personal data is only allowed in the following cases: . . .
(IV)  – when the transfer is necessary to protect the life or physical safety of the data subject or of a third party" (LGPD Art. 33(IV), unofficial Translation)

controls.name: Art. 33(IX) - Cross-border transfer - Art. 7(II), (V), (VI)
controls.title: Cross-border transfer - Art. 7(II), (V), (VI)
controls.body:
"International transfer of personal data is only allowed in the following cases: . . .
(IX)  – when it is necessary to satisfy the situations provided in items II, V and VI
of Art. 7 of this Law" (LGPD Art. 33(IX), unofficial Translation)

controls.name: Art. 6(I) - Purpose
controls.title: Purpose
controls.body:
"Activities of processing of personal data shall be done in good faith and be subject to the following principles:
I – purpose: processing done for legitimate, specific and explicit purposes of which the data subject is informed, with no possibility of subsequent processing that is incompatible with these purposes" (LGPD Art. 6(I), unofficial translation)

controls.name: Art. 6(II) - Adequacy
controls.title: Adequacy
controls.body:
"Activities of processing of personal data shall be done in good faith and be
subject to the following principles: . . .
II -adequacy:  compatibility of the processing with the purposes communicated to the data subject, in accordance with the context of the processing" (LGPD Art. 6(II), unofficial translation)

controls.name: Art. 6(III) - Necessity
controls.title: Necessity
controls.body:
"Activities of processing of personal data shall be done in good faith and be subject to the following principles: . . .
III - necessity: limitation of the processing to the minimum necessary to achieve its purposes, covering data that are relevant, proportional and non-excessive in relation to the purposes of the data processing" (LGPD Art. 6(III), unofficial translation)

controls.name: Art. 6(IV) - Free access
controls.title: Free access
controls.body:
"Activities of processing of personal data shall be done in good faith and be subject to the following principles: . . .
IV - free access: guarantee to the data subjects of facilitated and free of charge consultation about the form and duration of the processing, as well as about the integrity of their personal data" (LGPD Art. 6(IV), unofficial translation)

controls.name: Art. 33(V) - Cross-border transfer - national authority authorization
controls.title: Cross-border transfer - national authority authorization
controls.body:
"International transfer of personal data is only allowed in the following cases: . . .
(V) – when the national authority authorizes the transfer" (LGPD Art. 33(V), unofficial Translation)

controls.name: Art. 33(VI) - Cross-border transfer - international cooperation
controls.title: Cross-border transfer - international cooperation
controls.body:
"International transfer of personal data is only allowed in the following cases: . . .
(VI) – when the transfer results in a commitment undertaken through international cooperation" (LGPD Art. 33(VI), unofficial Translation)

controls.name: Art. 33(VII) - Cross-border transfer - public policy
controls.title: Cross-border transfer - public policy
controls.body:
"International transfer of personal data is only allowed in the following cases: . . .
(VII) – when the transfer is necessary for the execution of a public policy or legal
attribution of public service, which shall be publicized pursuant to item I of the lead sentence of Art. 23 of this Law" (LGPD Art. 33(VII), unofficial Translation)

controls.name: Sec. 11(1)(c) - Legal basis - legal obligation
controls.title: Legal basis - legal obligation
controls.body: "Personal information may only be processed if - [...] (c) processing complies with an obligation imposed by law on the responsible party" (POPIA § 11(1)(c))

controls.name: Sec. 11(1)(d) - Legal basis - legitimate interests of data subject
controls.title: Legal basis - legitimate interests of data subject
controls.body: "Personal information may only be processed if- … (d) processing protects a legitimate interests of the data subject" (POPIA § 11(1)(d))

controls.name: Sec. 11(1)(e) - Legal basis - public body
controls.title: Legal basis - public body
controls.body: "Personal information may only be processed if - … (e) processing is necessary for the proper performance of a public law duty by a public body" (POPIA § 11(1)(e))

controls.name: Sec. 11(1)(f) - Legal basis - legitimate interests of responsible party
controls.title: Legal basis - legitimate interests of responsible party
controls.body: "Personal information may only be processed if- … (f) processing is necessary for pursuing the legitimate interests of the responsible party or third party to whom the information is supplied[...]" (POPIA § 11(1)(f))

controls.name: Sec. 12 - Collection directly from data subject
controls.title: Collection directly from data subject
controls.body: "(1) Personal information must be collected directly from the data subject, except as otherwise provided for in subsection (2)." (POPIA § 12)

controls.name: Sec. 13 - Collection for specific purpose
controls.title: Collection for specific purpose
controls.body:
"(1) Personal information must be collected for a specific, explicitly defined and lawful purpose related to a function or activity of the responsible party
(2) Steps must be taken in accordance with section 18(1) to ensure that the data subject is aware of the purpose of the collection of the information unless the provisions of section 18(4) are applicable." (POPIA § 13)

controls.name: Sec. 15(1) - Further processing to be compatible with purpose of collection
controls.title: Further processing to be compatible with purpose of collection
controls.body:
"15. (1) Further processing of personal information must be in accordance or compatible with the purpose for which it was collected in terms of section 13.
(2) To assess whether further processing is compatible with the purpose of collection, the responsible party must take account of—(a) the relationship between the purpose of the intended further processing and the purpose for which the information has been collected; (b) the nature of the information concerned; (c) the consequences of the intended further processing for the data subject; (d) the manner in which the information has been collected; and (e) any contractual rights and obligations between the parties.
(3) The further processing of personal information is not incompatible with the purpose of collection if—(a)the data subject or a competent person where the data subject is a child has consented to the further processing of the information; (b)	the information is available in or derived from a public record or has deliberately been made public by the data subject; (c) further processing is necessary—(i) to avoid prejudice to the maintenance of the law by any public body including the prevention, detection, investigation, prosecution and punishment of offences; (ii) to comply with an obligation imposed by law or to enforce legislation concerning the collection of revenue as de?ned in section 1 of the South African Revenue Service Act, 1997 (Act No. 34 of 1997); (iii) for the conduct of proceedings in any court or tribunal that have commenced or are reasonably contemplated; or (iv) in the interests of national security;
(d) the further processing of the information is necessary to prevent or mitigate a	50
serious and imminent threat to—(i) public health or public safety; or (ii) the life or health of the data subject or another individual" (POPIA § 15)

controls.name: Sec. 16 - Quality of information
controls.title: Quality of information
controls.body:
"(1) A responsible party must take reasonably practicable steps to ensure that the personal information is complete, accurate, not misleading and updated where necessary.
(2) In taking the steps referred to in subsection (1), the responsible party must have regard to the purpose for which personal information is collected or further processed." (POPIA § 16)

controls.name: Sec. 17 - Openness - Documentation
controls.title: Openness - Documentation
controls.body: "A responsible party must maintain the documentation of all processing operations under its responsibility as referred to in section 14 or 51 of the Promotion of Access to Information Act." (POPIA § 17)

controls.name: Sec. 58 - Responsible party to notify Regulator if processing is subject to prior authorisation
controls.title: Responsible party to notify Regulator if processing is subject to prior authorisation
controls.body:
"(1) Information processing as contemplated in section 57(1) must be noti?ed as such by the responsible party to the Regulator.
(2) Responsible parties may not carry out information processing that has been noti?ed to the Regulator in terms of subsection (1) until the Regulator has completed its investigation or until they have received notice that a more detailed investigation will not be conducted.
(3) In the case of the noti?cation of information processing to which section 57(1) is applicable, the Regulator must inform the responsible party in writing within four weeks of the noti?cation as to whether or not it will conduct a more detailed investigation.
(4) In the event that the Regulator decides to conduct a more detailed investigation, it must indicate the period within which it plans to conduct this investigation, which period must not exceed 13 weeks.
(5) On conclusion of the more detailed investigation referred to in subsection (4) the Regulator must issue a statement concerning the lawfulness of the information processing.
(6) A statement by the Regulator in terms of subsection (5), to the extent that the 10 information processing is not lawful, is deemed to be an enforcement notice served in terms of section 95 of this Act.
(7) A responsible party that has suspended its processing as required by subsection (2), and which has not received the Regulator’s decision within the time limits speci?ed in subsections (3) and (4), may presume a decision in its favour and continue with its 15 processing." (POPIA § 58)

controls.name: Sec. 72(1)(b) - Cross-border transfer - consent
controls.title: Cross-border transfer - consent
controls.body: "(1) A responsible party in the Republic may not transfer personal information about a data subjct to a third party who is in a foreign country unless - … (b) the data subject consents to the transfer" (POPIA § 72(1)(b))

controls.name: Sec. 72(1)(c) - Cross-border transfer - contract with data subject
controls.title: Cross-border transfer - contract with data subject
controls.body: "(1) A responsible party in the Republic may not transfer personal information about a data subjct to a third party who is in a foreign country unless - [...] (c) the transfer is necessary for the performance of a contract between the data subject and the responsible party, or for the implementation of pre-contractual measures taken in response to the data subject's request" (POPIA § 72(1)(c))

controls.name: Sec. 72(1)(d) - Cross-border transfer - contract with a third party
controls.title: Cross-border transfer - contract with a third party
controls.body: "(1) A responsible party in the Republic may not transfer personal information about a data subject to a third party who is in a foreign country unless - [...] (d) the transfer is necessary for the conclusion or performance of a contract concluded in the interest of the data subject between the responsible party and a third party" (POPIA § 72(1)(d))

controls.name: Sec. 72(1)(e) - Transfers of personal information outside Republic - Benefit of data subject
controls.title: Transfers of personal information outside Republic - Benefit of data subject
controls.body: "(1) A responsible party in the Republic may not transfer personal information about a data subjct to a third party who is in a foreign country unless - [...] (e) the transfer is for the benefit of the data subject, and - (i) it is not reasonably practicable to obtain the consent of the data subject to that transfer; and (ii) if it were reasonably practicable to obtain such consent, the data subject would be likely to give it." (POPIA § 72(1)(e))

controls.name: Sec. 8 - Accountability
controls.title: Accountability
controls.body: "The responsible party must ensure that the conditions set out in this Chapter, and all the measures that give effect to such conditions, are complied with at the time of the determination of the purpose and means of the processing and during the processing itself." (POPIA § 8)

controls.name: Sec. 9 - Lawfulness of processing
controls.title: Lawfulness of processing
controls.body: "Personal information must be processed; (a) lawfully; and (b) in a reasonable manner that does not infringe the privacy of the data subject." (POPIA § 9)

controls.name: § 64(3)(11) - Integrity
controls.title: Integrity
controls.body: Ensure that stored personal data cannot be corrupted by means of a malfunctioning of the system

controls.name: § 64(3)(12) - Processing control
controls.title: Processing control
controls.body: Ensure that personal data processed on behalf of the controller can only be processed in compliance with the controller’s instructions

controls.name: 1.18 - Rapportage van informatiebeveiligingsgebeurtenissen
controls.title: Rapportage van informatiebeveiligingsgebeurtenissen
controls.body: lnformatiebeveiligingsgebeurtenissen behoren zo snel mogelijk via de juiste leidinggevende niveaus te warden gerapporteerd.

controls.name: 1.8 - lnformatie labelen
controls.title: lnformatie labelen
controls.body:
Om informatie te labelen behoort een passende reeks procedures te warden ontwik­
keld en ge'implementeerd in overeenstemming met het informatieclassificatieschema dat is vastgesteld door de organisatie.

controls.name: 3.13 - Beveiliging van apparatuur en bedrijfsmiddelen buiten het terrein
controls.title: Beveiliging van apparatuur en bedrijfsmiddelen buiten het terrein
controls.body:
Bedrijfsmiddelen die zich buiten het
terrein bevinden, behoren te warden beveiligd, waarbij rekening behoort te warden gehouden met de verschillende risico's van werken buiten het terrein van de organisatie.

controls.name: 4.2 - Scheiding van ontwikkel-, test- en productieomgevingen
controls.title: Scheiding van ontwikkel-, test- en productieomgevingen
controls.body: Ontwikkel-, test- en productieomgevingen behoren te warden gescheiden om het risico van onbevoegde toegang tot of veranderingen aan de pro­ductieomgeving te verlagen.

controls.name: Sec. 10 - Minimality
controls.title: Minimality
controls.body: "Personal information may only be processed if, given the purpose for which it is processed, it is adequate, relevant and not excessive." (POPIA § 10)

controls.name: D1.3.3 - Limitation of authorized personnel to those who are verifiable and approved
controls.title: Limitation of authorized personnel to those who are verifiable and approved
controls.body: Limitation of authorized personnel to those who are verifiably responsible (locally, professionally), qualified, reliable (if necessary with security clearance) and formally approved, and with whom no conflict of interests may arise in the exercise of their duties

controls.name: 4.8 - Beheer van technische kwetsbaarheden
controls.title: Beheer van technische kwetsbaarheden
controls.body:
lnformatie over technische kwetsbaarheden van informatiesys­temen die warden gebruikt behoort tijdig te warden verkregen, de blootstelling van de organisatie aan dergelijke kwetsbaarheden te warden geevalueerd en passende maatregelen te warden genomen om
het risico dat ermee samenhangt aan te pakken.

controls.name: 12 - Deploy through policies and procedures
controls.title: Deploy through policies and procedures
controls.body: The organization deploys control activities through policies that establish what is expected and procedures that put policies into action.

controls.name: Art. 46 - Security measures
controls.title: Security measures
controls.body: "Processing agents shall adopt security, technical and administrative measures able to protect personal data from unauthorized accesses and accidental or unlawful situations of destruction, loss, alteration, communication or any type of improper or unlawful processing." (LGPD Art. 46, unofficial translation)

controls.name: Art. 50 - Governance program
controls.title: Governance program
controls.body:
"Controllers and processors, within the scope of their functions, concerning the
processing of personal data, individually or by associations, may formulate rules for good practices and governance that set forth conditions of organization, a regime of operation, the procedures, including those for complaints and petitions from data subjects, security norms, technical standards, specific obligations for the various parties involved in the processing, educational activities, internal mechanisms of supervision and risk mitigation and other aspects related to the processing of personal data" (LGPD Art. 50, unofficial translation)

controls.name: Art. 19 - Facilitation of data subject rights
controls.title: Facilitation of data subject rights
controls.body:
"Confirmation of the existence of or access to personal data shall be provided by means of request by the data subject:
(I) In a simplified format, immediately; or
(II) by means of a clear and complete declaration that indicates the origin of the data, the nonexistence of registration, the criteria used and the purpose of the processing, subject to commercial and industrial secrecy, provided within a period of fifteen (15) days as from the date of the data subject’s request.
§1 Personal data shall be stored in a format that facilitates the exercise of the right to
access.
§2 Information and the data may be provided, at the data subject’s discretion:
I – by electronic means that is safe and suitable for this purpose; or
II – in printed form" (LGPD Art. 19 (I)-(II), unofficial translation)

controls.name: Art. 6(IX) - Nondiscrimination
controls.title: Nondiscrimination
controls.body:
"Activities of processing of personal data shall be done in good faith and be subject to the following principles: . . .
IX – nondiscrimination: impossibility of carrying out the processing for unlawful or abusive discriminatory purposes" (LGPD Art. 6(IX), unofficial translation)

controls.name: Art. 6(V) - Quality of the data
controls.title: Quality of the data
controls.body:
"Activities of processing of personal data shall be done in good faith and be subject to the following principles: . . .
V - quality of the data: guarantee to the data subjects of the accuracy, clarity, relevancy and updating of the data, in accordance with the need and for achieving the purpose of the processing" (LGPD Art. 6(V), unofficial translation)

controls.name: Art. 18(V) - Right to data portability
controls.title: Right to data portability
controls.body:
"The data subject, regarding the data subject’s data being processed by the
controller, at any time and by means of request, has the right to obtain the following from the controller: . . .
(V)  – portability of the data to another service provider or product provider, by the means of an express request, pursuant with the regulations of the national authority, and subject to commercial and industrial secrets" (LGPD Art. 18(V), unofficial translation)

controls.name: Art. 23 - Public entities - fulfillment of public purpose
controls.title: Public entities - fulfillment of public purpose
controls.body:
"Processing of personal data by legal entities of public law referred to in sole
paragraph of Art. 1 of Law No. 12,527, of November 18, 2011 (the “Brazilian Access to Information Law”), shall be done in fulfillment of its public purpose, in benefit of the public interest, for the purpose of performing legal capabilities or discharging legal attributions of the public service, provided that: . . . ." (See LGPD Art. 23, unofficial translation)

controls.name: Art. 27 - Public entities - communication and consent for sharing
controls.title: Public entities - communication and consent for sharing
controls.body:
"Communication or shared use of personal data from a legal entity of public
law to a legal entity of private law shall be communicated to the national authority and shall rely on the consent of the data subject, except:
I – in situations in which consent is waived as provided in this Law;
II – when there is shared use of data, which will be given publicity pursuant to item I
of the lead sentence of Art. 23 of this Law; or
III – in the exceptions contained in §1 of Art. 26 of this Law.
Sole paragraph. The information to be given to the national authority referred to in this article shall be subject to regulation.” (Included by Law No. 13,853/2019)" (LGPD Art. 27, unofficial translation)

controls.name: 7.2.1 - Disclosure of Personal Information
controls.title: Disclosure of Personal Information
controls.body: Personal information is disclosed to third parties only for the purposes described in the notice, and for which the individual has provided implicit or explicit consent, unless a law or regulation specifically requires or allows otherwise .

controls.name: Art. 11(I) - Sensitive data - explicit consent
controls.title: Sensitive data - explicit consent
controls.body:
"The processing of sensitive personal data shall only occur in the following
situations: . . .
I – when the data subject or her/his legal representative specifically and distinctly consents, for the specific purposes" (LGPD Art. 11(I), unofficial translation)

controls.name: Art. 11(II)(a) - Sensitive data - legal obligation
controls.title: Sensitive data - legal obligation
controls.body:
"The processing of sensitive personal data shall only occur in the following
situations: . . .
II – without consent from the data subject, in the situations when it is indispensable for: . . .
(a) controller's compliance with a legal or regulatory obligation" (LGPD Art. 11(II)(a), unofficial translation)

controls.name: Art. 12 - Anonymization
controls.title: Anonymization
controls.body: "Anonymized data shall not be considered personal data, for purposes of this Law, except when the process of anonymization to which the data were submitted has been reversed, using exclusively its own efforts, or when it can be reversed applying reasonable efforts" (LGPD Art. 12, unofficial translation)

controls.name: Art. 13 - Security for public health studies
controls.title: Security for public health studies
controls.body:
"When carrying out public health studies, research entities may have access to
personal databases, which shall be processed exclusively within the entity and strictly for the purpose of carrying out studies and research. Those databases shall be kept in a controlled and secure environment, in accordance with security practices provided in specific regulation and this includes, whenever possible, anonymization or pseudonymization of the data, as well as taking into account the proper ethical standards related to studies and research" (LGPD Art. 13, unofficial translation)

controls.name: 6.2.4 - Denial of Access
controls.title: Denial of Access
controls.body: Individuals are informed, in writing, of the reason a request for access to their personal information was denied, the source of the entity’s legal right to deny such access, if applicable, and the individual’s right, if any, to challenge such denial, as specifically permitted or required by law or regulation .

controls.name: 8.2.1 - Information security Program
controls.title: Information security Program
controls.body: A security program has been developed, documented, approved, and implemented that includes administrative, technical and physical safeguards to protect personal information from loss, misuse, unauthorized access, disclosure, alteration and destruction . The security program should address, but not be limited to, the following areas3 insofar as they relate to the security of personal information: a . Risk assessment and treatment [1 .2 .4] b . Security policy [8 .1 .0] c . Organization of information security [sections 1, 7, and 10] d . Asset management [section 1] e . Human resources security [section 1] f . Physical and environmental security [8 .2 .3 and 8 .2 .4] g . Communications and operations management [sections 1, 7, and 10] h . Access control [sections 1, 8 .2, and 10] i . Information systems acquisition, development, and maintenance [1 .2 .6] j . Information security incident management [1 .2 .7] k . Business continuity management [section 8 .2] l . Compliance [sections 1 and 10]

controls.name: 4.2.2 - Collection by fair and lawful Means
controls.title: Collection by fair and lawful Means
controls.body: Methods of collecting personal information are reviewed by management before they are implemented to confirm that personal information is obtained (a) fairly, without intimidation or deception, and (b) lawfully, adhering to all relevant rules of law, whether derived from statute or common law, relating to the collection of personal information .

controls.name: 1.1.1 - Communication to Internal Personnel
controls.title: Communication to Internal Personnel
controls.body: Privacy policies and the consequences of non- compliance with such policies are communicated, at least annually, to the entity’s internal personnel responsible for collecting, using, retaining and disclosing personal information .  Changes in privacy policies are communicated to such personnel shortly after the changes are approved .

controls.name: 1.2.6 - Infrastructure and systems Management
controls.title: Infrastructure and systems Management
controls.body: The potential privacy impact is assessed when new processes involving personal information are implemented, and when changes are made to such processes (including any such activities outsourced to third parties or contractors), and personal information continues to be protected in accordance with the privacy policies . For this purpose, processes involving personal information include the design, acquisition, development, implementation, configuration, modification and management of the following: • Infrastructure • Systems • Applications • Web sites • Procedures • Products and services • Data bases and information repositories • Mobile computing and other similar electronic devices The use of personal information in process and system test and development is prohibited unless such information is anonymized or otherwise protected in accordance with the entity’s privacy policies and procedures .

controls.name: 1.2.7 - Privacy Incident and breach Management
controls.title: Privacy Incident and breach Management
controls.body: A documented privacy incident and breach management program has been implemented that includes, but is not limited to, the following: • Procedures for the identification, management and resolution of privacy incidents and breaches • Defined responsibilities • A process to identify incident severity and determine required actions and escalation procedures • A process for complying with breach laws and regulations, including stakeholder breach notification, if required • An accountability process for employees or third parties responsible for incidents or breaches with remediation, penalties or discipline, as appropriate • A process for periodic review (at least annually) of actual incidents to identify necessary program updates based on the following: — Incident patterns and root cause — Changes in the internal control environment or external requirements (regulation or legislation) • Periodic testing or walkthrough process (at least on an annual basis) and associated program remediation as needed

controls.name: 6 - Accuracy
controls.title: Accuracy
controls.body:
Personal data shall be accurate and kept up to date, and every reasonable step must be taken to ensure that personal data that is inaccurate, having regard to the purposes for which they are processed, are erased or rectified without delay. [See GDPR, Art. 5(1)(d)]

The requirements must be seen in relation to the risks and consequences of the concrete use of data. Inaccurate personal data could be a risk to the data subjects’ rights and freedoms, for example when leading to a faulty diagnosis or wrongful treatment of a health protocol, or an incorrect image of a person can lead to decisions being made on the wrong basis either manually, using automated decision-making, or through artificial intelligence.

Example:
A bank wishes to use artificial intelligence (AI) to profile customers applying for bank loans as a basis for their decision making. When determining how their AI solutions should be developed, they are determining the means of processing and must consider data protection by design when choosing an AI from a vendor and when deciding on how to train the AI.

When determining how to train the AI, the controller must have accurate data to achieve precise results. Therefore, the controller must ensure that the data used to train the AI is accurate.

Granted they have the legal basis to train the AI using personal data from a large pool of their existing customers, the controller chooses a pool of customers that is representative of the population to also avoid bias.

Customer data is gathered from their own systems, gathering data about the existing loan customers’ payment history, bank transactions, credit card debt, they conduct new credit checks, and they gather data from public registries that they have legal access to use.

To ensure that the data used for AI training is as accurate as possible, the controller only collects data from data sources with correct and up-to date information.

Finally, the bank tests whether the AI is reliable and provides non-discriminatory results. When the AI is fully trained and operative, the bank uses the results as a part of the loan assessments, and will never rely solely on the AI to decide whether to grant loans.

The bank will also review the reliability of the results from the AI at regular intervals.

EDPB Guidelines 4/2019, pp. 21-22
https://edpb.europa.eu/sites/edpb/files/consultation/edpb_guidelines_201904_dataprotection_by_design_and_by_default.pdf

controls.name: 6.8 - Continued Accuracy
controls.title: Continued Accuracy
controls.body: Personal data should be accurate at all stages of the processing, tests of accuracy should be carried out at critical steps.

controls.name: 7 - Storage Limitation
controls.title: Storage Limitation
controls.body:
The controller must ensure that personal data is kept in a form which permits identification of data subjects for no longer than is necessary for the purposes for which the personal data is processed. [See GDPR, Art. 5(1)(c)] It is vital that the controller knows exactly what personal data the company processes and why. The purpose of the processing shall be the deciding criteria in how long personal data shall be stored.

Measures and safeguards that implement the principle of storage limitation shall complement the rights and freedoms of the data subjects, specifically, the right to erasure, the right to object and profiling.

Example:
The controller collects personal data where the purpose of the processing is to administer a membership with the data subject, the personal data shall be deleted when the membership is terminated.

The controller makes an internal procedure for data retention and deletion. According to this, employees must manually delete personal data after the retention period ends. The employee follows the procedure to regularly delete and correct data from any devices, from backups, logs, e-mails and other relevant storage media.

To make deletion more effective, the controller instead implements an automatic system to delete data automatically and more regularly. The system is configured to follow the given procedure for data deletion which then occurs at a predefined regular interval to remove personal data from all of the company’s storage media. The controller reviews and tests the retention policy regularly.

EDPB Guidelines 4/2019, pp. 22-23
https://edpb.europa.eu/sites/edpb/files/consultation/edpb_guidelines_201904_dataprotection_by_design_and_by_default.pdf

controls.name: 4 - Purpose Limitation
controls.title: Purpose Limitation
controls.body:
The controller must collect data for specified, explicit, and legitimate purposes, and not further process the data in a manner that is incompatible with the purposes for which they were collected. [GDPR, Art. 51(b)] The design of the processing should therefore be shaped by what is necessary to achieve the purposes. If any further processing is to take place, the controller must first make sure that this processing has purposes compatible with the original ones and design such processing accordingly. Whether a new purpose is compatible or not, shall be assessed according to the criteria in Article 6(4).

Example:
The controller processes personal data about its customers. The purpose of the processing is to fulfil a contract, i.e. to be able to deliver goods to the correct address and obtain payment. The personal data stored is the purchase history, name, address, e-mail address and telephone number.

The controller is considering buying a Customer Relationship Management (CRM) product that gathers all the customer data such as sales, marketing and customer service in one place. The product gives the opportunity of storing all phone calls, activities, documents, emails and marketing campaigns to get a 360-degree view of the customer. Ultimately the CRM automatically analyses the customers’ purchasing power by using public information. The purpose of the analysis is to target the advertising better but is not a part of the original lawful purpose of the processing.

To be in line with the principle of purpose limitation, the controller requires the provider of the product to map the different processing activities using personal data with the purposes relevant for the controller. Another requirement is that the product shall be able to flag which kind of processing activities using personal data that is not in line with the legitimate purposes of the controller.

After receiving the results of the mapping, the controller assesses whether the new marketing purpose and the targeted advertisement purpose are within the contractual purposes or if they need another legal ground for this processing. Alternatively the controller could choose to not make use of this functionality in the product.

EDPB Guidelines 4/2019, pp. 18-19
https://edpb.europa.eu/sites/edpb/files/consultation/edpb_guidelines_201904_dataprotection_by_design_and_by_default.pdf
