controls.name: D1.8 - Gewährleistungsziele als Design-Strategie
controls.title: Gewährleistungsziele als Design-Strategie
controls.body: Bereits bei der Modellierung von Verarbeitungstätigkeiten müssen für alle Ebenen die Anforderungen des Art. 25 DS-GVO berücksichtigt werden. Der dort formulierte Grundsatz der datenschutzfördernden Technikgestaltung („Data Protection by Design“) und datenschutzfreundlicher Voreinstellungen („Data Protection by Default“) verlangen eine Beachtung operativer Datenschutzanforderungen bereits während der Planungsphase einer Verarbeitung. Demnach sollen technische und organisatorische Maßnahmen nicht erst nachträglich festgelegt und umgesetzt werden, um ggf. nicht-rechtskonforme Funktionalitäten abzustellen. Datenschutzfreundliche Voreinstellungen verlangen auch, dass eine Fachapplikation von vornherein datenschutzkonform konfiguriert werden muss. Diese Grundsätze schließen das Prinzip der Datenminimierung als Design-Strategie ein

controls.name: 1.5 - Organizational Bias
controls.title: Organizational Bias
controls.body: Bias in decision-making has always existed and always will. It is not unusual to find within an entity evidence of dominant personalities, overreliance on numbers, disregard of contrary information, disproportionate weighting of recent events, and a tendency for risk avoidance or risk taking. So the question is not whether bias exists, but rather how bias affecting decisions relating to enterprise risk management can be managed. The board is expected to understand the potential organizational biases that exist and challenge management to overcome them.

controls.name: 5.3.4 - Effective privacy information - 4
controls.title: Effective privacy information - 4

controls.name: 19.1 - Communicating with Stakeholders
controls.title: Communicating with Stakeholders
controls.body:
Various channels are available to the organization for communicating risk data and information to internal and external stakeholders. These channels enable organizations to provide relevant information for use in decision-making.

Internally, management communicates the entity’s strategy and business objectives clearly throughout the organization so that all personnel at all levels understand their individual roles. Specifically, communication channels enable management to convey:
- The importance, relevance, and value of enterprise risk management.
- The characteristics, desired behaviors, and core values that define the culture of the entity.
- The strategy and business objectives of the entity.
- The risk appetite and tolerance.
- The overarching expectations of management and personnel in relation to enterprise risk and performance management.
- The expectations of the organization on any important matters relating to enterprise risk management, including instances of weakness, deterioration, or non-adherence.

Management also communicates information about the entity’s strategy and business objectives to shareholders and other external parties. Enterprise risk management is a key topic in these communications so that external stakeholders not only understand the performance against strategy but the actions consciously taken to achieve it. External communication may include holding quarterly analyst meetings to discuss performance.

An entity with open communication channels can also be on the receiving end of information from external stakeholders. For example, customers and suppliers can provide input on the design or quality of products or services, enabling the organization to address evolving customer demands or preferences. Or inquiries from environmental groups about sustainability approaches could provide an organization with insight into leading approaches or identify potential risks to its reputation. This information may come through email communications, public forums, blogs, hotlines, or other channels.

controls.name: 5.6.1 - Privacy information review - 1
controls.title: Privacy information review - 1
controls.body: You review privacy information against the records of processing activities, to make sure it remains up-to-date and that it actually explains what happens with individuals’ personal data.

controls.name: 9.3 - Data quality
controls.title: Data quality
controls.body: You have procedures in place to make sure that records containing personal data are accurate, adequate and not excessive.

controls.name: 5.6.2 - Privacy information review - 2
controls.title: Privacy information review - 2
controls.body: You maintain a log of historical privacy notices, including the dates you made any changes, in order to allow a review of what privacy information was provided to individuals and when.

controls.name: 5.6.3 - Privacy information review - 3
controls.title: Privacy information review - 3
controls.body: Your organisation carries out user-testing to evaluate how effective their privacy information is.

controls.name: 19.3 - Methods of Communicating
controls.title: Methods of Communicating
controls.body:
For information to be received as intended, it must be communicated clearly. To be sure communication methods are working, organizations should periodically evaluate them. This can be done through existing processes such as stating expectations for enterprise risk management in employee performance goals and subsequent periodic performance evaluations.

Communication methods vary widely, from holding face-to-face meetings, to posting messages on the entity’s intranet, to announcing a new product at an industry convention, to broadcasting to shareholders globally through social media and newswires.

Communication methods can take the form of:
- Electronic messages (e.g., emails, social media, text messages, instant messaging).
- External/third-party materials (e.g., industry, trade, and professional journals, media reports, peer company websites, key internal and external indexes).
- Informal/verbal communications (e.g., one-on-one discussions, meetings).
- Public events (e.g., roadshows, town hall meetings, industry/technical conferences).
- Training and seminars (e.g., live or on-line training, webcast and other video forms, workshops).
- Written internal documents (e.g., briefing documents, dashboards, performance evaluations, presentations, questionnaires and surveys, policies and procedures, FAQs).

In addition to the list above, separate lines of communication are needed when normal channels are inoperative or insufficient for communicating matters requiring heightened attention. Many organizations provide a means to communicate anonymously to the board of directors or a board delegate—such as a whistle-blower hotline. Many organizations also establish escalation protocols and policies to facilitate communication when there are exceptions in standards of conduct or inappropriate behaviors occurring.

controls.title: Data-mapping - 1
controls.body: Your organisation carries out Information audits (or data mapping exercises) to find out what personal data is held and to understand how the information flows through your organisation.

controls.name: 6.1.2 - Data-mapping - 2
controls.title: Data-mapping - 2

controls.name: 20.3 - Types of Reporting
controls.title: Types of Reporting
controls.body:
Risk reporting may include any or all of the following:
- Portfolio view of risk outlines the severity of the risks at the entity level that may impact the achievement of strategy and business objectives. The reporting of the portfolio view highlights the greatest risks to the entity, interdependencies between specific risks, and opportunities. The portfolio view of risk is typically found in management and board reporting.
- Profile view of risk, similar to the portfolio view, outlines the severity of risks, but focuses on different levels within the entity. For example, the risk profile of a division or operating unit may feature in designated risk reporting for management or those areas of the entity.
- Analysis of root causes enables users to understand assumptions and changes underpinning the portfolio and profile views of risk.
- Sensitivity analysis measures the sensitivity of changes in key assumptions embedded in strategy and the potential effect on strategy and business objectives.
- Analysis of new, emerging, and changing risks provides the forward-looking view to anticipate changes to the risk inventory, effects on resource requirements and allocation, and the anticipated performance of the entity.
- Key performance indicators and measures outline the tolerance of the entity and potential risk to a strategy or business objective.
- Trend analysis demonstrates movements and changes in the portfolio view of risk, risk profile, and performance of the entity.
- Disclosure of incidents, breaches, and losses provides insight into effectiveness of risk responses.
- Tracking enterprise risk management plans and initiatives provides a summary of the plan and initiatives in establishing or maintaining enterprise risk management practices. Investment in resources, and the urgency by which initiatives are completed, may also reflect the commitment to enterprise risk management and culture by organizational leaders in responding to risks.

Risk reporting is supplemented by commentary and analysis by subject matter experts. For example, compliance, legal, and technology experts often provide commentary and analysis on the severity of risk, effectiveness of risk responses, drivers for changes in trend analysis, and industry developments and opportunities the entity may have.

controls.name: 5.6.4 - Privacy information review - 4
controls.title: Privacy information review - 4
controls.body: You analyse complaints from the public about how you use personal data, and in particular, any complaints about how you explain that use.

controls.name: 5.6.5 - Privacy information review - 5
controls.title: Privacy information review - 5
controls.body: If you plan to use personal data for a new purpose, you have a procedure to update the privacy information and communicate the changes to individuals before starting any new processing.

controls.name: 20.6 - Key Indicators
controls.title: Key Indicators
controls.body:
Key indicators are used to predict a risk manifesting. They are usually quantitative, but can be qualitative. Key indicators are reported to the levels of the entity that are in the best position to manage the onset of a risk where necessary. They should be reported in tandem with key performance indicators to demonstrate the interrelationship between risk and performance.

Key indicators support a proactive approach to performance management. Key indicators and key performance indicators can be reflected in a single measure. For example, in a manufacturing company, production volumes and the thresholds around them can be viewed through a risk lens. Production volumes above the target can be seen as potential risks to quality, and production volumes below the target can suggest potential risk such as supplier delays, labor shortages, or equipment downtime.

Key indicators are reported along with corresponding targets and acceptable variations. Knowing where an entity lies on the culture spectrum, whether risk averse or risk aggressive, will help determine the key indicators and key performance indicators that are tracked as well as the acceptable variation in performance.

controls.name: 9.3.1 - Data quality - 1
controls.title: Data quality - 1
controls.body: You conduct regular data quality reviews of records containing personal data to make sure they are accurate, adequate and not excessive.

controls.name: 5.7 - Tools supporting transparency and control
controls.title: Tools supporting transparency and control
controls.body: You are open about how you use personal data, and offer tools to support transparency and control, especially when processing children's personal data.

controls.name: 5.7.1 - Tools supporting transparency and control - 1
controls.title: Tools supporting transparency and control - 1
controls.body: Privacy policies are clear and easy for members of the public to access.

controls.name: 5.7.2 - Tools supporting transparency and control - 2
controls.title: Tools supporting transparency and control - 2
controls.body: You provide individuals with tools, such as secure self-service systems, dashboards and just-in-time notices, so they can access, determine and manage how you use their personal data.

controls.name: 5.1 - Establishing and Evaluating Competence
controls.title: Establishing and Evaluating Competence
controls.body:
Management, with board oversight, defines the human capital needed to carry out strategy and business objectives. Understanding the needed competencies helps in establishing how various business processes should be carried out and what skills should be applied. This begins with the board of directors relative to the chief executive officer, and the chief executive officer relative to the management and personnel of each of the divisions, operating units, and functions in the entity. That is, the board of directors evaluates the competence of the chief executive officer and, in turn, management evaluates competence across the entity and addresses any shortcomings or excesses as necessary.

The human resources function helps promote competence by assisting management in developing job descriptions and roles and responsibilities, facilitating training, and evaluating individual performance for managing risk. Management considers the following factors when developing competence requirements:
- Knowledge, skills, and experience with enterprise risk management.
- Nature and degree of judgment and limitations of authority to be applied to a specific position.
- The costs and benefits of different skill levels and experience.

controls.name: 5.7.3 - Tools supporting transparency and control - 3
controls.title: Tools supporting transparency and control - 3
controls.body: Your organisation offers strong privacy defaults and user-friendly options and controls.

controls.name: 5.7.4 - Tools supporting transparency and control - 4
controls.title: Tools supporting transparency and control - 4
controls.body: You help children to exercise their data protection rights, where relevant, in an easily accessible way that they understand.

controls.name: 5.7.5 - Tools supporting transparency and control - 5
controls.title: Tools supporting transparency and control - 5

controls.name: 5.2 - Attracting, Developing, and Retaining Individuals
controls.title: Attracting, Developing, and Retaining Individuals
controls.body:
The ongoing commitment to competence is supported by and embedded in the human resource management processes. Management at different levels establishes the structure and process to:
- Attract: Seek out the necessary number of candidates who fit the entity’s desired risk-aware culture, desired behaviors, operating style, and organizational needs, and who have the competence for the proposed roles.
- Train: Enable individuals to develop and maintain enterprise risk management competencies appropriate for assigned roles and responsibilities, reinforce standards of conduct and desired levels of competence, tailor training to specific needs, and consider a mix of delivery techniques, including classroom instruction, self-study, and on-the-job training.
- Mentor: Provide guidance on the individual’s performance regarding standards of conduct and competence, align the individual’s skills and expertise with the entity’s strategy and business objectives, and help the individual to adapt to an evolving business context.
- Evaluate: Measure the performance of individuals in relation to achieving business objectives and demonstrating enterprise risk management competence against agreed-upon standards.
- Retain: Provide incentives to motivate an individual and reinforce the desired level of performance and conduct. This includes offering training and credentialing as appropriate.

Throughout this process, any behavior not consistent with standards of conduct, policies, performance expectations, and enterprise risk management responsibilities is identified, assessed, and corrected in a timely manner.

In addition, organizations must continually identify and evaluate those roles that are essential to achieving strategy and business objectives. The decision of whether a role is essential is made by assessing the consequences of having that role temporarily or permanently unfilled. The question needs to be asked: How will strategy and business objectives be achieved if the position of, for example, the chief executive officer is left unfilled?

controls.name: UC.006 - Wurde während UC.003 tatsächlich ein Sicherheitsvorfall festgestellt, muss dieser als solcher bearbeitet werden.
controls.title: Wurde während UC.003 tatsächlich ein Sicherheitsvorfall festgestellt, muss dieser als solcher bearbeitet werden.
controls.body: Wurde während UC.003 tatsächlich ein Sicherheitsvorfall festgestellt, muss dieser als solcher bearbeitet werden. In diesem Anwendungsfall werden alle betroffenen Geräte ermittelt und im Anschluss forensisch analysiert, um weitere Spuren sicherzustellen, die in den Protokollierungsdaten nicht enthalten waren. Daraufhin werden die betroffenen Geräte bereinigt. Das heißt, in diesem Anwendungsfall liegt einerseits die Erkenntnis vor, dass es sich um einen Sicherheitsvorfall handelt (ggf. mag dies aber kein gezielter Angriff gewesen sein) und andererseits besteht die Notwendigkeit, tatsächlich einzelne physische Geräte zu identifizieren. Wie zuvor schon beschrieben, ist es hierbei unausweichlich, auch die dazugehörige Person zu ermitteln. Wie UC.003 (um weitere Betroffene Systeme zu identifizieren) Zusätzlich: DR.009: Die Protokollierungsdaten von den betroffenen Systemen müssen in der ursprünglichen Form vorliegen, um die Identifizierung der physischen Geräte und die weitere forensische Analyse zu ermöglichen. DR.010: Da die Bearbeitung eines Sicherheitsvorfalls sehr viel Zeit beanspruchen kann, müssen die Daten der Systeme, die mit dem Sicherheitsvorfall in Verbindung stehen, für den Zeitraum der Bearbeitung über die Speicherfrist (siehe Kapitel 2.3) hinaus gesichert werden können.

controls.category: Records Of Processing And Lawful Basis
controls.name: 6.2 - Records of processing activities (ROPA)
controls.title: Records of processing activities (ROPA)
controls.body: Your organisation has a formal, documented, comprehensive and accurate ROPA based on a data mapping exercise that is reviewed regularly.

controls.name: D1.2.8 - Sollverhaltens von Prozessen und regelmäßiges Durchführen von Tests, Risiken und Sicherheitslücken
controls.title: Sollverhaltens von Prozessen und regelmäßiges Durchführen von Tests, Risiken und Sicherheitslücken

controls.category: Records Of Processing And Lawful Basis
controls.name: 6.2.1 - Records of processing activities (ROPA) - 1
controls.title: Records of processing activities (ROPA) - 1
controls.body: You record processing activities in electronic form so you can add, remove or amend information easily.

controls.name: 9.4 - Retention schedule
controls.title: Retention schedule
controls.body: You have an appropriate retention schedule outlining storage periods for all personal data, which you review regularly.

controls.name: 10.7.4 - Performance and compliance information - 4
controls.title: Performance and compliance information - 4
controls.body: You have KPIs regarding records management, including the use of metrics such as file retrieval statistics, adherence to disposal schedules, and the performance of the system in place to index and track paper files containing personal data.

controls.name: 2.1 - Direction and support
controls.title: Direction and support
controls.body: Direction and support: Your organisation's policies and procedures provide your staff with enough direction to understand their roles and responsibilities regarding data protection and information governance.

controls.name: 3.1.2 - All staff training programme - 2
controls.title: All staff training programme - 2
controls.body: The programme is comprehensive and includes training for all staff on key areas of data protection such as handling requests, data sharing, information security, personal data breaches and records management.

controls.name: 2.2.4 - Review and approval - 4
controls.title: Review and approval - 4
controls.body: You update policies and procedures without undue delay when they require changes, eg because of operational change, court or regulatory decisions, or changes in regulatory guidance.

controls.name: MDM.05 - Berechtigungsmanagement im MDM
controls.title: Berechtigungsmanagement im MDM
controls.body: Das MDM muss über ein Rechtemanagement verfügen, so dass das Berechtigungskonzept vollständig umgesetzt werden kann. Über das Rechtemanagement müssen Zugriffsrechte zuverlässig zugeordnet werden können, so dass Benutzergruppen und Administratoren nur über Berechtigungen verfügen, die für die Aufgabenerfüllung notwendig sind (Minimalprinzip).

controls.name: 3.1.4 - All staff training programme - 4
controls.title: All staff training programme - 4
controls.body: You assign responsibilities for managing data protection and information governance training across your organisation and you have training plans or strategies in place to meet training needs within agreed time-scales.

controls.name: 3.3 - Specialised roles
controls.title: Specialised roles
controls.body: Specialised roles or functions with key data protection responsibilities (such as DPOs, subject access and records management teams) receive additional training and professional development beyond the basic level provided to all staff.

controls.name: 4.1.3 - Informing individuals and identifying requests - 3
controls.title: Informing individuals and identifying requests - 3
controls.body: All staff receive training and guidance about how to recognise requests and where to send them.

controls.category: Risks And Data Protection Impact Assessments
controls.name: 8.1.4 - Identifying, recording and managing risks - 4
controls.title: Identifying, recording and managing risks - 4
controls.body: You have formal procedures to identify, record and manage risks associated with information assets in an information asset register.

controls.category: Records Of Processing And Lawful Basis
controls.name: 6.4.1 - Good practice for ROPAs - 1
controls.title: Good practice for ROPAs - 1

controls.category: Records Of Processing And Lawful Basis
controls.name: 6.5 - Documenting your lawful basis
controls.title: Documenting your lawful basis
controls.body: You document and appropriately justify your organisation's lawful basis for processing personal data in line with Article 6 of the GDPR (and Articles 9 and 10, if the processing involves special category or criminal offence data).

controls.category: Records Of Processing And Lawful Basis
controls.name: 6.5.1 - Documenting your lawful basis - 1
controls.title: Documenting your lawful basis - 1
controls.body: Your organisation selects the most appropriate lawful basis (or bases) for each activity following a review of the processing purposes.

controls.category: Records Of Processing And Lawful Basis
controls.name: 6.5.2 - Documenting your lawful basis - 2
controls.title: Documenting your lawful basis - 2
controls.body: You document the lawful basis (or bases) relied upon and the reasons why.

controls.category: Records Of Processing And Lawful Basis
controls.name: 6.5.3 - Documenting your lawful basis - 3
controls.title: Documenting your lawful basis - 3
controls.body: If your organisation processes special category data or criminal offence data, you identify and document a lawful basis for general processing and an additional condition for processing this type of data (or in the case of criminal offence data only, you identify the official authority to process).

controls.category: Records Of Processing And Lawful Basis
controls.name: 6.5.4 - Documenting your lawful basis - 4
controls.title: Documenting your lawful basis - 4
controls.body: In the case of special category or criminal offence data, you document consideration of the requirements of Article 9 or 10 of the GDPR and Schedule 1 of the DPA 2018 where relevant.

controls.name: 7.1.2 - Data sharing policies and procedures - 2
controls.title: Data sharing policies and procedures - 2
controls.body: You document all sharing decisions for audit, monitoring and investigation purposes and you regularly review them.

controls.name: M43.28 - Fragen zur Spezifikation von Protokolldaten
controls.title: Fragen zur Spezifikation von Protokolldaten
controls.body: Fragen zur Spezifikation von Protokolldaten

controls.category: Records Of Processing And Lawful Basis
controls.name: 6.5.6 - Documenting your lawful basis - 6
controls.title: Documenting your lawful basis - 6
controls.body: You identify the lawful basis before starting any new processing.

controls.category: Records Of Processing And Lawful Basis
controls.name: 6.6 - Lawful basis transparency
controls.title: Lawful basis transparency
controls.body: You make information about the purpose of the processing and the lawful basis publicly available. This is easy to locate, access and read.

controls.category: Records Of Processing And Lawful Basis
controls.name: 6.6.1 - Lawful basis transparency - 1
controls.title: Lawful basis transparency - 1
controls.body: You make information about the purposes of the processing, your lawful basis and relevant conditions for processing any special category data or criminal offence data publicly available in your organisation's privacy notice(s).

controls.category: Records Of Processing And Lawful Basis
controls.name: 6.6.2 - Lawful basis transparency - 2
controls.title: Lawful basis transparency - 2
controls.body: You provide information in an easily understandable format.

controls.category: Records Of Processing And Lawful Basis
controls.name: 6.6.3 - Lawful basis transparency - 3
controls.title: Lawful basis transparency - 3
controls.body: If there is a genuine change in circumstances, or if your lawful basis must change due to a new and unanticipated purpose, you inform individuals in timely manner and record the changes.

controls.category: Records Of Processing And Lawful Basis
controls.name: 6.7 - Consent requirements
controls.title: Consent requirements
controls.body: If your organisation relies on consent for the processing of personal data, you comply with the requirements that consent must be: specific; granular; prominent; opt-in; documented; and easily withdrawn.

controls.category: Records Of Processing And Lawful Basis
controls.name: 6.7.1 - Consent requirements - 1
controls.title: Consent requirements - 1
controls.body: Consent requests: are kept separate from other terms and conditions; require a positive opt-in and do not use pre-ticked boxes; are clear and specific (not a pre-condition of signing up to a service); inform individuals how to withdraw consent in an easy way; and give your organisation's name as well as the names of any third parties relying on consent.

controls.category: Records Of Processing And Lawful Basis
controls.name: 6.7.2 - Consent requirements - 2
controls.title: Consent requirements - 2
controls.body: You have records of what an individual has consented to, including what they were told and when and how they consented. The records are thorough and easy for relevant staff to access, review and withdraw if required.

controls.category: Records Of Processing And Lawful Basis
controls.name: 6.7.3 - Consent requirements - 3
controls.title: Consent requirements - 3
controls.body: You have evidence and examples of how consent is sought from individuals, for example online forms or notices, opt in-tick boxes, and paper-based forms.

controls.category: Records Of Processing And Lawful Basis
controls.name: 6.8 - Reviewing consent
controls.title: Reviewing consent
controls.body: You proactively review records of previously gathered consent, which demonstrates a commitment to confirming and refreshing consents.

controls.category: Records Of Processing And Lawful Basis
controls.name: 6.9.4 - Risk-based age checks and parental/guardian consent - 4
controls.title: Risk-based age checks and parental/guardian consent - 4
controls.body: When providing online services to children, if the child is under 13, you have records of parental or guardian consent which are reviewed regularly, and you make reasonable efforts to verify that the person giving consent has parental or guardian responsibility. You give particular consideration when a child reaches the age of 13 and is able to provide their own consent.

controls.name: 7.1 - Data sharing policies and procedures
controls.title: Data sharing policies and procedures
controls.body: Your organisation's policies and procedures make sure that you appropriately manage data sharing decisions.

controls.name: 7.1.4 - Data sharing policies and procedures - 4
controls.title: Data sharing policies and procedures - 4
controls.body: Your organisation adequately trains all staff likely to make decisions about data sharing, and makes them aware of their responsibilities. You refresh this training appropriately.

controls.name: 7.2.1 - Data sharing agreements - 1
controls.title: Data sharing agreements - 1
controls.body: You agree data sharing agreements with all the relevant parties and senior management signs them off.

controls.name: 7.2.2 - Data sharing agreements - 2
controls.title: Data sharing agreements - 2
controls.body: The data sharing agreement includes details about: the parties' roles; the purpose of the data sharing; what is going to happen to the data at each stage; and sets standards (with a high privacy default for children).

controls.name: 7.2.3 - Data sharing agreements - 3
controls.title: Data sharing agreements - 3
controls.body: Where necessary, procedures and guidance covering each organisation's day-to-day operations support the agreements.

controls.name: 7.2.5 - Data sharing agreements - 5
controls.title: Data sharing agreements - 5
controls.body: You have a regular review process to make sure that the information remains accurate and up-to-date, and to examine how the agreement is working.

controls.name: 7.2.6 - Data sharing agreements - 6
controls.title: Data sharing agreements - 6
controls.body: There is a central log of the current data sharing agreements.

controls.name: 7.3 - Restricted transfers
controls.title: Restricted transfers
controls.body: Your organisation has procedures in place to make sure that restricted transfers are made appropriately.

controls.name: 7.3.1 - Restricted transfers - 1
controls.title: Restricted transfers - 1
controls.body: You consider whether the restricted transfer is covered by an adequacy decision or by 'appropriate safeguards' listed in data protection law, such as contracts incorporating standard contractual data protection clauses adopted by the Commission or Binding Corporate Rules.

controls.name: 7.7.2 - Processor compliance reviews - 2
controls.title: Processor compliance reviews - 2
controls.body: You carry out routine compliance checks, proportionate to the processing risks, to test that processors are complying with contractual agreements.

controls.name: 7.8 - Third party products and services
controls.title: Third party products and services
controls.body: Your organisation considers 'data protection by design' when selecting services and products to use in data processing activities.

controls.name: 7.8.1 - Third party products and services - 1
controls.title: Third party products and services - 1
controls.body: When third parties supply products or services to process personal data, you choose suppliers that design their products or services with data protection in mind.

controls.name: 7.9 - Purpose limitation
controls.title: Purpose limitation
controls.body: Your organisation proactively takes steps to only share necessary personal data with processors or other third parties.

controls.name: 7.9.1 - Purpose limitation - 1
controls.title: Purpose limitation - 1
controls.body: Your organisation only shares the personal data necessary to achieve its specific purpose.

controls.name: 7.9.2 - Purpose limitation - 2
controls.title: Purpose limitation - 2
controls.body: When information is shared, it is pseudonymised or minimised wherever possible. You also consider anonymisation so that the information is no longer personal data.

controls.category: Risks And Data Protection Impact Assessments
controls.name: 8.1 - Identifying, recording and managing risks
controls.title: Identifying, recording and managing risks
controls.body: Your organisation has appropriate policies, procedures and measures to identify, record and manage information risks.

controls.category: Risks And Data Protection Impact Assessments
controls.name: 8.1.1 - Identifying, recording and managing risks - 1
controls.title: Identifying, recording and managing risks - 1
controls.body: An information risk policy (either a separate document or part of a wider corporate risk policy) sets out how your organisation and its data processors manage information risk, and how you monitor compliance with the information risk policy.

controls.category: Risks And Data Protection Impact Assessments
controls.name: 8.1.2 - Identifying, recording and managing risks - 2
controls.title: Identifying, recording and managing risks - 2
controls.body: You have a process to help staff report and escalate data protection and information governance concerns and risks to a central point, for example, staff forums.

controls.category: Risks And Data Protection Impact Assessments
controls.name: 8.1.5 - Identifying, recording and managing risks - 5
controls.title: Identifying, recording and managing risks - 5
controls.body: If you identify information risks, you have appropriate action plans, progress reports and a consideration of the lessons learnt to avoid future risk.

controls.category: Risks And Data Protection Impact Assessments
controls.name: 8.5.2 - DPIA risk mitigation and review - 2
controls.title: DPIA risk mitigation and review - 2
controls.body: You integrate outcomes from DPIAs into relevant work plans, project action plans and risk registers.

controls.category: Risks And Data Protection Impact Assessments
controls.name: 8.2 - Data protection by design and by default
controls.title: Data protection by design and by default
controls.body: You take a' data protection by design and by default' approach to managing risks, and, as appropriate, you build DPIA requirements into policies and procedures.

controls.name: 9.8.2 - Access control - 2
controls.title: Access control - 2
controls.body: You implement a formal user access provisioning procedure to assign access rights for staff (including temporary staff) and third party contractors to all relevant systems and services required to fulfil their role, for example 'new starter process'.

controls.name: 9.8.3 - Access control - 3
controls.title: Access control - 3
controls.body: You restrict and control the allocation and use of privileged access rights.

controls.name: 9.8.4 - Access control - 4
controls.title: Access control - 4
controls.body: You keep a log of user access to systems holding personal data.

controls.name: 9.8.5 - Access control - 5
controls.title: Access control - 5
controls.body: You regularly review users' access rights and adjust or remove rights where appropriate, for example when an employee changes role or leaves the organisation.

controls.name: 9.9 - Unauthorised access
controls.title: Unauthorised access
controls.body: You prevent unauthorised access to systems and applications.

controls.name: 9.9.1 - Unauthorised access - 1
controls.title: Unauthorised access - 1
controls.body: You restrict access to systems or applications processing personal data to the absolute minimum in accordance with the principle of least privilege (for example read/write/delete/execute access rules are applied).

controls.name: 9.9.10 - Unauthorised access - 10
controls.title: Unauthorised access - 10
controls.body: You deploy URL or web content filtering to block specific websites or entire categories.

controls.name: 9.9.11 - Unauthorised access - 11
controls.title: Unauthorised access - 11
controls.body: You strictly control or prohibit the use of social media, or messaging apps such as WhatsApp to share personal data.

controls.name: 9.9.13 - Unauthorised access - 13
controls.title: Unauthorised access - 13
controls.body: You do not have unsupported operating systems in use, for example Windows XP, Windows Server 2003.

controls.name: D1.2.4 - Löschen oder Berichtigen falscher Daten
controls.title: Löschen oder Berichtigen falscher Daten
controls.body: Löschen oder Berichtigen falscher Daten

controls.name: 9.9.2 - Unauthorised access - 2
controls.title: Unauthorised access - 2
controls.body: You apply minimum password complexity rules and limited log on attempts to systems or applications processing personal data.

controls.name: 9.9.3 - Unauthorised access - 3
controls.title: Unauthorised access - 3
controls.body: You have password management controls in place, including default password changing, controlled use of any shared passwords and secure password storage (not in plain text).

controls.name: 9.9.4 - Unauthorised access - 4
controls.title: Unauthorised access - 4
controls.body: Emails content and attachment security solutions (encryption) appropriately protect emails containing sensitive personal data.

controls.name: 9.9.5 - Unauthorised access - 5
controls.title: Unauthorised access - 5
controls.body: You log and monitor user and system activity to detect anything unusual.

controls.name: 9.9.7 - Unauthorised access - 7
controls.title: Unauthorised access - 7
controls.body: Anti-malware and anti-virus protection is kept up-to-date and you configure it to perform regular scans.

controls.name: 9.9.8 - Unauthorised access - 8
controls.title: Unauthorised access - 8
controls.body: Your organisation has access to and acts upon any updates on technical vulnerabilities to systems or software, for example vendor’s alerts or patches.

controls.name: 9.9.9 - Unauthorised access - 9
controls.title: Unauthorised access - 9
controls.body: You regularly run vulnerability scans.

 Anonymisierungsverfahren.
