controls.name: J.9 - IS/IT Incident Management - Eradication
controls.title: IS/IT Incident Management - Eradication
controls.body:
Control: An organization has implemented a process for eradicating potential threats in a prioritized manner.

Control Objective: An organization should identify the key components of the incident including sources of attacks, assets that may be impacted and take actions to eradicate the threats.

controls.name: K. - Business Resiliency
controls.title: Business Resiliency
controls.body: Domain Objective: Organizations should incorporate business resiliency considerations into the overall design of their business model to mitigate the risk of service disruptions and the impacts of those within the supply chain. This should include an enterprise-wide, process-oriented approach that considers technology, business operations, testing and communication strategies that are critical to business resiliency planning for the entire business and should be formally documented and approved by senior management.

controls.name: K.1 - Business Resiliency Governance
controls.title: Business Resiliency Governance
controls.body:
Control: A formal policy is in place which establishes program objectives, responsibilities and processes.

Control Objective: An organization should create and maintain in-depth business resiliency governance policy, function and processes that documents overall expectations for the program, how the program is to be executed and defines responsibility for each element of the program.

Risk Statement: The absence of a business resiliency governance policy to guide the risk management program may result in a lack of clear direction and senior management involvement to assure readiness to handle service disruptions and impact to the products and services provided by the organization.

controls.name: K.5 - Data Backup Restoration
controls.title: Data Backup Restoration
controls.body:
Control: An organization has implemented a backup and replication (as appropriate) process for its systems, applications and data to ensure successful restoration.

Control Objective: An organization should have systems, applications and data available in the event of an incident that compromises its production information technology operations. Backups and replications (as appropriate) of scoped data should be available to meet required Recovery Point.

Risk Statement: The absence of processes and capabilities for the restoration of scoped data and software may lead to a loss of ability to resume operations and the provisioning of services in the event of corruption or loss of the primary data source.

controls.name: K.6 - Exercising
controls.title: Exercising
controls.body:
Control: Business resiliency and disaster recovery exercises are defined, scheduled, planned, conducted and evaluated according to a consistent process. The problems identified are made visible and documented with an associated remediation action plan.

Control Objective: An organization should conduct thorough exercises that validate the effectiveness of business continuity and disaster recovery procedures and capabilities, the readiness of its personnel to perform required actions and the viability of related communication mechanisms and procedures.

Risk Statement: The absence of exercising and testing may lead to unprepared individuals, unanticipated delays in meeting recovery objectives and/or unidentified gaps in the program.

controls.name: L.4 - Marketing and Selling Business Practices
controls.title: Marketing and Selling Business Practices
controls.body:

Control Objective: An organization should have a process implemented to ensure all systems and networks are protected from DoS attacks.

Risk Statement: The absence of documented process ensuring DoS protection exists may result in the inability of the organization to meet its internal and external obligations for protecting the availability of scoped data.

controls.name: N.8 - Wireless Networks Encryption
controls.title: Wireless Networks Encryption
controls.body:
Control: Encryption is required prior to connecting to authorized wireless networks.

Control Objective: An organization should ensure that wireless encryption for authorized wireless networks is implemented to protect from threats and to maintain security for the systems and applications using the network.

Risk Statement: The absence of wireless network encryption may lead to a loss of confidentiality, integrity and availability of scoped data through unauthorized access.

controls.name: T. - Threat Management
controls.title: Threat Management
controls.body: Domain Objective: Organizations should ensure that security threats are managed using both automated and manual scanning tools.

controls.name: T.1 - Anti-malware protection policy and program
controls.title: Anti-malware protection policy and program
controls.body:
Control: The organization has defined and implemented policies and procedures that address deployment of controls to protect against malware.

Control Objective: An organization should define and maintain policies and procedures for the deployment of controls to protect against malware.

Risk Statement: The absence of a malware protection policy and/or procedures may result in an increase in the probability of the organization being susceptible to malware and virus infection, causing business interruptions and vulnerability exposure, due to lack of organizational controls.

controls.body:

controls.title: Technical Compliance Checking - Vulnerability Testing and Remediation
controls.body:
Control: Target systems are scanned for vulnerabilities and identified vulnerabilities are remediated.

Control Objective: An organization should ensure that externally facing systems are regularly scanned for compliance against industry security standards and that any applicable detected vulnerabilities are remediated.

Risk Statement: The absence of identifying and remediating vulnerabilities may increase risk exposure and potential for attack.

controls.name: T.6 - Mobile Code Security
controls.title: Mobile Code Security
controls.body:
Control: An organization has a formal program regarding the download, authentication, updates, signing, access and use of mobile code.

Control Objective: An organization should have formalized policies and procedures related to the use and restrictions of mobile code.

Risk Statement: The absence of formalized policies and procedures related to the use and restrictions of mobile code may result in errors or issues regarding integrity, availability or confidentiality.

controls.name: 2.4.3 - Contractual obligations regarding redress mechanisms and legal counseling for data subjects seeking to exercise their rights.
controls.title: Contractual obligations regarding redress mechanisms and legal counseling for data subjects seeking to exercise their rights.
controls.body:
The contract could commit the exporter and importer to assist the data subject in exercising his/her rights in the third country jurisdiction through ad hoc redress mechanisms and legal counselling.

Conditions for effectiveness:
- National regulations and policies may impose conditions that may undermine the effectiveness of the ad hoc redress mechanisms provided for.
- Legal counselling could be helpful for the data subject, especially considering how complex and costly it can be for a data subject to understand a third country’s legal system and to exercise legal actions from abroad, potentially in a foreign language. However, this clause will always offer a limited additional protection, as providing assistance and legal counselling to data subjects cannot in itself remedy a third country’s legal order failure to provide for a level of protection essentially equivalent to that guaranteed within the EU. This contractual measure will necessarily need to be complementary to other supplementary measures.

This supplementary measure would only be effective provided that the law of the third country provides for redress before its national courts or that an ad hoc redress mechanism exist. In any case, this would however not be an efficient supplementary measure against surveillance measures if no redress mechanism exists.

controls.name: 3.1.1 - Internal policies for governance of transfers especially with groups of enterprises.
controls.title: Internal policies for governance of transfers especially with groups of enterprises.
controls.body:
Adoption of adequate internal policies with clear allocation of responsibilities for data transfers, reporting channels and standard operating procedures for cases of covert or official requests from public authorities to access the data. Especially in case of transfers among groups of enterprises, these policies may include, among others, the appointment of a specific team, which should be based within the EEA, composed by experts on IT, data protection and privacy laws, to deal with requests that involve personal data transferred from the EU; the notification to the senior legal and corporate management and to the data exporter upon receipt of such requests; the procedural steps to challenge disproportionate or unlawful requests and the provision of transparent information to data subjects.

Development of specific training procedures for personnel in charge of managing requests for access to personal data from public authorities, which should be periodically updated to reflect new legislative and jurisprudential developments in the third country and in the EEA. The training procedures should include the requirements of EU law as to access by public authorities to personal data, in particular as following from Article 52 (1) of the Charter of Fundamental Rights. Awareness of personnel should be raised in particular by means of assessment of practical examples of public
authorities’ data access requests and by applying the standard following from Article 52(1) of the Charter of Fundamental Rights to such practical examples. Such training should take into account the particular situation of the data importer, e.g. legislation and regulations of the third country to which the data importer is subject to, and should be developed where possible in cooperation with the data exporter.

Conditions for effectiveness:
- These policies may only be envisaged for those cases where the request from public authorities in the third country is compatible with EU law. When the request is incompatible, these policies would not suffice to ensure an equivalent level of protection of the personal data and, as said above, transfers must be stopped or appropriate supplementary measures to avoid the access must be put in place.

controls.name: 3.2.1 - Document and record the requests for access received from public authorities and the response provided, alongside the legal reasoning and the actors involved.
controls.title: Document and record the requests for access received from public authorities and the response provided, alongside the legal reasoning and the actors involved.
controls.body:
Document and record the requests for access received from public authorities and the response provided, alongside the legal reasoning and the actors involved (e.g. if the exporter has been notified
and its reply, the assessment of the team in charge of dealing with such requests, etc.). These records should be made available to the data exporter, who should in turn provide them to the data subjects concerned where required.

Conditions for effectiveness:
- National legislation in the third country may prevent disclosure of the requests or substantial information thereof and therefore render this practice ineffective. The data importer should inform the exporter of its inability to provide such documents and records, thus offering the exporter the option to suspend the transfers if such inability would lead to a decrease of the level of protection.

controls.name: V.3 - Security Review of Hypervisor Configuration
controls.title: Security Review of Hypervisor Configuration
controls.body:
Control: A CSP has implemented a process to confirm secure configurations and operational practices are being applied to its virtual host systems and hypervisors prior to production and on a consistent basis thereafter.

Control Objective: A Cloud Service Provider (CSP) should implement a monitoring process to ensure secure configuration and operational practices are being applied to virtual host systems and hypervisors.

Risk Statement: The absence of baseline and continual monitoring of virtual host systems and hypervisors may result in systems that are misconfigured using vulnerable system settings.

controls.name: 2.2.1 - Contractual obligations regarding access to data by public authorities.
controls.title: Contractual obligations regarding access to data by public authorities.

controls.name: 2.2.2 - Contractual obligations regarding system back doors.
controls.title: Contractual obligations regarding system back doors.
controls.body:
The exporter could also add clauses whereby the importer certifies that (1) it has not purposefully created back doors or similar programming that could be used to access the system and/or personal data (2) it has not purposefully created or changed its business processes in a manner that facilitates access to personal data or systems, and (3) that national law or government policy does not require the importer to create or maintain back doors or to facilitate access to personal data or systems or for the importer to be in possession or to hand over the encryption key.

Conditions for effectiveness:
- The existence of legislation or government policies preventing importers from disclosing this information may render this clause ineffective. The importer will thus not be able to enter into the contract or will need to notify to the exporter of its inability to continue complying with its contractual commitments.81
- The contract must include penalties and/or the exporter’s ability to terminate the contract on short notice in those cases in which the importer does not reveal the existence of a back door or similar programming or manipulated business processes or any requirement to implement any of these or fails to promptly inform the exporter once their existence comes to its knowledge.

controls.name: 2.2.3 - Contractual obligations regarding audits and inspections of the data processing facilities.
controls.title: Contractual obligations regarding audits and inspections of the data processing facilities.
controls.body:
The exporter could reinforce its power to conduct audits or inspections of the data processing facilities of the importer, on-site and/or remotely, to verify if data was disclosed to public authorities
and under which conditions (access not beyond what is necessary and proportionate in a democratic society), for instance by providing for a short notice and mechanisms ensuring the rapid intervention of inspection bodies and reinforcing the autonomy of the exporter in selecting the inspection bodies

Conditions for effectiveness:
- The scope of the audit should legally and technically cover any processing by the importer’s processors or sub-processors of the personal data transmitted in the third country to be fully effective.
- Access logs and other similar trails should be tamper proof so that the auditors can find evidence of disclosure. Access logs and other similar trails should also distinguish between accesses due to regular business operations and accesses due to orders or requests for access.

controls.name: L.3 - Professional Ethics and Business Practices
controls.title: Professional Ethics and Business Practices
controls.body:
Control: A compliance program that defines the organization's professional ethics and business practices and compliance expectations for the organization is implemented and maintained.

Control Objective: An organization's risk management program should include a formal compliance and ethics program that ensures an organization's professional ethics and business practices requirements, based on company values and standards of conduct and its compliance obligations.

Risk Statement: The absence of a compliance program may result in the organization's inability to adhere to professional and ethical business practices or required corporate governance or compliance obligations.

controls.name: 2.2.4 - Contractual obligations regarding notification of inabilty to comply with contractual commmitemtns.
controls.title: Contractual obligations regarding notification of inabilty to comply with contractual commmitemtns.
controls.body:
Where the law and practice of the third country of the importer was initially assessed and deemed to provide an essentially equivalent level of protection as provided in the EU for data transferred by the exporter, the exporter could still strengthen the obligation of the data importer to inform promptly the data exporter of its inability to comply with the contractual commitments and as a
result with the required standard of “essentially equivalent level of data protection”.

This inability to comply may result from changes in the third country’s legislation or practice.84 The clauses could set specific and strict time limits and procedures for the swift suspension of the transfer of data and/or the termination of the contract and the importer’s return or deletion of the data received. Keeping track of the requests received, their scope, and the effectiveness of the measures adopted to counter them, should provide the exporter with sufficient indications to exercise its duty to suspend or end the transfer and/or terminate the contract. 

Condigions for effectiveness:
- The notification needs to take place before access is granted to the data. Otherwise, by the time the exporter receives the notification, the rights of the individual may have already been
violated if the request is based on laws of that third country that exceed what the level of data protection afforded under EU law permits. The notification may still serve to prevent future violations and to allow the exporter to fulfil its duty to suspend the transfer of personal data to the third country and/or terminate the contract.
- The data importer must monitor any legal or policy developments that might lead to its inability to comply with its obligations, and promptly inform the data exporter of any such changes and developments, and if possible ahead of their implementation to enable the data exporter to recover the data from the data importer.
- The clauses should provide for a quick mechanism whereby the data exporter authorises the data importer to promptly secure or return the data to the data exporter, or if this is not feasible, delete or securely encrypt the data without necessarily waiting for the exporter’s instructions, if a specific threshold to be agreed between the data exporter and the data importer is met. The importer should implement this mechanism from the beginning of the data transfer and test it regularly to ensure that it can be applied on short notice.
- Other clauses could enable the exporter to monitor the importer’s compliance with these obligations via audits, inspections and other verification measures and to enforce them with penalties on the importer and/or the exporter’s capacity to suspend the transfer and/or terminate immediately the contract.

controls.name: 2.2.5 - Contractual obligations regarding "Warrant Canary" method of notifying of orders by public authorities to disclose data.
controls.title: Contractual obligations regarding "Warrant Canary" method of notifying of orders by public authorities to disclose data.
controls.body:
Insofar as allowed by national law in the third country, the contract could reinforce the transparency obligations of the importer by providing for a “Warrant Canary” method, whereby the importer
commits to regularly publish (e.g. at least every 24 hours) a cryptographically signed message informing the exporter that as of a certain date and time it has received no order to disclose personal data or the like. The absence of an update of this notification will indicate to the exporter that the importer may have received an order.

Conditions for effectiveness:
- The regulations of the third country must permit the data importer to issue this form of passive notification to the exporter.
- The data exporter must automatically monitor the warrant canary notifications.
- The data importer must ensure that its private key for signing the Warrant Canary is kept safe and that it cannot be forced to issue false Warrant Canaries by the regulations of the third country. To this end, it might be of use if several signatures by different persons are needed and/or the Warrant Canary is issued by a person outside the third country’s jurisdiction.

controls.name: 2.3.2 - Contractual obligations regarding informing a public authority of the incompatibility of an order with Article 46 GDPR and other obligations.
controls.title: Contractual obligations regarding informing a public authority of the incompatibility of an order with Article 46 GDPR and other obligations.
controls.body:
In the same situation as described above, the the importer could commit to inform the requesting public authority of the incompatibility of the order with the safeguards contained in the Article 46 GDPR transfer tool and the resulting conflict of obligations for the importer. The importer would notify simultaneously and as soon as possible the exporter and/or the competent supervisory
authority from the EEA, insofar as possible under the third country legal order. 

Conditions for effectiveness:
- Such information on the protection conferred by EU law and the conflict of obligations should have some legal effect in the legal order of the third country, such as a judicial or administrative review of the order or request for access, the requirement of a judicial warrant, and/or a temporary suspension of the order to add some protection to the data.
- The legal system of the country must not prevent the importer from notifying the exporter or at least the competent supervisory authority from the EEA of the order or request for access received.
- The importer will need to be able to document and demonstrate to the exporter the actions it has taken, exercising its best efforts, to fulfill this commitment.

controls.name: 2.4.1 - Contractual obligations regarding data subject consent to access data.
controls.title: Contractual obligations regarding data subject consent to access data.
controls.body:
The contract could provide that personal data transmitted in plain text in the normal course of business (including in support cases) may only be accessed with the express or implied consent of the exporter and/or the data subject.

Conditions for effectiveness:
- This clause could be effective in those situations in which importers receive requests from public authorities to cooperate on a voluntary basis, as opposed to e.g. data access by public authorities that occurs without the data importer’s knowledge or against its will.
- In some situations the data subject may not be in a position to oppose the access or to give a consent that meets all the conditions set out under EU law (freely given, specific, informed, and unambiguous) (e.g in the case of employees).
- National regulations or policies compelling the importer not to disclose the order for access may render this clause ineffective, unless it can be backed with technical methods requiring the exporter’s or the data subject’s intervention for the data in plant text to be accessible. Such technical measures to restrict access may be envisaged in particular if access is only granted in specific support or service cases, but the data itself is stored in the EEA.

controls.name: 2.4.2 - Contractual obligations regarding notifying data subjects of orders by public authorities to disclose data.
controls.title: Contractual obligations regarding notifying data subjects of orders by public authorities to disclose data.
controls.body:
The contract could oblige the importer and/or the exporter to notify promptly the data subject of the request or order received from the public authorities of the third country, or of the importer’s inability to comply with the contractual commitments, to enable the data subject to seek information and an effective redress (e.g. by lodging a claim with his/her competent supervisory authority and/or judicial authority and demonstrate his/her standing in the courts of the third country).

Conditions for effectiveness:
- This notification could alert the data subject to potential accesses by public authorities in third countries to his/her data. It could thus enable the data subject to seek additional information with the exporters and to lodge a claim with his/her competent supervisory authority. This clause could also address some of the difficulties an individual may face in demonstrating his/her standing (locus standi) before third country courts to challenge the public authorities’ access to his/her data.
- National regulations and policies may prevent this notification to the data subject. The exporter and importer could nonetheless commit to informing the data subject as soon as the restrictions on the disclosure of data are lifted and to make its best efforts to obtain the waiver of the prohibition to disclose. At a minimum, the exporter or the competent supervisory authority could notify the data subject of the suspension or termination of the transfer of his/her personal data due to the importer’s inability to comply with its contractual commitments as a result of its receipt of a request for access.

controls.name: 3.2.2 - Regular publication of transparency reports or summaries regarding governmental requests for access to data and the kind of reply provided, insofar publication is allowed by local law.
controls.title: Regular publication of transparency reports or summaries regarding governmental requests for access to data and the kind of reply provided, insofar publication is allowed by local law.
controls.body:
Regular publication of transparency reports or summaries regarding governmental requests for access to data and the kind of reply provided, insofar publication is allowed by local law. 

Conditions for effectiveness:
- The information provided should be relevant, clear and as detailed as possible. National legislation in the third country may prevent disclosure of detailed information. In those cases, the data importer should employ its best efforts to publish statistical information or similar type of aggregated information.

controls.name: 3.3.1 - Adoption of strict and granular data access and confidentiality policies and best practices, based on a strict need-to-know principle, monitored with regular audits and enforced through disciplinary measures may also be useful measures in a transfer context.
controls.title: Adoption of strict and granular data access and confidentiality policies and best practices, based on a strict need-to-know principle, monitored with regular audits and enforced through disciplinary measures may also be useful measures in a transfer context.
controls.body:
Already existing organisational requirements under the accountability principle, such as the adoption of strict and granular data access and confidentiality policies and best practices, based on
a strict need-to-know principle, monitored with regular audits and enforced through disciplinary measures may also be useful measures in a transfer context. Data minimisation should be considered in this regard, in order to limit the exposure of personal data to unauthorised access. For example, in some cases it might not be necessary to transfer certain data (e.g. in case of remote access to EEA data, such as in support cases, when restricted access is granted instead of full access; or when the provision of a service only requires the transfer of a limited set of data, and not an entire database). 

Conditions for effectiveness:
- Regular audits and strong disciplinary measures should be in place in order to monitor and enforce compliance with the data minimisation measures also in the transfer context. 
- The data exporter shall perform an assessment of the personal data in its possession before the transfer takes place, in order to identify those sets of data that are not necessary for the purposes of the transfer and, therefore, won’t be shared with the data importer.
- Data minimisation measures should be accompanied with technical measures as to ensure that data are not subject to unauthorised access. For example, the implementation of secure multiparty computation mechanisms and the spread of encrypted datasets among different trusted entities can prevent by design that any unilateral access lead to the disclosure of identifiable data.

controls.name: N.4 - Network Security - Input Validation
controls.title: Network Security - Input Validation
controls.body:
Control: An organization has implemented a process for input validation on all internet facing web forms.

Control Objective: An organization should have a process implemented for input validation to be performed on all internet facing web forms.

Risk Statement: The absence of an implemented process for input validation on internet-facing web forms or applications may result in the inability of the organization to protect the integrity of scoped data.

controls.name: P.4 - Privacy Impact Risk Assessments
controls.title: Privacy Impact Risk Assessments
controls.body:
Control: A risk assessment process is maintained to address identification and classification of privacy risks; mitigation; policy management/monitoring based on changes in the environment; including reporting of privacy risks to management.

Control Objective: The organization should develop and maintain a privacy impact or risk assessment process to address its privacy obligations due to changes in the internal or external environment.

Risk Statement: The absence of a privacy impact or risk assessment process may lead to a violation of contract, privacy law or privacy policy/notice obligations, thereby increasing the risk of non-compliance.

controls.title: Frequency of privacy risk assessment | Privacy Impact Risk Assessments

controls.name: L.2 - Monitoring and Reporting - Compliance Requirement Identification
controls.title: Monitoring and Reporting - Compliance Requirement Identification
controls.body:
Control: A process is implemented to identify and assess changes in the regulatory environment that could affect internal controls related to its regulatory, statutory or contractual obligations.

Control Objective: The organization should ensure a regulatory change management process is implemented to monitor, identify, assess and implement changes (for example, environmental, regulatory and technological changes) that could significantly affect reputation risk and compliance to its regulatory, statutory or contractual obligations.

Risk Statement: The absence of a process to track regulatory and other compliance requirements that are used as applicable to develop internal controls, may result in improper identification of requirements and/or lack of compliance.

controls.name: L.2.7 - Evidence of a process for tracking outcomes or corrective actions | Monitoring and Reporting - Compliance Requirement Identification
controls.title: Evidence of a process for tracking outcomes or corrective actions | Monitoring and Reporting - Compliance Requirement Identification
controls.body: Attribute of L.2 Monitoring and Reporting - Compliance Requirement Identification

controls.name: K.2 - Business Impact Analysis (BIA)
controls.title: Business Impact Analysis (BIA)
controls.body:
Control: Business impact analysis is performed, maintained and reviewed by senior management, as well as exercised periodically (at the minimum, annually) and upon material changes to critical business functions and their required assets and dependencies.

Control Objective: An organization should conduct an assessment to prioritize all business assets and activities, including their interdependencies, as part of a workflow analysis. This assessment should also evaluate the potential impact of business disruptions resulting from uncontrolled, non-specific events on the organization’s business functions and activities.

Risk Statement: The absence of a business impact analysis may result in lack of prioritization of business assets and activities that could in turn prevent the necessary assets and activities from being prepared to respond to a business disruption that impacts the continued availability of critical products and services.

controls.name: L.1 - Monitoring and Reporting - Compliance/organization
controls.title: Monitoring and Reporting - Compliance/organization
controls.body:
Control: An internal function(s) of the organization has defined responsibility to implement compliance management functions, an environmental risk management program, including the monitoring and reporting of resolution of outstanding regulatory and/or contractual issues, including performing assessments to audit such compliance on a periodic basis.

Control Objective: An organization should establish a formalized process for monitoring compliance with regulatory matters, environmental risk, recording and reporting compliance issues and implementing programs or processes to meet these obligations, through an internal audit, risk management or compliance department or similar management oversight entity with responsibility for defining compliance management functions, including assessing, identifying and tracking resolution of outstanding regulatory issues.

Risk Statement: The absence of accountability for compliance matters and environmental risk management as they apply to the organization may result in the organization being non-compliant with regulatory and/or contractual requirements.

controls.name: L.1.2 - Evidence that there is a process for reporting issues and findings to senior management or to board of directors on a routine | Monitoring and Reporting - Compliance/organization
controls.title: Evidence that there is a process for reporting issues and findings to senior management or to board of directors on a routine | Monitoring and Reporting - Compliance/organization
controls.body: Attribute of L.1 Monitoring and Reporting - Compliance/organization

controls.name: N.1 - Network Security - Intrusion Detection Systems (IDS) / Intrusion Prevention Systems (IPS) Signature Updates
controls.title: Network Security - Intrusion Detection Systems (IDS) / Intrusion Prevention Systems (IPS) Signature Updates
controls.body:
Control: Signatures are up to date on network IDS/IPS per the organization’s policy.

Control Objective: An organization must ensure that intrusion detection systems (IDS)/intrusion prevention systems (IPS) have the latest signatures applied to effectively monitor for the most recent threats and vulnerabilities.

Risk Statement: The absence of regular updates to IDS/IPS signatures may result in the organization's inability to effectively identify and prevent threats.

controls.name: N.12 - Data Loss Prevention - Program
controls.title: Data Loss Prevention - Program
controls.body:
Control: A formalized data loss prevention program is implemented, maintained and evaluated.

Control Objective: An organization should implement and maintain a data loss prevention program that identifies, monitors and protects an organization's critical and sensitive data while in motion, in use and at rest to ensure the organization's data is protected and prevented from loss.

Risk Statement: The absence of a data loss prevention program may result in the organization’s inability to prevent data leakage or loss that could cause harm to the organization financially, reputationally and operationally.

controls.name: V.2.3 - Review process for external audit reports to confirm review control considerations responsibilities | Cloud Audit Program
controls.title: Review process for external audit reports to confirm review control considerations responsibilities | Cloud Audit Program
controls.body: Attribute of V.2 Cloud Audit Program

controls.name: U.1.27 - Standalone authentication requirements are required, such as a PIN or secret question | Server Security Configuration Standards
controls.title: Standalone authentication requirements are required, such as a PIN or secret question | Server Security Configuration Standards
controls.body: Attribute of U.1 Server Security Configuration Standards

controls.name: N.2 - Network Security - Firewall(s) and/or Other Devices Providing the Same Functionality
controls.title: Network Security - Firewall(s) and/or Other Devices Providing the Same Functionality
controls.body:
Control: An organization has firewall(s) and/or other devices providing the same functionality in place to protect and filter traffic between defined network zones that possess different levels of trust.

Control Objective: Networks should be segregated to ensure systems and applications are protected from threats outside of their connected network. This should include utilizing firewalls to segment and protect the organization’s internal network from the Internet and from other less restricted internal networks.

Risk Statement: The absence of a firewall (or similar device) protecting the organization from outside entities may result in unauthorized access to scoped data or systems.

controls.name: V.2.4 - Identification of individuals responsible for ensuring all application server components (e.g., web server, mail server, databases) remain hardened | Cloud Audit Program
controls.title: Identification of individuals responsible for ensuring all application server components (e.g., web server, mail server, databases) remain hardened | Cloud Audit Program
controls.body: Attribute of V.2 Cloud Audit Program

controls.name: P.1 - Privacy Program Management
controls.title: Privacy Program Management
controls.body:
Control: The organization has defined and maintained an inventory of scoped data, based upon data category or data classification, including location information and identification of data flows or transfers

Control Objective: An organization should define and maintain processes to identify privacy data classification, maintain data inventories and document data flows for scoped data.

Risk Statement: The absence of data classification, privacy data inventories and privacy data flows may result in repositories of unprotected and unmanaged privacy data which becomes vulnerable to a breach or non-compliance with applicable privacy laws.

controls.name: P.10 - Authorizations, Monitoring & Enforcement
controls.title: Authorizations, Monitoring & Enforcement
controls.body:
Control: The organization has implemented processes to address required legal authorizations, including monitoring and enforcement procedures that address the monitoring of inquiries, complaints, disputes and recourse for violations of privacy compliance.

Control Objective: The organization should define and maintain a privacy or data protection function to maintain compliance, enforcement and monitoring procedures including processes that address complaint or dispute handling for the right of recourse of individuals.

Risk Statement: The absence of enforcement or monitoring procedures to maintain legal authorizations and to address the right of recourse of individuals may lead to a violation of law or contractual obligation or risk of litigation to the organization.

controls.name: V.2.5 - Identification of individuals responsible for deploying patches to all application server components (e.g., web server, mail server, databases) | Cloud Audit Program
controls.title: Identification of individuals responsible for deploying patches to all application server components (e.g., web server, mail server, databases) | Cloud Audit Program
controls.body: Attribute of V.2 Cloud Audit Program

controls.name: P.2 - Privacy Organization & Program Maintenance
controls.title: Privacy Organization & Program Maintenance
controls.body:
Control: An individual or function has been assigned as accountable for the privacy program at the organization and for oversight of privacy obligations at its relevant third parties.

Control Objective: An organization should define, document, communicate and assign accountability for its privacy program or data protection function.

Risk Statement: The absence of a privacy or data protection function program within an organization may increase the risk of privacy compliance issues and poor protection of personal information that may lead to unauthorized disclosures, misuse of personal information and breaches.

controls.name: P.3 - Privacy Awareness
controls.title: Privacy Awareness
controls.body:
Control: The organization has developed, implemented and maintained a privacy awareness training for its constituents on an annual basis.

Control Objective: An organization should have processes in place to develop, implement and maintain privacy awareness training for its constituents to ensure understanding of key information privacy requirements and obligations to maintain the privacy of scoped data.

Risk Statement: The absence of privacy awareness training may lead to poor understanding of the inherent risks of not protecting the data resulting in poor implementation of controls designed to protect personal information.

controls.name: P.5 - Privacy Data Collection, Notice, Choice & Consent
controls.title: Privacy Data Collection, Notice, Choice & Consent
controls.body:
Control: The organization has defined, implemented and maintains agreements or operational procedures for data collection, use, disclosure and consent practices of target data based on privacy jurisdiction and in alignment with the organization's privacy practices.

Control Objective: The organization should define and document agreements or operational procedures between outsourcers and third parties that define the authorized data collection, use, disclosure and consent practices of scoped data consistent with the applicable privacy jurisdiction and the organization's privacy policies and notices.

Risk Statement: The absence of documented agreements, notices or operational procedures that define the authorized data collection, use, disclosure or consent mechanisms may be a contractual or regulatory violation and lead to poor privacy practices increasing the risk of unauthorized disclosure of data.

controls.name: P.5.4 - Authorized purpose or use of client scoped data | Privacy Data Collection, Notice, Choice & Consent
controls.title: Authorized purpose or use of client scoped data | Privacy Data Collection, Notice, Choice & Consent
controls.body: Attribute of P.5 Privacy Data Collection, Notice, Choice & Consent

controls.name: P.6 - Online Privacy
controls.title: Online Privacy
controls.body:
Control: The organization has defined, implemented and maintains a website, mobile application or digital services privacy notice on Internet-facing websites, mobile applications or other digital services from the point where users access client-scoped data.

Control Objective: An organization with one or more Internet-facing website(s), mobile applications or other digital services that provide access to scoped data should have a publicly-facing privacy notice, easily accessible to all users that includes mechanisms to authorize or acquire consent for the collection, use and disclosure of personal information.

Risk Statement: Absence of an online privacy notice limits users' awareness of how the organization collects, uses and discloses personal information creating the risk of customer dissatisfaction and may be a contractual or regulatory violation.

controls.name: P.7 - Management Of Client-Scoped Privacy Data
controls.title: Management Of Client-Scoped Privacy Data
controls.body:
Control: The organization has documented and maintained procedures for the management of client scoped data that addresses its legal, statutory, regulatory or contractual obligations.

Control Objective: An organization should ensure that it documents and maintains adequate data governance or data management procedures for the protection of client-scoped privacy data based on its' legal, statutory, regulatory and contractual obligations.

Risk Statement: The absence of documented privacy or data protection procedures may lead to a privacy breach vulnerability, risk of identity theft or unauthorized disclosure of personal information.

controls.name: P.8 - Privacy Incident Notification And Response Management
controls.title: Privacy Incident Notification And Response Management
controls.body:
Control: The organization has established a formal privacy incident communication, notification and incident handling procedure to be executed in the event of unauthorized disclosure or breach of scoped data

Control Objective: An organization should establish a formal privacy incident communication , notification, and incident handling procedure, integrated with the organizations' security incident response and escalation procedures, to be executed in the event of unauthorized disclosure or breach of scoped data.

Risk Statement: The absence of privacy incident notification procedures and a response management program may be a contractual or regulatory violation and lead to poor privacy practices including non-compliance with privacy laws or contractual obligations.

controls.name: V.3.10 - Requirements for masking of Guest virtual server passwords | Security Review of Hypervisor Configuration
controls.title: Requirements for masking of Guest virtual server passwords | Security Review of Hypervisor Configuration
controls.body: Attribute of V.3 Security Review of Hypervisor Configuration

controls.name: P.9 - Third Party Privacy Agreements
controls.title: Third Party Privacy Agreements
controls.body:
Control: The organization has defined standard Privacy contractual provisions and governance processes that define privacy and protection requirements between the organization and its third parties that collect, receive, access, transmit, process or retain scoped data.

Control Objective: An organization should define and maintain standard contractual provisions and governance processes to ensure scoped data is collected, accessed, transmitted, processed, disclosed or retained in accordance to its regulatory and contractual obligations and that privacy obligations are extended to fourth parties (e.g., subcontractors, vendors, sub-processors) who collect, receive, have access to, process or retain scoped data.

Risk Statement: The absence of privacy agreements and governance processes with third parties with whom data is shared may lead to a privacy violation; risk of identity theft; or unauthorized use, disclosure or breach of personal information; which can result in fines, enforcement penalties or risk of litigation.

controls.name: T.4 - Application Vulnerability Assessments/Ethical Hacking
controls.title: Application Vulnerability Assessments/Ethical Hacking
controls.body:
Control: An organization performs vulnerability assessments on internal and external network applications that process, store or transmit scoped data on a periodic basis, as well as when a change to any application has been made.

Control Objective: An organization should perform application penetration tests or ethical hacking of proprietary web-facing applications. Industry standards such as OWASP should be utilized as a foundation for detecting vulnerabilities in the applications and measuring the effectiveness of the application security controls in place.

Risk Statement: The absence of application penetration tests or ethical hacking of proprietary web-facing applications may result in undetected vulnerabilities and/or inappropriate vulnerability management.

controls.name: T.6.1 - Requirements for download and acceptance of mobile code | Mobile Code Security
controls.title: Requirements for download and acceptance of mobile code | Mobile Code Security
controls.body: Attribute of T.6 Mobile Code Security

controls.name: U.1 - Server Security Configuration Standards
controls.title: Server Security Configuration Standards
controls.body:
Control: An organization has secure system configuration and hardening standards based on external industry or vendor guidance.

Control Objective: An organization should define and maintain a formal, documented configuration standard for building and managing target systems, including hardening requirements in accordance with external industry or vendor guidance.

Risk Statement: The absence of formal documented configuration standard for building and managing target systems may result in systems that are misconfigured using vulnerable system settings increasing the risk of compromise.

controls.name: U.1.19 - Logs are retained for a minimum of one year | Server Security Configuration Standards
controls.title: Logs are retained for a minimum of one year | Server Security Configuration Standards
controls.body: Attribute of U.1 Server Security Configuration Standards

controls.name: V.2.6 - Identification of individuals responsible for ensuring the live Guest Operating Systems remained hardened | Cloud Audit Program
controls.title: Identification of individuals responsible for ensuring the live Guest Operating Systems remained hardened | Cloud Audit Program
controls.body: Attribute of V.2 Cloud Audit Program

controls.name: V.2.7 - Identification of individuals responsible for deploying patches to the live guest Operating Systems | Cloud Audit Program
controls.title: Identification of individuals responsible for deploying patches to the live guest Operating Systems | Cloud Audit Program
controls.body: Attribute of V.2 Cloud Audit Program

controls.name: V.2.8 - Audit roles and responsibilities | Cloud Audit Program
controls.title: Audit roles and responsibilities | Cloud Audit Program
controls.body: Attribute of V.2 Cloud Audit Program

controls.name: V.1 - Service and Deployment Models
controls.title: Service and Deployment Models
controls.body:
Control: The organization has formal documentation of its security policies, controls and security responsibilities based on the type of service and deployment models provided and that the documentation has been approved by management.

Control Objective: An organization hosting Cloud Services or a Cloud Service Provider (CSP), should have formalized security policies and controls in place protecting its service and deployment models that include the documentation of its security responsibilities.

Risk Statement: The absence of documented policies, controls, delivery models and lines of demarcation may lead to variances and obscurity in implementing cloud services.

controls.name: V.1.1 - Roles and responsibility for the CSP | Service and Deployment Models
controls.title: Roles and responsibility for the CSP | Service and Deployment Models
controls.body: Attribute of V.1 Service and Deployment Models

controls.name: V.1.10 - OS system images and software packages | Service and Deployment Models
controls.title: OS system images and software packages | Service and Deployment Models
controls.body: Attribute of V.1 Service and Deployment Models

controls.name: V.1.11 - Policy related to client's rights to run their own security services within their Cloud environment | Service and Deployment Models
controls.title: Policy related to client's rights to run their own security services within their Cloud environment | Service and Deployment Models
controls.body: Attribute of V.1 Service and Deployment Models

controls.name: V.1.12 - Process for patch management | Service and Deployment Models
controls.title: Process for patch management | Service and Deployment Models
controls.body: Attribute of V.1 Service and Deployment Models

controls.name: V.1.14 - Procedures that address responsibilities for multi-tenant | Service and Deployment Models
controls.title: Procedures that address responsibilities for multi-tenant | Service and Deployment Models
controls.body: Attribute of V.1 Service and Deployment Models

controls.name: V.1.15 - Development methodology - includes process for the release of applications developed into production | Service and Deployment Models
controls.title: Development methodology - includes process for the release of applications developed into production | Service and Deployment Models
controls.body: Attribute of V.1 Service and Deployment Models

controls.name: V.1.16 - Service and deployment models' maintenance frequency | Service and Deployment Models
controls.title: Service and deployment models' maintenance frequency | Service and Deployment Models
controls.body: Attribute of V.1 Service and Deployment Models

controls.name: V.1.17 - Security monitoring (includes what is being monitored, i.e., inbound/outbound traffic, Cloud platform, CSP staff) | Service and Deployment Models
controls.title: Security monitoring (includes what is being monitored, i.e., inbound/outbound traffic, Cloud platform, CSP staff) | Service and Deployment Models
controls.body: Attribute of V.1 Service and Deployment Models

controls.name: V.2.9 - Internal audit schedule | Cloud Audit Program
controls.title: Internal audit schedule | Cloud Audit Program
controls.body: Attribute of V.2 Cloud Audit Program

controls.name: V.2 - Cloud Audit Program
controls.title: Cloud Audit Program
controls.body:
Control: A formalized governance process and audit program has been implemented and approved by management.

Control Objective: An organization hosting Cloud Services or CSPs should develop and maintain governance processes and audit plans which focus on review and management of information security and that are reviewed annually by audit teams and management.

Risk Statement: The absence of a CSP governance and information security audit program may result in the organization's inability to identify ineffective practices and risks, including the selection or use of embedded service provider relationships.

controls.name: V.2.1 - Requirements to document the list of its third party service providers and the services they provide related to the CSP's services offered | Cloud Audit Program
controls.title: Requirements to document the list of its third party service providers and the services they provide related to the CSP's services offered | Cloud Audit Program
controls.body: Attribute of V.2 Cloud Audit Program

controls.name: V.2.11 - Dedicated internal security team assigned to protecting the cloud hosting infrastructure | Cloud Audit Program
controls.title: Dedicated internal security team assigned to protecting the cloud hosting infrastructure | Cloud Audit Program
controls.body: Attribute of V.2 Cloud Audit Program

controls.name: V.2.12 - API reviews are included in business continuity plans | Cloud Audit Program
controls.title: API reviews are included in business continuity plans | Cloud Audit Program
controls.body: Attribute of V.2 Cloud Audit Program

controls.name: V.2.13 - Audit was performed by a certified audit firm, free of qualified opinion | Cloud Audit Program
controls.title: Audit was performed by a certified audit firm, free of qualified opinion | Cloud Audit Program
controls.body: Attribute of V.2 Cloud Audit Program

controls.name: V.2.14 - Process for onsite assessments | Cloud Audit Program
controls.title: Process for onsite assessments | Cloud Audit Program
controls.body: Attribute of V.2 Cloud Audit Program

controls.name: V.2.15 - Policy on self-service | Cloud Audit Program
controls.title: Policy on self-service | Cloud Audit Program
controls.body: Attribute of V.2 Cloud Audit Program

controls.name: V.2.16 - Processes for clients to run vulnerability scans against their own cloud environments | Cloud Audit Program
controls.title: Processes for clients to run vulnerability scans against their own cloud environments | Cloud Audit Program
controls.body: Attribute of V.2 Cloud Audit Program

controls.name: V.2.17 - Ability for clients to procure their own network security services (e.g., Firewall, IDS, IPS, WAF) | Cloud Audit Program
controls.title: Ability for clients to procure their own network security services (e.g., Firewall, IDS, IPS, WAF) | Cloud Audit Program
controls.body: Attribute of V.2 Cloud Audit Program

controls.name: V.2.18 - Procedures to maintain inventory of third party service providers and the services they provide related to the CSP's services offered. | Cloud Audit Program
controls.title: Procedures to maintain inventory of third party service providers and the services they provide related to the CSP's services offered. | Cloud Audit Program
controls.body: Attribute of V.2 Cloud Audit Program

controls.name: V.2.2 - Certification was performed by a certified, independent third party | Cloud Audit Program
controls.title: Certification was performed by a certified, independent third party | Cloud Audit Program
controls.body: Attribute of V.2 Cloud Audit Program

controls.name: IA-9 - Service Identification and Authentication
controls.title: Service Identification and Authentication
controls.body: Uniquely identify and authenticate [Assignment: organization-defined system services and applications] before establishing communications with devices, users, or other services or applications.

controls.name: IR-4(10) - Incident Handling | Supply Chain Coordination
controls.title: Incident Handling | Supply Chain Coordination
controls.body: Coordinate incident handling activities involving supply chain events with other organizations involved in the supply chain.

controls.name: CM-8(3) - System Component Inventory | Automated Unauthorized Component Detection
controls.title: System Component Inventory | Automated Unauthorized Component Detection
controls.body:
a. Detect the presence of unauthorized hardware, software, and firmware components within the system using [Assignment: organization-defined automated mechanisms]
                     [Assignment: organization-defined frequency]; and
b. Take the following actions when unauthorized components are detected: [Selection (one or more): disable network access by such components; isolate the components; notify [Assignment: organization-defined personnel or roles]].

controls.name: IR-9(2) - Information Spillage Response | Training
controls.title: Information Spillage Response | Training
controls.body: Provide information spillage response training [Assignment: organization-defined frequency].

controls.name: GC - Right of Data Portability
controls.title: Right of Data Portability
controls.body: Access requests from data subjects for transmission of their personal information to another controller in a structured format are documented, retained, and acted upon without undue days.

controls.name: AC-7(2) - Unsuccessful Logon Attempts | Purge or Wipe Mobile Device
controls.title: Unsuccessful Logon Attempts | Purge or Wipe Mobile Device
controls.body: Purge or wipe information from [Assignment: organization-defined mobile devices] based on [Assignment: organization-defined purging or wiping requirements and techniques] after [Assignment: organization-defined number] consecutive, unsuccessful device logon attempts.

controls.name: AC-24(1) - Access Control Decisions | Transmit Access Authorization Information
controls.title: Access Control Decisions | Transmit Access Authorization Information
controls.body: Transmit [Assignment: organization-defined access authorization information] using [Assignment: organization-defined controls] to [Assignment: organization-defined systems] that enforce access control decisions.

controls.name: AC-20(3) - Use of External Systems | Non-organizationally Owned Systems — Restricted Use
controls.title: Use of External Systems | Non-organizationally Owned Systems — Restricted Use
controls.body: Restrict the use of non-organizationally owned systems or system components to process, store, or transmit organizational information using [Assignment: organization-defined restrictions].

controls.name: PE-15 - Water Damage Protection
controls.title: Water Damage Protection
controls.body: Protect the system from damage resulting from water leakage by providing master shutoff or isolation valves that are accessible, working properly, and known to key personnel.

controls.name: AC-21 - Information Sharing
controls.title: Information Sharing
controls.body:
a. Enable authorized users to determine whether access authorizations assigned to a sharing partner match the information’s access and use restrictions for [Assignment: organization-defined information sharing circumstances where user discretion is required]; and
b. Employ [Assignment: organization-defined automated mechanisms or manual processes] to assist users in making information sharing and collaboration decisions.

controls.name: AC-19(5) - Access Control for Mobile Devices | Full Device or Container-based Encryption
controls.title: Access Control for Mobile Devices | Full Device or Container-based Encryption
controls.body: Employ [Selection: full-device encryption; container-based encryption] to protect the confidentiality and integrity of information on [Assignment: organization-defined mobile devices].

controls.name: PE-9(1) - Power Equipment and Cabling | Redundant Cabling
controls.title: Power Equipment and Cabling | Redundant Cabling
controls.body: Employ redundant power cabling paths that are physically separated by [Assignment: organization-defined distance].

controls.name: PE-9(2) - Power Equipment and Cabling | Automatic Voltage Controls
controls.title: Power Equipment and Cabling | Automatic Voltage Controls
controls.body: Employ automatic voltage controls for [Assignment: organization-defined critical system components].

controls.name: IR-4(15) - Incident Handling | Public Relations and Reputation Repair
controls.title: Incident Handling | Public Relations and Reputation Repair
controls.body:
a. Manage public relations associated with an incident; and
b. Employ measures to repair the reputation of the organization.

controls.name: AC-22 - Publicly Accessible Content
controls.title: Publicly Accessible Content

controls.name: MP-6(2) - Media Sanitization | Equipment Testing
controls.title: Media Sanitization | Equipment Testing
controls.body: Test sanitization equipment and procedures [Assignment: organization-defined frequency] to ensure that the intended sanitization is being achieved.

controls.name: AC-23 - Data Mining Protection
controls.title: Data Mining Protection
controls.body: Employ [Assignment: organization-defined data mining prevention and detection techniques] for [Assignment: organization-defined data storage objects] to detect and protect against unauthorized data mining.

controls.name: PL-8(2) - Security and Privacy Architectures | Supplier Diversity
controls.title: Security and Privacy Architectures | Supplier Diversity
controls.body: Require that [Assignment: organization-defined controls] allocated to [Assignment: organization-defined locations and architectural layers] are obtained from different suppliers.

controls.name: AC-24(2) - Access Control Decisions | No User or Process Identity
controls.title: Access Control Decisions | No User or Process Identity
controls.body: Enforce access control decisions based on [Assignment: organization-defined security or privacy attributes] that do not include the identity of the user or process acting on behalf of the user.

controls.name: PM-7(1) - Enterprise Architecture | Offloading
controls.title: Enterprise Architecture | Offloading
controls.body: Offload [Assignment: organization-defined non-essential functions or services] to other systems, system components, or an external provider.

controls.name: PM-11 - Mission and Business Process Definition
controls.title: Mission and Business Process Definition
controls.body:
a. Define organizational mission and business processes with consideration for information security and privacy and the resulting risk to organizational operations, organizational assets, individuals, other organizations, and the Nation; and
b. Determine information protection and personally identifiable information processing needs arising from the defined mission and business processes; and
c. Review and revise the mission and business processes [Assignment: organization-defined frequency].

controls.name: PM-8 - Critical Infrastructure Plan
controls.title: Critical Infrastructure Plan
controls.body: Address information security and privacy issues in the development, documentation, and updating of a critical infrastructure and key resources protection plan.

controls.name: PM-19 - Privacy Program Leadership Role
controls.title: Privacy Program Leadership Role
controls.body: Appoint a senior agency official for privacy with the authority, mission, accountability, and resources to coordinate, develop, and implement, applicable privacy requirements and manage privacy risks through the organization-wide privacy program.

controls.name: PM-10 - Authorization Process
controls.title: Authorization Process

controls.name: RA-5(2) - Vulnerability Monitoring and Scanning | Update Vulnerabilities to Be Scanned
controls.title: Vulnerability Monitoring and Scanning | Update Vulnerabilities to Be Scanned
controls.body: Update the system vulnerabilities to be scanned [Selection (one or more): [Assignment: organization-defined frequency]; prior to a new scan; when new vulnerabilities are identified and reported].

controls.name: PM-16 - Threat Awareness Program
controls.title: Threat Awareness Program
controls.body: Implement a threat awareness program that includes a cross-organization information-sharing capability for threat intelligence.

controls.name: IR-2 - Incident Response Training
controls.title: Incident Response Training
controls.body:
a. Provide incident response training to system users consistent with assigned roles and responsibilities:
1. Within [Assignment: organization-defined time period] of assuming an incident response role or responsibility or acquiring system access;
2. When required by system changes; and
3. [Assignment: organization-defined frequency] thereafter; and

b. Review and update incident response training content [Assignment: organization-defined frequency] and following [Assignment: organization-defined events].

controls.name: PM-15 - Security and Privacy Groups and Associations
controls.title: Security and Privacy Groups and Associations
controls.body:
Establish and institutionalize contact with selected groups and associations within the security and privacy communities:

a. To facilitate ongoing security and privacy education and training for organizational personnel;
b. To maintain currency with recommended security and privacy practices, techniques, and technologies; and
c. To share current security and privacy information, including threats, vulnerabilities, and incidents.

controls.name: AU-10(4) - Non-repudiation | Validate Binding of Information Reviewer Identity
controls.title: Non-repudiation | Validate Binding of Information Reviewer Identity
controls.body:
a. Validate the binding of the information reviewer identity to the information at the transfer or release points prior to release or transfer between [Assignment: organization-defined security domains]; and
b. Perform [Assignment: organization-defined actions] in the event of a validation error.

controls.name: PT-2(1) - Authority to Process Personally Identifiable Information | Data Tagging
controls.title: Authority to Process Personally Identifiable Information | Data Tagging
controls.body: Attach data tags containing [Assignment: organization-defined authorized processing] to [Assignment: organization-defined elements of personally identifiable information].

controls.name: PM-23 - Data Governance Body
controls.title: Data Governance Body
controls.body: Establish a Data Governance Body consisting of [Assignment: organization-defined roles] with [Assignment: organization-defined responsibilities].

controls.name: PM-26 - Complaint Management
controls.title: Complaint Management

controls.name: D3.DC.Ev.Inn.1 - Development of Event Detection Systems
controls.title: Development of Event Detection Systems
controls.body: The institution is leading efforts to develop event detection systems that will correlate in real time when events are about to occur.

controls.name: PS-3(2) - Personnel Screening | Formal Indoctrination
controls.title: Personnel Screening | Formal Indoctrination
controls.body: Verify that individuals accessing a system processing, storing, or transmitting types of classified information that require formal indoctrination, are formally indoctrinated for all the relevant types of information to which they have access on the system.

controls.name: PM-24 - Data Integrity Board
controls.title: Data Integrity Board
controls.body:
Establish a Data Integrity Board to:

a. Review proposals to conduct or participate in a matching program; and
b. Conduct an annual review of all matching programs in which the agency has participated.

controls.name: PS-3(4) - Personnel Screening | Citizenship Requirements
controls.title: Personnel Screening | Citizenship Requirements
controls.body: Verify that individuals accessing a system processing, storing, or transmitting [Assignment: organization-defined information types] meet [Assignment: organization-defined citizenship requirements].

controls.name: PS-4(2) - Personnel Termination | Automated Actions
controls.title: Personnel Termination | Automated Actions
controls.body: Use [Assignment: organization-defined automated mechanisms] to [Selection (one or more): notify [Assignment: organization-defined personnel or roles] of individual termination actions; disable access to system resources].

controls.name: D3.CC.Re.Inn.1 - Development of Remediation Technology for Zero-Day Attacks
controls.title: Development of Remediation Technology for Zero-Day Attacks
controls.body: The institution is developing technologies that will remediate systems damaged by zero-day attacks to maintain current recovery time objectives.

controls.name: SI-3 - Malicious Code Protection
controls.title: Malicious Code Protection

controls.name: D5.ER.Es.B.4 - Incident Management
controls.title: Incident Management
controls.body: Incidents are classified, logged, and tracked. (FFIEC Operations Booklet, page 28)

controls.name: PS-3(1) - Personnel Screening | Classified Information
controls.title: Personnel Screening | Classified Information
controls.body: Verify that individuals accessing a system processing, storing, or transmitting classified information are cleared and indoctrinated to the highest classification level of the information to which they have access on the system.

controls.name: IR-8(1) - Incident Response Plan | Breaches
controls.title: Incident Response Plan | Breaches
controls.body:
Include the following in the Incident Response Plan for breaches involving personally identifiable information:

a. A process to determine if notice to individuals or other organizations, including oversight organizations, is needed;
b. An assessment process to determine the extent of the harm, embarrassment, inconvenience, or unfairness to affected individuals and any mechanisms to mitigate such harms; and
c. Identification of applicable privacy requirements.

controls.name: PS-5 - Personnel Transfer
controls.title: Personnel Transfer

controls.name: PS-6 - Access Agreements
controls.title: Access Agreements
controls.body:
a. Develop and document access agreements for organizational systems;
b. Review and update the access agreements [Assignment: organization-defined frequency]; and
c. Verify that individuals requiring access to organizational information and systems:

1. Sign appropriate access agreements prior to being granted access; and
2. Re-sign access agreements to maintain access to organizational systems when access agreements have been updated or [Assignment: organization-defined frequency].

controls.name: PS-8 - Personnel Sanctions
controls.title: Personnel Sanctions
controls.body:
a. Employ a formal sanctions process for individuals failing to comply with established information security and privacy policies and procedures; and
b. Notify [Assignment: organization-defined personnel or roles] within [Assignment: organization-defined time period] when a formal employee sanctions process is initiated, identifying the individual sanctioned and the reason for the sanction.

controls.name: D3.DC.Th.E.3 - Updating of Antivirus and Anti-Malware Tools
controls.title: Updating of Antivirus and Anti-Malware Tools
controls.body: Antivirus and anti-malware tools are updated automatically.

controls.name: PT-2(2) - Authority to Process Personally Identifiable Information | Automation
controls.title: Authority to Process Personally Identifiable Information | Automation
controls.body: Manage enforcement of the authorized processing of personally identifiable information using [Assignment: organization-defined automated mechanisms].

controls.name: AU-16 - Cross-organizational Audit Logging
controls.title: Cross-organizational Audit Logging
controls.body: Employ [Assignment: organization-defined methods] for coordinating [Assignment: organization-defined audit information] among external organizations when audit information is transmitted across organizational boundaries.

controls.name: PT-4(1) - Consent | Tailored Consent
controls.title: Consent | Tailored Consent
controls.body: Provide [Assignment: organization-defined mechanisms] to allow individuals to tailor processing permissions to selected elements of personally identifiable information.

controls.name: MA-3(3) - Maintenance Tools | Prevent Unauthorized Removal
controls.title: Maintenance Tools | Prevent Unauthorized Removal

controls.name: AU-14 - Session Audit
controls.title: Session Audit
controls.body:
a. Provide and implement the capability for [Assignment: organization-defined users or roles] to [Selection (one or more): record; view; hear; log] the content of a user session under [Assignment: organization-defined circumstances]; and
b. Develop, integrate, and use session auditing activities in consultation with legal counsel and in accordance with applicable laws, executive orders, directives, regulations, policies, standards, and guidelines.

controls.name: CIS 2.4-DE - Software Inventory Tools
controls.title: Software Inventory Tools
controls.body:
Inventory and Control of Software Assets
Safeguard 2.4: Utilize automated software inventory tools.

controls.name: PT-5(2) - Privacy Notice | Privacy Act Statements
controls.title: Privacy Notice | Privacy Act Statements
controls.body: Include Privacy Act statements on forms that collect information that will be maintained in a Privacy Act system of records, or provide Privacy Act statements on separate forms that can be retained by individuals.

controls.name: PT-6(2) - System of Records Notice | Exemption Rules
controls.title: System of Records Notice | Exemption Rules
controls.body: Review all Privacy Act exemptions claimed for the system of records at [Assignment: organization-defined frequency] to ensure they remain appropriate and necessary in accordance with law, that they have been promulgated as regulations, and that they are accurately described in the system of records notice.

controls.name: PT-7 - Specific Categories of Personally Identifiable Information
controls.title: Specific Categories of Personally Identifiable Information
controls.body: Apply [Assignment: organization-defined processing conditions] for specific categories of personally identifiable information.

controls.name: D3.DC.Th.E.6 - Monitoring of Insider Activity
controls.title: Monitoring of Insider Activity
controls.body: Processes are in place to monitor potential insider activity that could lead to data theft or destruction.

controls.name: PT-6(1) - System of Records Notice | Routine Uses
controls.title: System of Records Notice | Routine Uses
controls.body: Review all routine uses published in the system of records notice at [Assignment: organization-defined frequency] to ensure continued accuracy, and to ensure that routine uses continue to be compatible with the purpose for which the information was collected.

controls.name: RA-5(11) - Vulnerability Monitoring and Scanning | Public Disclosure Program
controls.title: Vulnerability Monitoring and Scanning | Public Disclosure Program
controls.body: Establish a public reporting channel for receiving reports of vulnerabilities in organizational systems and system components.

controls.name: RA-2 - Security Categorization
controls.title: Security Categorization

controls.name: D3.DC.Th.Int.2 - Email Malware Scanning
controls.title: Email Malware Scanning
controls.body: E-mails and attachments are automatically scanned to detect malware and are blocked when malware is present.

controls.name: RA-3(3) - Risk Assessment | Dynamic Threat Awareness
controls.title: Risk Assessment | Dynamic Threat Awareness
controls.body: Determine the current cyber threat environment on an ongoing basis using [Assignment: organization-defined means].

controls.name: D3.DC.An.E.4 - Log Activity Response Threshold
controls.title: Log Activity Response Threshold
controls.body: Thresholds have been established to determine activity within logs that would warrant management response.

controls.name: RA-5(4) - Vulnerability Monitoring and Scanning | Discoverable Information
controls.title: Vulnerability Monitoring and Scanning | Discoverable Information
controls.body: Determine information about the system that is discoverable and take [Assignment: organization-defined corrective actions].

controls.name: RA-5(5) - Vulnerability Monitoring and Scanning | Privileged Access
controls.title: Vulnerability Monitoring and Scanning | Privileged Access
controls.body: Implement privileged access authorization to [Assignment: organization-defined system components] for [Assignment: organization-defined vulnerability scanning activities].

controls.name: RA-5(8) - Vulnerability Monitoring and Scanning | Review Historic Audit Logs
controls.title: Vulnerability Monitoring and Scanning | Review Historic Audit Logs
controls.body: Review historic audit logs to determine if a vulnerability identified in a [Assignment: organization-defined system] has been previously exploited within an [Assignment: organization-defined time period].

controls.name: SA-3(2) - System Development Life Cycle | Use of Live or Operational Data
controls.title: System Development Life Cycle | Use of Live or Operational Data
controls.body:
a. Approve, document, and control the use of live data in preproduction environments for the system, system component, or system service; and
b. Protect preproduction environments for the system, system component, or system service at the same impact or classification level as any live data in use within the preproduction environments.

controls.name: SA-3(1) - System Development Life Cycle | Manage Preproduction Environment
controls.title: System Development Life Cycle | Manage Preproduction Environment
controls.body: Protect system preproduction environments commensurate with risk throughout the system development life cycle for the system, system component, or system service.

controls.name: D3.DC.An.Int.5 - Security Log Thresholds
controls.title: Security Log Thresholds
controls.body: Thresholds for security logging are evaluated periodically.
