controls.body: Change default or guessable account passwords (for both admin and non-admin accounts) and disable/remove all unnecessary accounts on all devices managed by the organization.

controls.name: CE.006 - Boundary Firewall
controls.title: Boundary Firewall
controls.body: Implement boundary firewall(s) and internet gateways to protect all devices that are in scope for the assessment.

controls.name: CE.017 - Software Inventory
controls.title: Software Inventory
controls.body:
Maintain an inventory of all software used by the organizations along with version, licensing status, and whether it is supported or unsupported. This should include the following:
 - Operating systems, firmware and application  
 - Internet browsers
 - Malware protection systems
 - Email applications
 - Office applications

controls.name: CE.018 - Auto-Update Configuration
controls.title: Auto-Update Configuration
controls.body: Apply updates that fix critical and high-risk vulnerabilities on organizational systems (including operating systems, firmware and applications) within 14 days of an update being released.

controls.name: CLD.8.1.5 - Removal of Cloud Service Customer Assets
controls.title: Removal of Cloud Service Customer Assets
controls.body: Assets of the cloud service customer that are on the cloud service provider's premises shall be removed, and returned if necessary, in a timely manner upon termination of the cloud service agreement.

controls.name: C.13.1.1 - Supervisory Authority Information
controls.title: Supervisory Authority Information
controls.body: A) Where required by national law, the Applicant shall demonstrate it has informed, and where required obtained prior authorization from, its National Supervisory Authority to deliver the financial and/or insurance services in the Target of Evaluation.

controls.name: CLD.12.4.5 - Monitoring of Cloud Services
controls.title: Monitoring of Cloud Services
controls.body: The cloud service customer shall have the capability to monitor specified aspects of the operation of the cloud services that the cloud service customer uses.

controls.name: 8.31 - Separation of Development, Test and Production Environments (27018)
controls.title: Separation of Development, Test and Production Environments (27018)
controls.body: Development, testing and production environments shall be separated and secured.

controls.name: 8.24 - Use of Cryptography (27018)
controls.title: Use of Cryptography (27018)
controls.body: Rules for the effective use of cryptography, including cryptographic key management, shall be defined and implemented.

controls.name: A.2.1 - Co-operating to Fulfill Obligations to PII Principals
controls.title: Co-operating to Fulfill Obligations to PII Principals
controls.body: The public cloud PII processor should provide the cloud service customer with the means to enable them to fulfill their obligation to facilitate the exercise of PII principals’ rights to access, correct and/or erase PII pertaining to them.

controls.name: C.7.1.1 - Data Protection Impact Assessment
controls.title: Data Protection Impact Assessment
controls.body: A) The Applicant shall have performed a Data Protection Impact Assessment.

controls.name: 2.13 - Notice for Sensitive Processing
controls.title: Notice for Sensitive Processing
controls.body: Clear notice is provided to consumers prior to the processing of their sensitive personal information. Consumers are provided with a mechanism to exercise their right to opt-out of the processing, and any such requests are documented and retained in accordance with organizational policies.

controls.name: A.3.2 - Public Cloud PII Processor's Commercial Use
controls.title: Public Cloud PII Processor's Commercial Use
controls.body: PII processed under a contract should not be used by the public cloud PII processor for the purposes of marketing and advertising without express consent. Such consent should not be a condition of receiving the service.

controls.name: A.11.1 - Confidentiality or Non-disclosure Agreements
controls.title: Confidentiality or Non-disclosure Agreements
controls.body: Individuals under the public cloud PII processor’s control with access to PII should be subject to a confidentiality obligation.

controls.name: A.6.1 - PII Disclosure Notification
controls.title: PII Disclosure Notification
controls.body: The contract between the public cloud PII processor and the cloud service customer should require the public cloud PII processor to notify the cloud service customer, in accordance with any procedure and time periods agreed in the contract, of any legally binding request for disclosure of PII by a law enforcement authority, unless such a disclosure is otherwise prohibited.

controls.name: CE.024 - Monitor Admin Accounts
controls.title: Monitor Admin Accounts
controls.body:
Implement mechanisms to:
 - Monitor activities of users with admin accounts.
 - Periodically review admin accounts.

controls.name: TISAX 5.3.3 - Return and Secure Removal of Information Assets
controls.title: Return and Secure Removal of Information Assets
controls.body: Information assets in the possession of employees and contractors are returned upon termination of their employment or contract or securely removed upon termination of service.

controls.name: CIP-009.R1-1.1 - Recovery Plan and Policy
controls.title: Recovery Plan and Policy
controls.body: Each responsible entity shall develop one or more documented recovery plan(s) that include conditions for activation of the recovery plan(s).

controls.name: C.11.1.1 - Complementary Risk Assessment
controls.title: Complementary Risk Assessment

controls.name: CE.030 - Approved Software
controls.title: Approved Software
controls.body: Restrict installations of applications that have not been approved and documented by the organization.

controls.name: CE.029 - Malware Update/Scan Configuration
controls.title: Malware Update/Scan Configuration
controls.body: Configure anti malware software to update at least daily or as per vendor recommendations, scan files (including files on external media when inserted) and websites automatically upon access and take corrective action when an infection is detected or a malicious website is accessed.

controls.name: 5.36 - Compliance with Information Security Policies, Rules and Standards
controls.title: Compliance with Information Security Policies, Rules and Standards
controls.body: Compliance with the organization’s information security policy, topic-specific policies, rules and standards shall be regularly reviewed.

controls.name: CE.031 - Sandboxing Infected Applications
controls.title: Sandboxing Infected Applications
controls.body: Implement sandboxing mechanisms to segregate and seal off applications that are suspected or known to have been compromised or applications with known critical security vulnerabilities so that they are unable to access data stores, sensitive peripherals and internal networks.

controls.name: MAP 3.2 - AI Error Costs and Organizational Risk Tolerance
controls.title: AI Error Costs and Organizational Risk Tolerance
controls.body: Potential costs, including non-monetary costs, which result from expected or realized AI errors or system functionality and trustworthiness – as connected to organizational risk tolerance – are examined and documented.

controls.name: G.3.3.1 - Duty to Inform
controls.title: Duty to Inform

controls.name: T.1.1.1 - Access Rights Minimization (Least Privilege)
controls.title: Access Rights Minimization (Least Privilege)
controls.body: A) Access rights shall be limited and delivered on a need basis in conformity with the "Least privilege" principle.

controls.name: T.1.1.6 - Automated Session Logout
controls.title: Automated Session Logout
controls.body: A) The access to the stored personal data shall be protected by an automated session log out mechanism.

controls.name: 1.1 - Privacy Notice
controls.title: Privacy Notice
controls.body: The organization has a privacy notice published on its website, which outlines privacy obligations and specifies individual rights in accordance with applicable laws and regulations. The notice is reviewed by management on an annual basis.

controls.name: 2.7 - Notice of Targeted Advertising, Profiling, Sale or Sharing of Personal Information
controls.title: Notice of Targeted Advertising, Profiling, Sale or Sharing of Personal Information
controls.body: Explicit notice is provided to consumers prior to processing personal data for targeted advertising, profiling or the sale or sharing of their personal information. Consumers are provided with a mechanism to exercise the right to opt out of the targeted advertising, sale or sharing of their personal information, and any such requests are handled in a timely manner.

controls.name: 2.3 - Right to Access/Know
controls.title: Right to Access/Know
controls.body: Requests from consumers to access/know about their personal information are documented, retained, and acted upon within 45 days from the receipt of the request. Any delay or denial on request is communicated to consumers and handled in accordance with applicable privacy regulations.

controls.name: 2.5 - Right to Opt-out of Targeted Advertising, Profiling, Sale or Sharing of Personal Information
controls.title: Right to Opt-out of Targeted Advertising, Profiling, Sale or Sharing of Personal Information
controls.body: Requests from consumers to opt out of the targeted advertising, profiling, sale or sharing of their personal information are documented, retained, and acted upon within state-specific timelines. Any delay or denial on request is communicated to consumers and handled in accordance with applicable privacy regulations.

controls.name: PCI 12.10.6 - Incorporate Lessons Learned from Security Incidents
controls.title: Incorporate Lessons Learned from Security Incidents
controls.body: The security incident response plan is modified and evolved according to lessons learned and to incorporate industry developments.

controls.name: 6.2 - Security Procedures and Practices
controls.title: Security Procedures and Practices
controls.body: Reasonable security procedures and practices have been implemented by the organization for the security and protection of consumers' personal information. These measures are assessed by management on an annual basis, and deficiencies identified are remediated in a timely manner.

controls.name: G.8.2.1 - DPIA Process Requirements
controls.title: DPIA Process Requirements

controls.name: G.8.2.3 - Data Subjects Involvement Requirement
controls.title: Data Subjects Involvement Requirement
controls.body: A) The Applicant shall keep records of the views of data subject and/or representatives consulted for the impact assessment (or documented justification for not involving data subjects or their representatives).

controls.name: G.10.1.3 - Cross-border Transfer Based on Appropriate Safeguards
controls.title: Cross-border Transfer Based on Appropriate Safeguards
controls.body:
IF personal data transfers to third countries or to international organisations are based on appropriate safeguards, THEN:
A) The Controller or Processor in the third country shall:
    a.1) regularly audit the security of its infrastructure that processes and/or stores the data of the Target of Evaluation;
    a.2) (AND) the last audit report shall have been reviewed by the DPO of the Applicant and assessed as satisfactory.
AND
B) The Controller or Processor in the third country shall have a procedure in place to enable the data subjects to enforce their rights and to access effective legal remedies from the controller or processor located in the third country.
AND
C) The Applicant shall provide information to the data subject on how they can exercise their rights with regards to the processing of their data in the third countries involved in the processing.
AND
D) The DPO of the Controller shall have assessed and confirmed that the data subjects can effectively exercise their rights and access legal remedies.

controls.name: G.10.2.1 - Complementary Requirements for Appropriate Safeguards
controls.title: Complementary Requirements for Appropriate Safeguards
controls.body:
The Applicant shall demonstrate that the data transfer benefits from appropriate safeguard through at least one of the following mechanisms:
A) The data transfer has adequate safeguards thanks to a **legally binding and enforceable instrument between public authorities or bodies.**
*OR*
B) The data transfer has adequate safeguards thanks to **binding corporate rules** that have been approved by the Supervisory Authority.
*OR*
C) The data transfer has adequate safeguards thanks to **standard data protection clauses** signed together by the data importer and exporter. 
*OR*
D) The data transfer has adequate safeguards thanks to **an approved code of conduct** with binding and enforceable commitment to apply appropriate safeguards. 
*OR*
E) The data transfer has adequate safeguards thanks to a **certification** mechanism, where:
    e.1) the certification mechanism is approved by the data protection authority;
    e.2) (AND) the Controller or Processor in the third country is bound by and enforceable commitment to apply the appropriate safeguards to the data processing, including as regards data subjects' rights.
*OR*
F) The data transfer is **authorized by the Supervisory Authority** on the basis of approved contractual clauses with the Controller or Processor.
*OR*
G) The data transfer is **authorized by the Supervisory Authority** on the basis of an administrative arrangement between public authorities or bodies which shall include:
    g.1) the provisions approved by the Supervisory Authorities;
    g.2) (AND) provisions to ensure enforceable and effective data subject rights.

controls.name: PCI 8.2.2 - Group, Shared, or Generic Accounts
controls.title: Group, Shared, or Generic Accounts
controls.body:
Group, shared, or generic accounts, or other shared authentication credentials are only used when necessary on an exception basis, and are managed as follows:
- Account use is prevented unless needed for an exceptional circumstance.
- Use is limited to the time needed for the exceptional circumstance.
- Business justification for use is documented.
- Use is explicitly approved by management.
- Individual user identity is confirmed before access to an account is granted.
- Every action taken is attributable to an individual user.

controls.name: CE.001 - Asset Inventory
controls.title: Asset Inventory
controls.body:
Maintain an inventory of IT assets, including quantities for the following:
- Laptops, desktops and virtual desktops along with model and operating system version as well as edition and feature version in case of Windows devices.
- Thin Client along with make, model and operating systems.
- Tablets and Mobile Devices along with model and operating system version.
- All other devices connected to the cloud services.

controls.name: G.8.2.2 - DPIA Content Requirements
controls.title: DPIA Content Requirements

controls.name: G.10.1.5 - Complementary Risk Assessment of Data Transfer to Third-countries Without Adequacy Decision
controls.title: Complementary Risk Assessment of Data Transfer to Third-countries Without Adequacy Decision

controls.name: CE.009 - Password Policy
controls.title: Password Policy
controls.body: Develop and implement a documented password policy that addresses the security of passwords and handling of any suspected or known password compromises.

controls.name: MAP 1.4 - Defining or Re-evaluating Business Value of AI Systems
controls.title: Defining or Re-evaluating Business Value of AI Systems
controls.body: The business value or context of business use has been clearly defined or – in the case of assessing existing AI systems – re-evaluated.

controls.name: A.11.12 - Sub-contracted PII Processing
controls.title: Sub-contracted PII Processing
controls.body: Contracts between the public cloud PII processor and any sub-contractors that process PII should specify minimum technical and organizational measures that meet the information security and PII protection obligations of the public cloud PII processor. Such measures should not be subject to unilateral reduction by the sub-contractor.

controls.name: 2.8 - Right to Data-Portability
controls.title: Right to Data-Portability
controls.body: Procedures and mechanisms are in place to provide consumers with a copy of their personal data in a portable and, to the extent technically feasible, readily usable format that allows the consumer to transmit the data to another controller.

controls.name: 2.6 - Right to Opt-in (Minors)
controls.title: Right to Opt-in (Minors)
controls.body: The sale or sharing of minor consumers' personal information is only performed based on affirmative authorization (“opt-in”) and by providing a mechanism to modify or withdraw the consent. Such authorizations are documented and retained in accordance with organization policies.

controls.name: C.14.1.5 - Tracking via in-vehicle WiFi Technology
controls.title: Tracking via in-vehicle WiFi Technology
controls.body:
IF the vehicle contains Wi-Fi connectivity THEN:
A) The driver shall have the possibility:
    a.1) to prevent the WiFi system of the vehicle to connect to external access points;
    a.2) (AND) to deactivate the collection and storage of IP and MAC addresses of passengers.

controls.name: G.10.1.1 - Cross border Transfer to Third Countries Validation
controls.title: Cross border Transfer to Third Countries Validation
controls.body:
A) The Applicant shall have a clear mapping or record of all personal data transfers to third countries and to international organizations by the Target of Evaluation.
*AND*
B) The transfer of personal data shall have been assessed as lawful by the DPO or by a legal expert with adequate expertise by taking into account:
    b.1)  the risks for the freedoms and rights of the data subjects;
    b.2) (AND) the safeguards and measures set in place to protect the transferred data.

controls.name: C.6.1.4 - IoT Devices Information
controls.title: IoT Devices Information

controls.name: C.11.1.2 - Complementary Informed Consent
controls.title: Complementary Informed Consent

controls.name: GOVERN 5.1 - Organizational Policies for AI Feedback Integration
controls.title: Organizational Policies for AI Feedback Integration
controls.body: Organizational policies and practices are in place to collect, consider, prioritize, and integrate feedback from those external to the team that developed or deployed the AI system regarding the potential individual and societal impacts related to AI risks.

controls.name: GOVERN 6.1 - AI Third-Party Risk Policies and Procedures
controls.title: AI Third-Party Risk Policies and Procedures
controls.body: Policies and procedures are in place that address AI risks associated with third-party entities, including risks of infringement of a third-party’s intellectual property or other rights.

controls.name: GOVERN 6.2 - Contingency Plan for High-Risk Third-Party Data & AI System Failures
controls.title: Contingency Plan for High-Risk Third-Party Data & AI System Failures
controls.body: Contingency processes are in place to handle failures or incidents in third-party data or AI systems deemed to be high-risk.

controls.name: MAP 1.1 - Documentation of Understanding and Considerations for AI Deployment
controls.title: Documentation of Understanding and Considerations for AI Deployment
controls.body: Intended purposes, potentially beneficial uses, contextspecific laws, norms and expectations, and prospective settings in which the AI system will be deployed are understood and documented. Considerations include: the specific set or types of users along with their expectations; potential positive and negative impacts of system uses to individuals, communities, organizations, society, and the planet; assumptions and related limitations about AI system purposes, uses, and risks across the development or product AI lifecycle; and related TEVV and system metrics.

controls.name: MAP 1.2 - Interdisciplinary AI: Diversity, Expertise, and Collaboration
controls.title: Interdisciplinary AI: Diversity, Expertise, and Collaboration
controls.body: Interdisciplinary AI actors, competencies, skills, and capacities for establishing context reflect demographic diversity and broad domain and user experience expertise, and their participation is documented. Opportunities for interdisciplinary collaboration are prioritized.

controls.name: MAP 5.1 - Identifying Impacts of AI Systems
controls.title: Identifying Impacts of AI Systems
controls.body: Likelihood and magnitude of each identified impact (both potentially beneficial and harmful) based on expected use, past uses of AI systems in similar contexts, public incident reports, feedback from those external to the team that developed or deployed the AI system, or other data are identified and documented.

controls.name: MAP 1.3 - Mission and Goals for AI Technology Documented
controls.title: Mission and Goals for AI Technology Documented
controls.body: The organization’s mission and relevant goals for AI technology are understood and documented.

controls.name: MAP 1.6 - AI Risk Mitigation through Socio-Technical Design Decisions and System Requirements
controls.title: AI Risk Mitigation through Socio-Technical Design Decisions and System Requirements
controls.body: System requirements (e.g., “the system shall respect the privacy of its users”) are elicited from and understood by relevant AI actors. Design decisions take socio-technical implications into account to address AI risks.

controls.name: MAP 2 - AI System Categorization
controls.title: AI System Categorization
controls.body: Categorization of the AI system is performed.

controls.name: MAP 2.1 - Defining AI System Tasks and Methods
controls.title: Defining AI System Tasks and Methods
controls.body: The specific tasks and methods used to implement the tasks that the AI system will support are defined (e.g., classifiers, generative models, recommenders).

controls.name: MEASURE 1.2 - AI Metrics and Controls Regularly Assessed and Updated
controls.title: AI Metrics and Controls Regularly Assessed and Updated
controls.body: Appropriateness of AI metrics and effectiveness of existing controls are regularly assessed and updated, including

controls.name: MEASURE 2.1 - Documentation of TEVV Tools and Metrics
controls.title: Documentation of TEVV Tools and Metrics
controls.body: Test sets, metrics, and details about the tools used during TEVV are documented.

controls.name: MAP 2.3 - Scientific Integrity and TEVV Considerations in Experimental Design and Data Collection
controls.title: Scientific Integrity and TEVV Considerations in Experimental Design and Data Collection
controls.body: Scientific integrity and TEVV considerations are identified and documented, including those related to experimental design, data collection and selection (e.g., availability, representativeness, suitability), system trustworthiness, and construct validation.

controls.name: MAP 3 - Understanding AI Capabilities and Targeted Usage: Goals, Benefits, and Costs Compared to Benchmarks
controls.title: Understanding AI Capabilities and Targeted Usage: Goals, Benefits, and Costs Compared to Benchmarks
controls.body: AI capabilities, targeted usage, goals, and expected benefits and costs compared with appropriate benchmarks are understood.

controls.name: MAP 3.1 - Examining Potential Benefits of AI System Functionality and Performance
controls.title: Examining Potential Benefits of AI System Functionality and Performance
controls.body: Potential benefits of intended AI system functionality and performance are examined and documented.

controls.name: MAP 3.3 - Specifying and Documenting AI System Application Scope
controls.title: Specifying and Documenting AI System Application Scope
controls.body: Targeted application scope is specified and documented based on the system’s capability, established context, and AI system categorization.

controls.name: MAP 3.5 - Defined, Assessed, and Documented Processes for Human Oversight from GOVERN Function
controls.title: Defined, Assessed, and Documented Processes for Human Oversight from GOVERN Function
controls.body: Processes for human oversight are defined, assessed, and documented in accordance with organizational policies from the GOVERN function.

controls.name: MEASURE 2.2 - Requirements Met for Human Subject Evaluations
controls.title: Requirements Met for Human Subject Evaluations
controls.body: Evaluations involving human subjects meet applicable requirements (including human subject protection) and are representative of the relevant population.

controls.name: MEASURE 2.3 - Measuring AI System Performance and Assurance Criteria for Deployment
controls.title: Measuring AI System Performance and Assurance Criteria for Deployment
controls.body: AI system performance or assurance criteria are measured qualitatively or quantitatively and demonstrated for conditions similar to deployment setting(s). Measures are documented.

controls.name: MEASURE 2.4 - Monitoring AI System Functionality and Behavior in Production
controls.title: Monitoring AI System Functionality and Behavior in Production
controls.body: The functionality and behavior of the AI system and its components – as identified in the MAP function – are monitored when in production.

controls.name: MEASURE 2.12 - Assessing the Environmental Impact of AI Training and Management Activities
controls.title: Assessing the Environmental Impact of AI Training and Management Activities
controls.body: Environmental impact and sustainability of AI model training and management activities – as identified in the MAP function – are assessed and documented.

controls.name: MEASURE 2.6 - Regular Safety Evaluation of AI System with Robust Metrics
controls.title: Regular Safety Evaluation of AI System with Robust Metrics
controls.body: The AI system is evaluated regularly for safety risks – as identified in the MAP function. The AI system to be deployed is demonstrated to be safe, its residual negative risk does not exceed the risk tolerance, and it can fail safely, particularly if made to operate beyond its knowledge limits. Safety metrics reflect system reliability and robustness, real-time monitoring, and response times for AI system failures.

controls.name: MEASURE 3.2 - Risk Tracking for AI Risks: Approaches for Difficult assessments and Missing Metrics
controls.title: Risk Tracking for AI Risks: Approaches for Difficult assessments and Missing Metrics
controls.body: Risk tracking approaches are considered for settings where AI risks are difficult to assess using currently available measurement techniques or where metrics are not yet available.

controls.name: MEASURE 2.7 - Evaluation and Documentation of AI System Security and Resilience in the MAP Function
controls.title: Evaluation and Documentation of AI System Security and Resilience in the MAP Function
controls.body: AI system security and resilience – as identified in the MAP function – are evaluated and documented.

controls.name: MEASURE 2.10 - Examining Privacy Risks in AI System's MAP Function
controls.title: Examining Privacy Risks in AI System's MAP Function
controls.body: Privacy risk of the AI system – as identified in the MAP function – is examined and documented.

controls.name: MEASURE 2.11 - Evaluating Fairness and Bias in the MAP Function
controls.title: Evaluating Fairness and Bias in the MAP Function
controls.body: Fairness and bias – as identified in the MAP function – are evaluated and results are documented.

controls.name: MEASURE 2.13 - Evaluation of TEVV Metrics and Processes in MEASURE Function
controls.title: Evaluation of TEVV Metrics and Processes in MEASURE Function
controls.body: Effectiveness of the employed TEVV metrics and processes in the MEASURE function are evaluated and documented.

controls.name: MEASURE 4.1 - Measurement Approaches for AI Risk Identification: Contextual and Expert-Informed with Documentation
controls.title: Measurement Approaches for AI Risk Identification: Contextual and Expert-Informed with Documentation
controls.body: Measurement approaches for identifying AI risks are connected to deployment context(s) and informed through consultation with domain experts and other end users. Approaches are documented.

controls.name: MEASURE 4.2 - Measuring AI System Trustworthiness with Input from Experts and Actors
controls.title: Measuring AI System Trustworthiness with Input from Experts and Actors
controls.body: Measurement results regarding AI system trustworthiness in deployment context(s) and across the AI lifecycle are informed by input from domain experts and relevant AI actors to validate whether the system is performing consistently as intended. Results are documented.

controls.name: MANAGE 1 - Managing AI Risks with MAP and MEASURE Functions
controls.title: Managing AI Risks with MAP and MEASURE Functions
controls.body: AI risks based on assessments and other analytical output from the MAP and MEASURE functions are prioritized, responded to, and managed.

controls.name: MANAGE 1.1 - Assessing AI System's Purpose and Development for Deployment
controls.title: Assessing AI System's Purpose and Development for Deployment
controls.body: A determination is made as to whether the AI system achieves its intended purposes and stated objectives and whether its development or deployment should proceed.

controls.name: MANAGE 1.2 - Prioritizing Treatment of AI Risks
controls.title: Prioritizing Treatment of AI Risks
controls.body: Treatment of documented AI risks is prioritized based on impact, likelihood, and available resources or methods.

controls.name: MANAGE 1.4 - Documenting Negative Residual Risks in AI Systems for Downstream Acquirers and End Users
controls.title: Documenting Negative Residual Risks in AI Systems for Downstream Acquirers and End Users
controls.body: Negative residual risks (defined as the sum of all unmitigated risks) to both downstream acquirers of AI systems and end users are documented.

controls.name: GOVERN 1.1 - Managing Legal and Regulatory Requirements for AI
controls.title: Managing Legal and Regulatory Requirements for AI
controls.body: Legal and regulatory requirements involving AI are understood, managed, and documented.

controls.name: GOVERN 1.3 - Risk Management Processes, Procedures, and Practices
controls.title: Risk Management Processes, Procedures, and Practices
controls.body: Processes, procedures, and practices are in place to determine the needed level of risk management activities based on the organization’s risk tolerance.

controls.name: GOVERN 1.4 - Establishing Risk Management through Transparent Policies and Controls
controls.title: Establishing Risk Management through Transparent Policies and Controls
controls.body: The risk management process and its outcomes are established through transparent policies, procedures, and other controls based on organizational risk priorities.

controls.name: GOVERN 2.2 - AI Risk Management Training for Personnel and Partners
controls.title: AI Risk Management Training for Personnel and Partners
controls.body: The organization’s personnel and partners receive AI risk management training to enable them to perform their duties and responsibilities consistent with related policies, procedures, and agreements.

controls.name: GOVERN 3.1 - Managing AI Risks: Importance of Diverse Teams
controls.title: Managing AI Risks: Importance of Diverse Teams
controls.body: Decision-making related to mapping, measuring, and managing AI risks throughout the lifecycle is informed by a diverse team (e.g., diversity of demographics, disciplines, experience, expertise, and backgrounds).

controls.name: GOVERN 4.1 - Organizational Policies for Safe AI Systems Development
controls.title: Organizational Policies for Safe AI Systems Development
controls.body: Organizational policies and practices are in place to foster a critical thinking and safety-first mindset in the design, development, deployment, and uses of AI systems to minimize potential negative impacts.

controls.name: GOVERN 4.2 - Documenting and Communicating AI Risks in Organizational Teams
controls.title: Documenting and Communicating AI Risks in Organizational Teams
controls.body: Organizational teams document the risks and potential impacts of the AI technology they design, develop, deploy, evaluate, and use, and they communicate about the impacts more broadly.

controls.name: GOVERN 4.3 - Organizational Practices for AI Testing and Incident Identification
controls.title: Organizational Practices for AI Testing and Incident Identification
controls.body: Organizational practices are in place to enable AI testing, identification of incidents, and information sharing.

controls.name: GOVERN 5.2 - Incorporating Adjudicated Feedback into AI System Design and Implementation
controls.title: Incorporating Adjudicated Feedback into AI System Design and Implementation
controls.body: Mechanisms are established to enable the team that developed or deployed AI systems to regularly incorporate adjudicated feedback from relevant AI actors into system design and implementation.

controls.name: MAP 1.5 - Determining and Documenting Organizational Risk Tolerances
controls.title: Determining and Documenting Organizational Risk Tolerances
controls.body: Organizational risk tolerances are determined and documented.

controls.name: MAP 2.2 - Documenting AI System Knowledge Limits and Oversight for Human Decision-Making
controls.title: Documenting AI System Knowledge Limits and Oversight for Human Decision-Making
controls.body: Information about the AI system’s knowledge limits and how system output may be utilized and overseen by humans is documented. Documentation provides sufficient information to assist relevant AI actors when making decisions and taking subsequent actions.

controls.name: MAP 3.4 - Proficiency Processes and Standards for AI System Performance and Trustworthiness
controls.title: Proficiency Processes and Standards for AI System Performance and Trustworthiness
controls.body: Processes for operator and practitioner proficiency with AI system performance and trustworthiness – and relevant technical standards and certifications – are defined, assessed, and documented.

controls.name: MAP 5.2 - Practices for AI Engagement and Impact Feedback Documented
controls.title: Practices for AI Engagement and Impact Feedback Documented
controls.body: Practices and personnel for supporting regular engagement with relevant AI actors and integrating feedback about positive, negative, and unanticipated impacts are in place and documented.

controls.name: MEASURE 1.1 - Selected Approaches and Metrics for Measuring AI Risks
controls.title: Selected Approaches and Metrics for Measuring AI Risks
controls.body: Approaches and metrics for measurement of AI risks enumerated during the MAP function are selected for implementation starting with the most significant AI risks. The risks or trustworthiness characteristics that will not – or cannot – be measured are properly documented.

controls.name: MEASURE 4.3 - Identifying Measurable Performance Changes Based on AI Consultations and Field Data
controls.title: Identifying Measurable Performance Changes Based on AI Consultations and Field Data
controls.body: Measurable performance improvements or declines based on consultations with relevant AI actors, including affected communities, and field data about contextrelevant risks and trustworthiness characteristics are identified and documented.

controls.name: MEASURE 1.3 - Experts Involved in AI System Assessments and Updates
controls.title: Experts Involved in AI System Assessments and Updates
controls.body: Internal experts who did not serve as front-line developers for the system and/or independent assessors are involved in regular assessments and updates. Domain experts, users, AI actors external to the team that developed or deployed the AI system, and affected communities are consulted in support of assessments as necessary per organizational risk tolerance.

controls.name: MEASURE 2.5 - Valid and Reliable AI System with Limited Generalizability
controls.title: Valid and Reliable AI System with Limited Generalizability
controls.body: The AI system to be deployed is demonstrated to be valid and reliable. Limitations of the generalizability beyond the conditions under which the technology was developed are documented.

controls.name: MEASURE 2.8 - Examining Risks of Transparency and Accountability: Insights from MAP Function
controls.title: Examining Risks of Transparency and Accountability: Insights from MAP Function
controls.body: Risks associated with transparency and accountability – as identified in the MAP function – are examined and documented.

controls.name: MEASURE 2.9 - Responsible AI Governance: Explaining, Validating, and Interpreting System Outputs within Context
controls.title: Responsible AI Governance: Explaining, Validating, and Interpreting System Outputs within Context
controls.body: The AI model is explained, validated, and documented, and AI system output is interpreted within its context – as identified in the MAP function – to inform responsible use and governance.

controls.name: MEASURE 3.1 - Regular Identification and Tracking of AI Risks Based on Performance
controls.title: Regular Identification and Tracking of AI Risks Based on Performance
controls.body: Approaches, personnel, and documentation are in place to regularly identify and track existing, unanticipated, and emergent AI risks based on factors such as intended and actual performance in deployed contexts.

controls.name: MANAGE 1.3 - Developing High Priority Responses to AI Risks with MAP Function
controls.title: Developing High Priority Responses to AI Risks with MAP Function
controls.body: Responses to the AI risks deemed high priority, as identified by the MAP function, are developed, planned, and documented. Risk response options can include mitigating, transferring, avoiding, or accepting.

controls.name: MANAGE 2.2 - Sustaining Value of AI Systems with Mechanisms
controls.title: Sustaining Value of AI Systems with Mechanisms
controls.body: Mechanisms are in place and applied to sustain the value of deployed AI systems.

controls.name: MANAGE 2.4 - Mechanisms and Responsibilities for Inconsistent AI Performance
controls.title: Mechanisms and Responsibilities for Inconsistent AI Performance
controls.body: Mechanisms are in place and applied, and responsibilities are assigned and understood, to supersede, disengage, or deactivate AI systems that demonstrate performance or outcomes inconsistent with intended use.

controls.name: TISAX 8.2.1 - Internal and External Non-disclosure Agreements
controls.title: Internal and External Non-disclosure Agreements
controls.body: Non-disclosure agreements highlighting security obligations are signed by contractors and customers, as well as all organization's employees and project members, in accordance with legal provisions for data protection.

controls.name: T.1.2.1 - Encrypted Communication Over Public Networks
controls.title: Encrypted Communication Over Public Networks
controls.body: A) The Applicant shall have rules, policies or mechanisms in place to ensure that remote access to personal data is encrypted when passing through public networks (such as the Internet).

controls.name: T.1.2.2 - Backups Encryption
controls.title: Backups Encryption
controls.body: A) The backup files shall be encrypted.

controls.name: T.1.2.3 - User Log Data Encryption
controls.title: User Log Data Encryption
controls.body: A) The logs of data subject access, including Internet website logs, shall be encrypted.

controls.name: CIP-010.R1-1.2 - Authorization for Changes to Baseline Configuration
controls.title: Authorization for Changes to Baseline Configuration
controls.body: Each responsible entity shall authorize and document changes that deviate from the existing baseline configuration.

controls.name: PCI 9.4.4 - Media Distribution Approval
controls.title: Media Distribution Approval
controls.body: Management approves all media with cardholder data that is moved outside the facility (including when media is distributed to individuals).

controls.name: T.1.3.4 - Fire and Flood Protection
controls.title: Fire and Flood Protection

controls.name: CIP-013.R1-1.1 - Identify and Assess Supply Chain Cyber Security Risks
controls.title: Identify and Assess Supply Chain Cyber Security Risks
controls.body:
Each responsible entity shall develop one or more documented supply chain cyber security risk management plan(s) for high and medium-impact BES cyber systems and their associated electronic Access Control or Monitoring Systems (EACMS) and Physical Access Control Systems (PACS).

The plan(s) shall include one or more process(es) used in planning for the procurement of BES cyber systems and their associated EACMS and PACS to identify and assess cyber security risk(s) to the Bulk Electric System (BES) from vendor products or services resulting from:
(i) procuring and installing vendor equipment and software; and
(ii) transitions from one vendor(s) to another vendor(s).

controls.name: T.2.1.3 - SSL
controls.title: SSL
controls.body: A) Unsecure SSL shall NOT be used.

controls.name: PCI A3.2.3 - Changes to Organizational Structure
controls.title: Changes to Organizational Structure
controls.body:
Changes to organizational structure result in a formal (internal) review of the impact to PCI DSS scope and applicability of controls.

PCI DSS Reference: Requirement 12

controls.name: 5.17 - Authentication Information (27017)
controls.title: Authentication Information (27017)
controls.body: Allocation and management of authentication information shall be controlled by a management process, including advising personnel on the appropriate handling of authentication information.

controls.name: PCI 5.3.2.1 - Anti-malware Scan Frequency based on Risk Analysis
controls.title: Anti-malware Scan Frequency based on Risk Analysis
controls.body: If periodic malware scans are performed to meet Requirement 5.3.2, the frequency of scans is defined in the entity’s targeted risk analysis, which is performed according to all elements specified in Requirement 12.3.1.

controls.name: T.2.2.2 - Cryptographic Policy
controls.title: Cryptographic Policy

controls.name: T.2.2.1 - Protection Tools Management Policy
controls.title: Protection Tools Management Policy
controls.body: A) There shall be a written policy framing the introduction, maintenance and phasing out of protection tools.

controls.name: CIP-013.R1-1.2 - Supply Chain Cyber Security Risk Management Processes
controls.title: Supply Chain Cyber Security Risk Management Processes

controls.name: PCI 9.4.5 - Media Inventory
controls.title: Media Inventory
controls.body: Inventory logs of all electronic media with cardholder data are maintained.

controls.name: PCI 7.3.1 - User Access Restriction
controls.title: User Access Restriction
controls.body: An access control system(s) is in place that restricts access based on a user’s need to know and covers all system components.

controls.name: PCI 12.8.2 - Acknowledged Card Security Agreement by TPSPs
controls.title: Acknowledged Card Security Agreement by TPSPs
controls.body:
Written agreements with TPSPs are maintained as follows:
- Written agreements are maintained with all TPSPs with which account data is shared or that could affect the security of the CDE.
- Written agreements include acknowledgments from TPSPs that they are responsible for the security of account data the TPSPs possess or otherwise store, process, or transmit on behalf of the entity, or to the extent that they could impact the security of the entity’s CDE.

controls.name: 5.1 - Policies for Information Security (27018)
controls.title: Policies for Information Security (27018)
controls.body: Information security policy and topic-specific policies shall be defined, approved by management, published, communicated to and acknowledged by relevant personnel and relevant interested parties, and reviewed at planned intervals and if significant changes occur.

controls.name: PCI A3.2.1 - Quarterly Documentation of Changes to the In-scope Environment
controls.title: Quarterly Documentation of Changes to the In-scope Environment
controls.body:
PCI DSS scope is documented and confirmed for accuracy at least once every three months and upon significant changes to the in-scope environment. At a minimum, the scoping validation includes:
- Identifying all data flows for the various payment stages (for example, authorization, capture, settlement, chargebacks, and refunds) and acceptance channels (for example, card-present, card-not-present, and e-commerce).
- Updating all data-flow diagrams per Requirement 1.2.4.
- Identifying all locations where account data is stored, processed, and transmitted, including but not limited to 1) any locations outside of the currently defined CDE, 2) applications that process CHD, 3) transmissions between systems and networks, and 4) file backups.
- For any account data found outside of the currently defined CDE, either 1) securely delete it, 2) migrate it into the currently defined CDE, or
3) expand the currently defined CDE to include it.
- Identifying all system components in the CDE, connected to the CDE, or that could impact security of the CDE.
- Identifying all segmentation controls in use and the environment(s) from which the CDE is segmented, including justification for environments being out of scope.
- Identifying all connections to third-party entities with access to the CDE.
- Confirming that all identified data flows, account data, system components, segmentation controls, and connections from third parties with access to the CDE are included in scope.

PCI DSS Reference: Scope of PCI DSS Requirements, Requirement 12.

controls.name: 5.14 - Information Transfer (27018)
controls.title: Information Transfer (27018)
controls.body: Information transfer rules, procedures, or agreements shall be in place for all types of transfer facilities within the organization and between the organization and other parties.

controls.name: CIP-007.R1-1.1 - Enabling Logical Ports
controls.title: Enabling Logical Ports
controls.body: Each responsible entity where technically feasible shall enable only logical network-accessible ports that have been determined to be needed by the responsible entity, including port ranges or services where needed to handle dynamic ports. If a device has no provision for disabling or restricting logical ports on the device then those ports that are open are deemed needed.

controls.name: 5.24 - Information Security Incident Management Planning and Preparation (27018)
controls.title: Information Security Incident Management Planning and Preparation (27018)
controls.body: The organization shall plan and prepare for managing information security incidents by defining,  establishing and communicating information security incident management processes, roles and responsibilities.

controls.name: CIP-007.R2-2.3 - Security Patch Management
controls.title: Security Patch Management
controls.body:
Each responsible entity shall take one of the following actions for applicable patches identified in the requirement "CIP-007.R2-2.2 - Periodic Evaluation of Security Patches", within 35 calendar days of the evaluation completion:
* Apply the applicable patches; or
* Create a dated mitigation plan; or
* Revise an existing mitigation plan. 

Mitigation plans shall include the responsible entity’s planned actions to mitigate the vulnerabilities addressed by each security patch and a timeframe to complete these mitigations.

controls.name: PCI 11.4.1 - Penetration Test Methodology
controls.title: Penetration Test Methodology
controls.body:
A penetration testing methodology is defined, documented, and implemented by the entity, and includes:
- Industry-accepted penetration testing approaches.
- Coverage for the entire CDE perimeter and critical systems.
- Testing from both inside and outside the network.
- Testing to validate any segmentation and scope- reduction controls.
- Application-layer penetration testing to identify, at a minimum, the vulnerabilities listed in Requirement 6.2.4.
- Network-layer penetration tests that encompass all components that support network functions as well as operating systems.
- Review and consideration of threats and vulnerabilities experienced in the last 12 months.
- Documented approach to assessing and addressing the risk posed by exploitable vulnerabilities and security weaknesses found during penetration testing.
- Retention of penetration testing results and remediation activities results for at least 12 months.

controls.name: 5.25 - Assessment and Decision on Information Security Events (27018)
controls.title: Assessment and Decision on Information Security Events (27018)
controls.body: The organization shall assess information security events and decide if they are to be categorized as information security incidents.

controls.name: PCI 9.5.1 - Protection of POI Devices
controls.title: Protection of POI Devices
controls.body:
POI devices that capture payment card data via direct physical interaction with the payment card form factor are protected from tampering and unauthorized substitution, including the following:
- Maintaining a list of POI devices.
- Periodically inspecting POI devices to look for tampering or unauthorized substitution.
- Training personnel to be aware of suspicious behavior and to report tampering or unauthorized substitution of devices.

controls.name: 8.15 - Logging (27018)
controls.title: Logging (27018)
controls.body: Logs that record activities, exceptions, faults and other relevant events shall be produced, stored, protected and analyzed.

controls.name: CIP-007.R5-5.4 - Default Passwords
controls.title: Default Passwords
controls.body: Each responsible entity shall change known default passwords, per cyber asset capability.

controls.name: PCI 9.5.1.1 - Updated List of Devices
controls.title: Updated List of Devices
controls.body:
An up-to-date list of POI devices is maintained, including:
- Make and model of the device.
- Location of device.
- Device serial number or other methods of unique identification.

controls.name: CIP-011.R1-1.1 - Identification of BES Cyber System Information
controls.title: Identification of BES Cyber System Information
controls.body: Each responsible entity shall implement one or more information protection program(s) that includes method(s) to identify information that meets the definition of BES cyber system information.

controls.name: CIP-013.R3 - Supply Chain Cyber Security Risk Management Plan Approval
controls.title: Supply Chain Cyber Security Risk Management Plan Approval
controls.body: Each responsible entity shall review and obtain CIP senior manager or delegate approval of its supply chain cyber security risk management plan(s) specified in CIP-013.R1 at least once every 15 calendar months.

controls.name: CIP-014.R1-1.1 - Transmission Station and Substation Risk Assessment
controls.title: Transmission Station and Substation Risk Assessment
controls.body:
Each transmission owner shall perform an initial risk assessment and subsequent risk assessments of its transmission stations and transmission substations (existing and planned to be in service within 24 months) that meet the criteria specified in Applicability Section 4.1.1. The initial and subsequent risk assessments shall consist of a transmission analysis or transmission analyses designed to identify the transmission station(s) and transmission substation(s) that if rendered inoperable or damaged could result in instability, uncontrolled separation, or cascading within an interconnection.

Subsequent risk assessments shall be performed:
* At least once every 30 calendar months for a transmission owner that has identified in its previous risk assessment (as verified according to CIP-014.R2) one or more transmission stations or transmission substations that if rendered inoperable or damaged could result in instability, uncontrolled separation, or cascading within an interconnection; or
* At least once every 60 calendar months for a transmission owner that has not identified in its previous risk assessment (as verified according to CIP-014.R2) any transmission stations or transmission substations that if rendered inoperable or damaged could result in instability, uncontrolled separation, or cascading within an interconnection.

controls.name: TISAX 1.5.1 - Compliance with Security Requirements and Policies
controls.title: Compliance with Security Requirements and Policies
controls.body: Information security policies and procedures are developed and published to all employees. These policies and procedures are reviewed by appropriate management team members to ensure it is relevant and current with respect to their areas of responsibility.

controls.name: 5.35 - Independent Review of Information Security (27017)
controls.title: Independent Review of Information Security (27017)
controls.body: The organization’s approach to managing information security and its implementation including people,  processes and technologies shall be reviewed independently at planned intervals, or when significant changes occur.

controls.name: TISAX 1.5.2 - Independent Review of ISMS
controls.title: Independent Review of ISMS
controls.body: The organization’s approach to managing information security and its implementation (i.e., control objectives, controls, policies, processes and procedures for information security) is reviewed independently at regular intervals or when significant changes occur.

controls.name: TISAX 4.2.1.1 - Access Right Approval
controls.title: Access Right Approval
controls.body: Access rights are approved by the organization's designated personnel. Information stored is encrypted or technically protected against unauthorized access.

controls.name: TISAX 8.2.7 - Device Usage in Security Areas
controls.title: Device Usage in Security Areas
controls.body: The organization has defined a process for carrying along and using mobile video and photography devices into security areas where vehicles, components or parts classified as requiring protection are manufactured, processed or stored.

controls.name: CIP-004-7.R4-4.1 - Need-Based User Authorization
controls.title: Need-Based User Authorization

controls.name: CIP-014.R1-1.2 - Primary Control Center Identification
controls.title: Primary Control Center Identification
controls.body: The transmission owner shall identify the primary control center that operationally controls each transmission station or transmission substation identified in the CIP-014.R1 risk assessment.

controls.name: CIP-004-7.R6-6.1 - Provisioning Electronic and Physical Access to BCSI
controls.title: Provisioning Electronic and Physical Access to BCSI
controls.body:
Each responsible entity shall, prior to provisioning, authorize (unless already authorized according to CIP-004-7.R4-4.1) based on need, as determined by the responsible entity, except for CIP exceptional circumstances:
6.1.1. provisioned electronic access to electronic BCSI; and
6.1.2. provisioned physical access to physical BCSI.

controls.name: PCI A3.2.6.1 - Response Procedures Initiated upon Detection to Remove Clear-text PAN
controls.title: Response Procedures Initiated upon Detection to Remove Clear-text PAN
controls.body:
Response procedures are implemented to be initiated upon the detection of attempts to remove cleartext PAN from the CDE via an unauthorized channel, method, or process.
Response procedures include:
- Procedures for the prompt investigation of alerts by responsible personnel.
- Procedures for remediating data leaks or process gaps, as necessary, to prevent any data loss.

PCI DSS Reference: Requirement 12

controls.name: 8.3 - Information Access Restriction (27017)
controls.title: Information Access Restriction (27017)
controls.body: Access to information and other associated assets shall be restricted in accordance with the established topic-specific policy on access control.

controls.name: PCI A3.3.1 - Detection and Alerting of Security Control Failures
controls.title: Detection and Alerting of Security Control Failures
controls.body:
Failures of critical security control systems are detected, alerted, and addressed promptly, including but not limited to failure of:
- Network security controls
- IDS/IPS
- FIM
- Anti-malware solutions
- Physical access controls
- Logical access controls
- Audit logging mechanisms
- Segmentation controls (if used)
- Automated audit log review mechanisms. This bullet is a best practice until its effective date.
- Automated code review tools (if used). This bullet is a best practice until its effective date.

PCI DSS Reference: Requirements 1-12

controls.name: CIP-004-7.R6-6.3 - Removal of Electronic and Physical Access to BCSI
controls.title: Removal of Electronic and Physical Access to BCSI
controls.body: Each responsible entity shall, in case of termination, remove the individual’s ability to use provisioned access to BCSI (unless already revoked according to CIP-004.R5-5.1) by the end of the next calendar day following the effective date of the termination action.

controls.name: TISAX 1.2.1 - Information Security Management System
controls.title: Information Security Management System
controls.body: The organization establishes, implements, maintains and continually improves an information security management system (ISMS).

controls.name: PCI A3.3.3 - Independent Review for Business-as-usual Activities
controls.title: Independent Review for Business-as-usual Activities
controls.body:
Reviews are performed at least once every three months to verify BAU activities are being followed. Reviews are performed by personnel assigned to the PCI DSS compliance program (as identified in A3.1.3), and include:
- Confirmation that all BAU activities, including A3.2.2, A3.2.6, and A3.3.1, are being performed.
- Confirmation that personnel are following security policies and operational procedures (for example, daily log reviews, ruleset reviews for network security controls, configuration standards for new systems).
- Documenting how the reviews were completed, including how all BAU activities were verified as being in place.
- Collection of documented evidence as required for the annual PCI DSS assessment.
- Review and sign-off of results by personnel assigned responsibility for the PCI DSS compliance program, as identified in A3.1.3.
- Retention of records and documentation for at least 12 months, covering all BAU activities.

PCI DSS Reference: Requirements 1-12

controls.name: PCI 7.1.1 - Access Control Policies and Procedures
controls.title: Access Control Policies and Procedures
controls.body:
All security policies and operational procedures that are identified in Requirement 7 are:
- Documented.
- Kept up to date.
- In use.
- Known to all affected parties.

controls.name: TISAX 7.1.1 - Compliance with Regulatory and Contractual Provisions
controls.title: Compliance with Regulatory and Contractual Provisions
controls.body: Organizational policies regarding compliance with legal, regulatory and contractual provisions have been developed, implemented, and communicated to relevant stakeholders. Annual reviews and updates (if applicable) of legal, regulatory and contractual provisions are performed to ensure they are relevant to information security.

controls.name: 5.16 - Identity Management (27018)
controls.title: Identity Management (27018)
controls.body: The full life cycle of identities shall be managed.

controls.name: VCDPA 2.1 - Consumers Rights Procedure
controls.title: Consumers Rights Procedure
controls.body: The organization has established a consumer rights procedure that specifies the process and time frames for handling consumers' requests with respect to their personal information. The procedure is communicated to all the employees and reviewed by management on at least an annual basis.

controls.name: TISAX 8.3.2 - Parking and Storage of Vehicles, Components and Parts
controls.title: Parking and Storage of Vehicles, Components and Parts
controls.body: The organization has a process in place for protecting vehicles, components and parts against unauthorized viewing, unauthorized photography and access during parking/storage.

controls.name: PCI A1.1.2 - Access Restriction to Cardholder Environment
controls.title: Access Restriction to Cardholder Environment
controls.body: Controls are implemented such that each customer only has permission to access its own cardholder data and CDE.

controls.name: PCI 9.1.1 - Policies and Procedures for Physical Access Restriction
controls.title: Policies and Procedures for Physical Access Restriction
controls.body:
All security policies and operational procedures that are identified in Requirement 9 are:
- Documented.
- Kept up to date.
- In use.
- Known to all affected parties.

controls.name: 5.18 - Access Rights (27018)
controls.title: Access Rights (27018)
controls.body: Access rights to information and other associated assets shall be provisioned, reviewed, modified and removed in accordance with the organization’s topic-specific policy on and rules for access control.

controls.name: 6.3 - Information Security Awareness, Education and Training (27018)
controls.title: Information Security Awareness, Education and Training (27018)
controls.body: Personnel of the organization and relevant interested parties shall receive appropriate information security awareness, education and training, and regular updates of the organization's information security policy, topic-specific policies and procedures, as relevant to their job function.

controls.name: CIP-014.R2-2.4 - Procedures for Sensitive/Confidential Information Protection from Third Party Verifier
controls.title: Procedures for Sensitive/Confidential Information Protection from Third Party Verifier
controls.body: Each transmission owner shall implement procedures, such as the use of nondisclosure agreements, for protecting sensitive or confidential information made available to the unaffiliated third-party verifier of the risk assessment and to protect or exempt sensitive or confidential information developed pursuant to this Reliability Standard from public disclosure.

controls.name: CIP-004.R1-1.1 - Cyber Security Awareness
controls.title: Cyber Security Awareness
controls.body: Each responsible entity shall implement security awareness that, at least once each calendar quarter, reinforces cyber security practices (which may include associated physical security practices) for the responsible entity’s personnel who have authorized electronic or authorized unescorted physical access to BES cyber systems.

controls.name: PCI 12.10.1 - Incident Response Plan
controls.title: Incident Response Plan
controls.body:
An incident response plan exists and is ready to be activated in the event of a suspected or confirmed security incident. The plan includes, but is not limited to:
- Roles, responsibilities, and communication and contact strategies in the event of a suspected or confirmed security incident, including notification of payment brands and acquirers, at a minimum.
- Incident response procedures with specific containment and mitigation activities for different types of incidents.
- Business recovery and continuity procedures.
- Data backup processes.
- Analysis of legal requirements for reporting compromises.
- Coverage and responses of all critical system components.
- Reference or inclusion of incident response procedures from the payment brands.

controls.name: TISAX 7.1.2 - Protection of Personally Identifiable Data
controls.title: Protection of Personally Identifiable Data
controls.body: A privacy policy or notice has been implemented and communicated to all relevant stakeholders regarding the protection of personally identifiable information in accordance with relevant legislation and regulations.

controls.name: TISAX 8.4.1 - Camouflage Regulations for Trial Vehicles
controls.title: Camouflage Regulations for Trial Vehicles
controls.body: Camouflage regulations are defined, known to and followed by each project member to guarantee adequate view protection of trial vehicles.

controls.name: CIP-014.R3-3.1 - Notification to Transmission Operator of Primary Control Center
controls.title: Notification to Transmission Operator of Primary Control Center
controls.body:
For a primary control center(s) identified by the transmission owner according to CIP-014.R1-1.2 that a) operationally controls an identified transmission station or transmission substation verified according to CIP-014.R2, and b) is not under the operational control of the transmission owner: the transmission owner shall, within seven calendar days following completion of CIP-014.R2, notify the transmission operator that has operational control of the primary control center of such identification and the date of completion of CIP-014.R2.

If a transmission station or transmission substation previously identified under CIP-014.R1 and verified according to CIP-014.R2 is removed from the identification during a subsequent risk assessment performed according to CIP-014.R1 or a verification according to CIP-014.R2, then the transmission owner shall, within seven calendar days following the verification or the subsequent risk assessment, notify the transmission operator that has operational control of the primary control center of the removal.

controls.name: 8.2 - Privileged Access Rights (27018)
controls.title: Privileged Access Rights (27018)
controls.body: The allocation and use of privileged access rights shall be restricted and managed.

controls.name: TISAX 8.1.7 - Visitor Management
controls.title: Visitor Management
controls.body: Visitor logs are used to track visitor activity at the facility and non-disclosure agreements signed prior to entering the facility in accordance with legal provisions for data protection.

controls.name: C.5.1.7 - Modification of "By Default" Passwords
controls.title: Modification of "By Default" Passwords
controls.body: A) The IoT devices shall never use a default password provided by the manufacturer.

controls.name: CIP-014.R4-4.1 - Facility-Specific Threat and Vulnerability Evaluation
controls.title: Facility-Specific Threat and Vulnerability Evaluation
controls.body: Each transmission owner that identified a transmission station, transmission substation, or a primary control center in CIP-014.R1 and verified according to CIP-014.R2, and each transmission operator notified by a transmission owner according to CIP-014.R3, shall conduct an evaluation of the potential threats and vulnerabilities of a physical attack to each of their respective transmission station(s), transmission substation(s), and primary control center(s) identified in CIP-014.R1 and verified according to CIP-014.R2. The evaluation shall consider the unique characteristics of the identified and verified transmission station(s), transmission substation(s), and primary control center(s).

controls.name: TISAX 5.2.6 - Audit of IT Systems
controls.title: Audit of IT Systems
controls.body: Audits are planned and conducted at regular intervals by designated personnel to assess the effectiveness and efficiency of existing controls. The audit results are communicated and reviewed by Management, identified deficiencies are addressed in a timely manner.

controls.name: C.5.1.1 - Impact Assessment Complementary Requirements
controls.title: Impact Assessment Complementary Requirements

controls.name: PCI 7.1.2 - Roles and Responsibilities
controls.title: Roles and Responsibilities
controls.body: Roles and responsibilities for performing activities in Requirement 7 are documented, assigned, and understood.

controls.name: G.3.1.1 - Duty to Inform in Clear Language
controls.title: Duty to Inform in Clear Language

controls.name: TISAX 8.1.8 - On-site Client Segregation
controls.title: On-site Client Segregation
controls.body: The organization has clear client segregation measures on site to ensure unauthorized viewing and access to locations where vehicles, components and classified parts requiring protection are processed and stored.

controls.name: PCI 9.1.2 - Roles and Responsibilities
controls.title: Roles and Responsibilities
controls.body: Roles and responsibilities for performing activities in Requirement 9 are documented, assigned, and understood.

controls.name: VCDPA 2.5 - Notice of Targeted Advertising or Sale of Personal Information
controls.title: Notice of Targeted Advertising or Sale of Personal Information
controls.body: Explicit notice is provided to consumers prior to processing personal data for targeted advertising or the sale of their personal information. Consumers are provided with a mechanism to exercise the right to opt-out of the targeted advertising or sale of their personal information, and any such requests are handled in a timely manner.

controls.name: TISAX 8.1.1 - Physical and Environmental Security for Prototype Protection
controls.title: Physical and Environmental Security for Prototype Protection
controls.body: The organization (operator) has physical and environmental security processes maintained and implemented by the operator and at the premises and facilities of suppliers, development partners and service providers to protect the prototypes.

controls.name: CIP-014.R4-4.2 - Threat and Vulnerability Evaluation - Prior History of Attacks
controls.title: Threat and Vulnerability Evaluation - Prior History of Attacks
controls.body: Each transmission owner that identified a transmission station, transmission substation, or a primary control center in CIP-014.R1 and verified according to CIP-014.R2, and each transmission operator notified by a transmission owner according to CIP-014.R3, shall conduct an evaluation of the potential threats and vulnerabilities of a physical attack to each of their respective transmission station(s), transmission substation(s), and primary control center(s) identified in CIP-014.R1 and verified according to CIP-014.R2. The evaluation shall consider the prior history of attacks on similar facilities taking into account the frequency, geographic proximity, and severity of past physical security-related events.

controls.name: CIP-014.R4-4.3 - Threat and Vulnerability Evaluation - Threat Intelligence
controls.title: Threat and Vulnerability Evaluation - Threat Intelligence
controls.body: Each transmission owner that identified a transmission station, transmission substation, or a primary control center in CIP-014.R1 and verified according to CIP-014.R2, and each transmission operator notified by a transmission owner according to CIP-014.R3, shall conduct an evaluation of the potential threats and vulnerabilities of a physical attack to each of their respective transmission station(s), transmission substation(s), and primary control center(s) identified in CIP-014.R1 and verified according to CIP-014.R2. The evaluation shall consider intelligence or threat warnings received from sources such as law enforcement, the Electric Reliability Organization (ERO), the Electricity Sector Information Sharing and Analysis Center (ES-ISAC), U.S. federal and/or Canadian governmental agencies, or their successors.

controls.name: PCI 3.6.1.2 - Use of Secret and Private Keys
controls.title: Use of Secret and Private Keys
controls.body:
Secret and private keys used to encrypt/decrypt stored account data are stored in one (or more) of the following forms at all times:
- Encrypted with a key-encrypting key that is at least as strong as the data-encrypting key, and that is stored separately from the data-encrypting key.
- Within a secure cryptographic device (SCD), such as a hardware security module (HSM) or PTS-approved point-of-interaction device.
- As at least two full-length key components or key shares, in accordance with an industry-accepted method.

controls.name: PCI 3.6.1.3 - Access to Cleartext Cryptographic Key
controls.title: Access to Cleartext Cryptographic Key
controls.body: Access to cleartext cryptographic key components is restricted to the fewest number of custodians necessary.

controls.name: C.14.1.4 - Special Processing of Geolocation Data in Case of Theft
controls.title: Special Processing of Geolocation Data in Case of Theft
controls.body:
IF a mechanism is in place to enable the location of a vehicle in case of theft THEN:
A) The activation and deactivation of remote geolocation of the vehicle in case theft shall be controlled by the owner of the vehicle (or by a qualified national authority).

controls.name: PCI 3.7.1 - Generation of Strong Cryptographic Keys
controls.title: Generation of Strong Cryptographic Keys
controls.body: Key-management policies and procedures are implemented to include the generation of strong cryptographic keys used to protect stored account data.

controls.name: PCI 3.7.2 - Secure Distribution of Cryptographic Keys
controls.title: Secure Distribution of Cryptographic Keys
controls.body: Key-management policies and procedures are implemented to include the secure distribution of cryptographic keys used to protect stored account data.

controls.name: VCDPA 2.6 - Right to Opt-out of Targeted Advertising, Profiling, or Sale of Personal Information
controls.title: Right to Opt-out of Targeted Advertising, Profiling, or Sale of Personal Information
controls.body: Requests from consumers to opt-out of targeted advertising, profiling, or sale of their personal information are documented, retained, and acted upon within 45 days from the receipt of the request. Any delay or denial on request is communicated to consumers and handled in accordance with applicable privacy regulations.

controls.name: PCI 3.7.3 - Storage of Cryptographic Keys
controls.title: Storage of Cryptographic Keys
controls.body: Key-management policies and procedures are implemented to include secure storage of cryptographic keys used to protect stored account data.

controls.name: CIP-002.R1 - BES Cyber System Categorization
controls.title: BES Cyber System Categorization

controls.name: CE.020 - Account Management
controls.title: Account Management
controls.body: Develop and implement a formal process for the approval and creation of user accounts. For privileged (admin) users, additional scrutiny is implemented before access is granted.

controls.name: PCI 4.1.1 - Security Policies and Procedures
controls.title: Security Policies and Procedures
controls.body:
All security policies and operational procedures that are identified in Requirement 4 are:
- Documented.
- Kept up to date.
- In use.
- Known to all affected parties.

controls.name: CIP-014.R5-5.1 - Physical Security Plan - Resiliency and Security Measures
controls.title: Physical Security Plan - Resiliency and Security Measures
controls.body:
Each transmission owner that identified a transmission station, transmission substation, or primary control center in CIP-014.R1 and verified according to CIP-014.R2, and each transmission operator notified by a transmission owner according to CIP-014.R3, shall develop and implement a documented physical security plan(s) that covers their respective transmission station(s), transmission substation(s), and primary control center(s). The physical security plan(s) shall be developed within 120 calendar days following the completion of CIP-014.R2 and executed according to the timeline specified in the physical security plan(s).

The physical security plan(s) shall include resiliency or security measures designed collectively to deter, detect, delay, assess, communicate, and respond to potential physical threats and vulnerabilities identified during the evaluation conducted in CIP-014.R4.

controls.name: CIP-002.R2 - BES Cyber System Categorization Review
controls.title: BES Cyber System Categorization Review
controls.body:
Each responsible entity shall:
2.1. Review the identifications in requirement R1 (CIP-002.R1) and its parts (and update them if there are changes identified) at least once every 15 calendar months, even if it has no identified items in requirement R1 (CIP-002.R1), and 
2.2. Have its CIP senior manager or delegate approve the identifications required by requirement R1 (CIP-002.R1) at least once every 15 calendar months, even if it has no identified items in requirement R1 (CIP-002.R1).

controls.name: VCDPA 2.7 - Right to Non-Discrimination
controls.title: Right to Non-Discrimination
controls.body: The organization has established processes to prohibit discrimination against consumers who exercised their rights under the VCDPA.

controls.name: C.5.1.2 - IoT Network Vulnerability Risk Assessment
controls.title: IoT Network Vulnerability Risk Assessment
controls.body: A) The Applicant shall have evaluated the risks associated to the IoT network in terms of security, including the risk that hackers use the IoT network as a weaker entry point for accessing servers where personal data are stored.

controls.name: PCI 3.7.4 - Cryptographic Keys Changes
controls.title: Cryptographic Keys Changes
controls.body:
Key management policies and procedures are implemented for cryptographic key changes for keys that have reached the end of their cryptoperiod, as defined by the associated application vendor or key owner, and based on industry best practices and guidelines, including the following:
- A defined cryptoperiod for each key type in use.
- A process for key changes at the end of the defined cryptoperiod.

controls.name: PCI 3.7.5 - Retirement, Replacement, or Destruction of Keys
controls.title: Retirement, Replacement, or Destruction of Keys
controls.body:
Key management policies and procedures are implemented to include the retirement, replacement, or destruction of keys used to protect stored account data, as deemed necessary when:
- The key has reached the end of its defined cryptoperiod.
- The integrity of the key has been weakened, including when personnel with knowledge of a cleartext key component leaves the company, or the role for which the key component was known.
- The key is suspected of or known to be compromised.
Retired or replaced keys are not used for encryption operations.

controls.name: A.11.8 - Unique Use of User IDs
controls.title: Unique Use of User IDs
controls.body: If more than one individual has access to stored PII, then they should each have a distinct user ID for identification, authentication and authorization purposes.

controls.name: TISAX 5.3.4 - Segregation of Information in Shared External Services
controls.title: Segregation of Information in Shared External Services
controls.body: System components are configured to properly segregate access for the organization and its customers from other tenant users.

controls.name: PCI 3.7.7 - Prevention of Unauthorized Substitution of Cryptographic Keys
controls.title: Prevention of Unauthorized Substitution of Cryptographic Keys
controls.body: Key management policies and procedures are implemented to include the prevention of unauthorized substitution of cryptographic keys.

controls.name: CIP-014.R5-5.2 - Physical Security Plan - Law Enforcement Contact and Coordination
controls.title: Physical Security Plan - Law Enforcement Contact and Coordination
controls.body:
